covenants.name: Epidauros
covenants.notes:
The Blood of Medusa. Athene gave Asklepios the blood of the gorgon's right vein, which heals, as that of her left vein kills. Drunk in quantity (a whole year's 16 pawns, so almost never allowed) it drops Incapacitating Wounds at once to Heavy, makes every later Recovery roll for current wounds succeed, and cures any disease or ailment; legend says it can even raise the dead, though magi say that has not been done for over a century. A dose of 4 pawns used in making a Longevity Ritual gives +12 to the Lab Total, and drunk it works a Chirurgeon's Healing Touch on the drinker.

Patron: Asklepios, chief Greek god of medicine, a Magic spirit bound to the sanctuary, who is willing to be its patron because the magi honour the place and keep it to its purpose. He has no body and does not speak, but is felt most at the end of the Hall of Repose, by his statue. Sleepers in the Hall, the sick above all, often have visions of him guiding them to a cure; they gain +12 to their next Wound Recovery roll, and +6 to the Lab Total of a Longevity Ritual made for them there.

Healing in the Theban way: the healer pays the vis and earns a token, the healed returns half; magi needing magical healing most often come here. Any magus may make a Longevity Ritual for the Tribunal for a token or two, and these are traditionally made at Epidauros.

The book gives no founding year (only before the Order's founding) and no season. Two magi are unnamed.

params.detail: a season of healing and a Longevity Ritual from each magus a year

covenants.summary:
A small, venerable covenant of the Ionian phyle, in the ancient healing sanctuary of Asklepios, renowned for its service to the Tribunal: it heals the sick and keeps magi young, and many of the Tribunal's magi live under a Longevity Ritual made by one of its specialists. Most of the Tribunal-funded Longevity Rituals are made here, the recipient sleeping in the Hall of Repose, and magi of other Tribunals come seeking its help too.

The asklepieion goes back to the fourth century BC, built on the god's supposed birthplace by a cult of pharmakeutria, physician magi, who tended the throngs of pilgrims; the Goths sacked it at the end of the fourth century AD and it lay empty until wizards of the Theban League revived it before the Order was founded. Magi have been there ever since, apart from a spell of Tremere usurpers in the ninth century who were driven out at the Sundering; since then its record has been long, honourable and quiet.

It has only three or four magi, all experts in Corpus, healing or longevity, led by its eldest, Xenias the Leper. Each spends a season a year as a physician at the sanctuary and usually another making a Longevity Ritual, so it draws only selfless magi not wrapped up in their own studies. Local people know to come when they are sick, and are usually treated, and the place keeps a little of its ancient fame among mortals.

Its servants and few soldiers were all healed or saved by the magi and have sworn their lives to its service: lepers, outcasts and reformed criminals, many of whom came as a last hope and have nowhere else to go, most with some disability from punishment or injury (tongues cut out, limbs lost, blinded or castrated).
covenants.what_matters:
Laboratory: the Hall of Repose, shared, specialised in healing and longevity; Tribunal-funded Longevity Rituals are made there
Boon: Powerful Ally (Asklepios, the covenant's patron)
Boon: Aura (Magic 5); Prestige (healers of the Tribunal); Loyal Covenfolk
Hook: Hermetic Services (a season of healing and a Longevity Ritual from each magus a year)
Hook: Distorted Covenfolk (maimed, leprous and outcast servants)
Tension: prejudice against lepers keeps many magi from Xenias, and magic cannot cure leprosy
Tension: healing the Prince of Achaea or his kin would be meddling with mundanes, and refusing would make enemies
covenants.secrets:
Healing the Realm: Geoffrey II of Achaea, in whose land the covenant lies, falls gravely ill, and his wife Agnes begs the magi for a cure. Refuse, and if he dies they make an enemy of her and leave a war of succession; heal him, and a rival accuses him of dealing with pagan sorcerers. Either way the covenant could be charged with interfering with mundanes.
Magi of Epidauros wonder whether the nectar and ambrosia Tantalus is said to have stolen could improve Longevity Rituals.

Vis: the Blood of Medusa, 16 pawns of extraordinary Corpus vis a year, kept in a basin atop a carved stele by the statue of Asklepios in the Hall of Repose

Vis: Imaginem from the ancient theatre

Vis: a small stipend from the Tribunal for healing magi

Library: an unrivalled collection on Medicine and outstanding books on Creo and Corpus

covenants.name: Erebos
covenants.notes:
Patron: Cyra, the founder, who passed into Final Twilight only a couple of decades after founding it but did not wholly vanish. She comes back now and then as a cryptic guide and guardian of her followers, who have taken her as their patron spirit, most often as her old familiar, a great white owl with bright red eyes much like the koukouvaouna, a guardian spirit of northern Greece; otherwise as a gaunt woman with glowing red eyes, in a black shawl, gripping an obsidian staff enchanted for destruction.

The book gives no founding year (the later ninth century) and no season. Nine magi are unnamed.

secretive, reluctant to serve, led by witches

covenants.summary:
An old but little-known covenant of the Ionian phyle, all of House Ex Miscellanea, sworn to preserve the Tribunal's native traditions of magic; its magi share a valley in the Cambunian Mountains but keep apart from each other and from the wider Tribunal, and it is among the most secretive covenants of all.

In the later ninth century, soon after the Sundering, Ex Miscellanea came to the Tribunal, among them a filius of Pralix sent to deal with the troublesome Witches of Thessaly. A few of the witches, led by the maga Cyra, were won over and joined the Order; Cyra would not move, so she founded a covenant in her tradition's homeland to shelter all the native Greek traditions Tremere had threatened, and named it Erebos, another name for Hades meaning blackness or shadow. Since then new magi from Greek traditions have drifted there expecting a welcome; most found it cool, and stayed anyway.

Counted by heads it is among the biggest covenants in the Tribunal, close to a dozen magi: Witches of Thessaly, members of the Cult of Orpheus, Pharmacopoieans, and one or more Slavic magi who say they were hounded out of the Transylvanian Tribunal. Traditions with several members meet among themselves, but there is no council and no council chamber. The leader is always a Witch of Thessaly of Cyra's line, who handles practical matters, sharing out books and vis, and is often called on to settle the petty quarrels that flare between traditions; the current one is young Destasia, with her mater Megethia still there but lost in ever longer Twilights.

Erebos has no covenfolk as such: most magi keep their own servants, guards and retainers, and some none. The autocrat, who holds the covenant's slender purse and stores, answers to Destasia alone, which gives her real power.

The Tribunal thinks poorly of it, for its secrecy, the unwillingness of some members to volunteer services, and the sinister air of the witches who lead it. House Tremere calls it little better than a devil-worshippers' nest, and Erebos and Gigas, to its north, loathe each other.

Boon: Local Ally (Cyra, the covenant's patron)
Boon: Hedge Tradition (the native traditions it shelters)
Hook: Fractured Council (no council; magi of rival traditions quarrel)
Hook: Infamous (secretive, reluctant to serve, led by witches)
Hook: Rival (the Daughters of Erictho in the mountains; the Tremere of Gigas)

Cyra is most likely a Magic spirit, but given the dark magic of the Witches of Thessaly she might be Infernal.
Proximios, through the League of the Vigilant, means to set demon-hunters on the young magi of Erebos as supposed diabolists.

Vis: Perdo from the bats of Hecate's cave near the valley

Library: no books named; the leader shares out the books and vis

covenants.name: Gigas
covenants.notes:
Patron in name only: Gigas has never accepted that a covenant needs a patron spirit, which smacks of idolatry to it, and in protest names its leader's familiar as its official patron. Čovek is a silver wolf of a line that has given familiars to many great Tremere, every leader of Gigas among them; to be chosen by one is an honour. It counts as no Boon.

The book gives no season. Three magi are unnamed. A Tremere who comes to Gigas from another Tribunal, as a guest or a temporary member, is a metoikos until the Assembly grants a decree of citizenship; the book names none of them, so the register lists only Boustaphan, Monorchis and Allectores, all politai.

covenants.summary:
House Tremere's chief holding in the Tribunal, of the Propontian phyle, set up to remind Thebes of Tremere's strength just to the north. It is often at odds with the rest of the Tribunal, yet its distance from the other covenants makes it a neutral ground for peace treaties and pacts of goodwill and non-aggression. It is no covenant's vassal, but it answers to Coeris, the Tremere domus magna in Transylvania, across the Tribunal border, and reports there all the news the usual channels miss.

It was founded in 1023 as a place where magi and favoured companions wounded in the Schism War could recover. The Tribunal distrusted it from the start, and more so after 1069, when it admitted only Tremere. Its six members are mostly Boustaphan's Hermetic descendants; it has room for nine, hosts Tremere from abroad, and gives support and even temporary membership to any Tremere moving to the Tribunal.

Several members loudly condemn Theban customs as the Order's magic debased by 'vulgar paganism' and want the Tribunal brought back into line with the rest of the Order: they champion Latin over Greek, seek precedents to add to the Peripheral Code, and review as many laws as they can when drawn to the Legislative Board. They claim a small win in the permanent logothete of 1186, which they did not propose but campaigned for. Its leader is said to have remarked that even the Roman Republic fell to a tyrant, which, if true, hints at what the House would do should the slow road fail. With Oikos tou Eleous it makes up the League Against Idolatry.
covenants.what_matters:
Boon: Hidden Resources (underground sancta under a modest lodge)
Hook: Superiors (Coeris, the Tremere domus magna)
Hook: House Covenant (Tremere only since 1069)
Hook: Hermetic Politics (its campaign to normalise the Tribunal)
Tension: feud with Erebos, which it thinks a nest of diabolists
Tension: Hedyosmos, which it suspects of the Sundering; Tremere are not welcome there
Tension: the Tremere appeal to the Grand Tribunal of 1228 to retry the League of Advisors
covenants.secrets:
Proximios hopes to convince Aiakia that Gigas's Tremere brought about the fall of Constantinople and plan to strike at her covenant, and Tisiphon that they have escaped justice; Boustaphan would never open Gigas's records to clear them.

Library: no books named; records Boustaphan will not open to outsiders

covenants.name: Hedyosmos
covenants.notes:
The Cult of the Earth. Guernicus was the last of a cult of the earth's mysteries and refounded it in his last years among some apprentices; it has since taken in magi of other Houses but is always led by a Guernicus. In Greece, as the threskeia geine (the cultus terrae elsewhere), it has taken over the old functions of Hades, the chief Underworld god, without worshipping him. All eight magi of Hedyosmos belong. Its Summoning is a variant that calls any Magic being aligned to Terram (spirits, magical beasts, elementals made de novo by scouring) and is not Infernal. Its ordeals usually leave a Restriction (feet on bare earth), Afflicted Tongue by mutilation, Deficient Auram or No Sense of Direction.

Patron: Minthe, a Magic Daimon, once Hades's lover: when he took Persephone she boasted he would come back to her and drive the girl from his halls, and Demeter trod her into dust, from which grew mint, Hades's sacred herb. She guards one of the entrances to the Underworld, thought a way into the Magic Realm, and for centuries the covenant has venerated her rather than Hades. Being set over a gate into Tartaros, where the titans lie, she is central to its hopes.

Rumours, mostly spread by Tremere: that Tremere's chief lieutenants were imprisoned and questioned here in the Sundering and the knowledge used for the rituals that broke the House, some of their ghosts still captive; that the Tremere dead sent through the Gate of Eurydice at Coeris come out, bodies or spirits, in the labyrinth; and that its wealth comes from turning human bones into gold.

Porphyrion of Tytalus left ten years ago for Rome, where he is said to have found the Jar of Pandora, and then for Normandy. The book gives no founding year (before the Order) and no season. Three magi are unnamed.

params.detail: the gate to Tartaros in the labyrinth

covenants.summary:
A covenant of the Ionian phyle shared by House Guernicus and House Tytalus, an alliance some think sinister, and earning its grim name: by every account it squats over a door to the Underworld, and its magi are masters of stygian magic, of earth, the dead and malice. Yet it has always stood firmly for the Hermetic polity; some doubt its motives, none its loyalty.

It is among the oldest covenants of the Tribunal: wizards lived there for at least a century before the Order. Three founders of the Theban League came from it, the youngest of them taught the Art by Guernicus in person; already given to venerating chthonic spirits, it embraced Guernicus's revived Terrae Cult and became one of its chief seats. Its Guernici and Tytalan theurgists are widely believed to have been central to the Sundering of Tremere in 848, and had both the motive and the skill. It shrugged off the Corruption of Tytalus and the Schism War alike, and mundane wars and Hermetic upheavals since. Tremere magi are not welcome.

No light or speech is allowed in the common areas: magi and companions may light and talk in their own caves as long as nothing leaks into the passages or shared chambers. Even the kitchens are dark, all food cooked outside or bought in the nearby village and kept warm with hot stones in covered baskets, and in places old enchantments make light or sound impossible. Everyone talks in a sign language pressed with the fingers into the listener's palm, and Hedyosmos Lore is needed not to get lost.

Its magi often advise the Judicial and Legislative Boards, and always vote for whatever does least harm. Anyone needing a skilled debater for a decree can usually hire one for the neutralisation of one of the debater's shards, though they refuse causes they think bad for the polity; and its magic is as easy to get. Aiakia, the archon, knows several rituals, Conjuring the Mystic Tower among them, and casts them for others for the ritual's vis and the neutralisation of a shard, hers or a sodalis's.

Covenfolk work mostly in the dark: most are fluent in the sign language, valued servants have enchantments to see, and all the grogs are trained to fight foes they cannot see, so that the polemarch sometimes borrows them for Marches against magi given to invisibility. Several have the Dowsing Virtue, often born of the strongly aligned aura in those born there, and through them the covenant has found seams of gold, silver and gems that make it fabulously rich, all worked through intermediaries to avoid any charge of meddling.
covenants.what_matters:
Income: hidden mines of gold, silver and gemstones found by dowsing covenfolk, worked through intermediaries
Mysteries: Initiation Scripts of the threskeia geine for Divination and Augury (Geomancy), Summoning (of Terram-aligned Magic beings), Dowsing, Puissant Terram, Silent Magic and Spirit Familiar
Services: debaters for decrees, and Aiakia's rituals, each for the neutralisation of a shard
Boon: Powerful Ally (Minthe, the covenant's patron)
Boon: Wealth; Vast and Labyrinthine; Veteran Fighters (grogs who fight blind)
Hook: Uncontrolled Portal (the gate to Tartaros in the labyrinth)
Hook: Infamous (stygian magic and dark rumours)
Hook: Rival (House Tremere, which wants its records of the Sundering)
Tension: its Terrae Cult is the heart of Kampe's Lovers, who would loosen Hades's hold on the titans
covenants.secrets:
Kampe's Lovers, centred on Hedyosmos's cult, mean to weaken Hades's power over the titans' prison and set them free to bring a golden age of magic; this is the Theban cult's aim, not the Terrae Cult's at large.
Ausculator's mater vanished; he says she will not return, and most think she went into the lower labyrinth and never came out.
Vrakos the cook, beneath the magi's notice, has been won over by Askalaphos, the faerie tattletale of Hades whom Demeter cursed into a screech owl. He has become a priest of Hades, holds secret rites in the depths and quietly recruits among the servants; for now he asks only offerings of milk, honey and a black ram's blood.
The Estate of Hades: Askalaphos means in time to make the covenant a temple of Hades again and rid it of the magi; the Aegis of the Hearth stands in his way, and he wonders how to get himself invited into the ritual.
Proximios hopes to turn Aiakia and Tisiphon against Gigas, and Celaenea against Lucian of Aegaea.

Library: Ausculator's works on Terram, and the covenant's records of the time of the Sundering

covenants.name: Oikos tou Eleous
covenants.notes:
Patron: St Demetrios, martyred Roman soldier and patron of Thessaloniki (see the Hagios Demetrios).

Covenfolk: none as such, and no grogs; the magae and their own people do whatever is needed. Anna runs the convent as mother superior, and her six novices are mostly widows of the recent wars. One, the cantankerous, sullen Gemma, has been there since 1185 and knows the sisters are far older than they look; she puts it down to God's grace, while loudly complaining of the unfairness. The nuns do their own housework, with one hired man, John the gardener.

Founded 1185. The book gives no season.

params.detail: the royal court through the twins
the boy king, the regency and the Montferrat claim
Epiros closes in; a siege is expected within a year

covenants.summary:
The House of Mercy, one of the last Jerbiton covenants in the Tribunal, of the Aegean phyle, in Thessaloniki, and known as the Ladies of Thessaloniki for its four magae. It is no single place but an alliance of magae bound, somewhat like a lavra, by a typikon (charter) to defend one another and to restore the city's health of body and soul. All four are holy magae, under vows of poverty, chastity and obedience and a heavy round of devotions; holy magae of three traditions, they have little use for vis, books or lab texts and hold few common resources, quite unlike most covenants.

Two holy magae founded it after the Sicilian sack of 1185, when five thousand citizens died, holy places were deliberately desecrated and a strong Infernal aura rose over the ruined streets. They soon found a wide diabolist ring tied to the Paulician heresy and set about fighting it and the demonic corruption of the citizens, and still preach and dispute against the Paulicians who live lawfully within the walls, whose evil few suspect, so that most take the nuns for bigots. The Infernal auras have much faded, but the fight for the city's soul goes on.

They worked to heal the wounded in body and spirit, and when Constantinople fell their example showed what could be done for a broken city. Even so, three of the magi, the men, took the signs for the end of days and left for Rome, believing they were needed there; only the sisters stayed. In 1207 they called on St Demetrios against the besieging Bulgarian tsar, and are sure the tsar died that October by the saint's own hand. The same year twins of the Seirene tradition came from Lesbos and at once drew the covenant into court affairs through their quiet support of Queen Margaret of Hungary, whose son Demetrios was already a great favourite of the nuns.

It is devoted to the protection of King Demetrios, the veneration of his namesake saint, and the survival of Thessaloniki, capital since 1205 of a kingdom attacked by Bulgarians and Epirotes and torn by the quarrel over the boy king's regency and William of Montferrat's claim; a siege seems likely within a year unless the new Latin emperor steps in. With Gigas it makes up the League Against Idolatry, which wants the Ceremony of Propitiation banned.
covenants.what_matters:
Laboratory: the chapel of Koukoubiou (Divine aura 4), and the twins' cramped room in the royal palace
Resources: very few in common; the nuns live on their own wealth
Boon: Powerful Ally (Saint Demetrios, the covenant's patron)
Boon: Urban (Thessaloniki); Informants (the royal court through the twins)
Hook: Mundane Politics (the boy king, the regency and the Montferrat claim)
Hook: War Zone (Epiros closes in; a siege is expected within a year)
Hook: Heretics (the Paulicians within the walls)
Tension: the twins argue with each other and want better laboratories
Tension: Nonna would oppose any man joining the covenant
Tension: the League Against Idolatry's petition against the Propitiation divides the Tribunal

covenants.name: Aegaea
covenants.notes:
The patron. Triton, son and herald of Poseidon, is perhaps the mightiest of the Tribunal's patrons, and unusually has a Faerie Might: a great golden-skinned merman with a trident and a conch trumpet that can calm the waves or rouse them. Sometimes he is at the palace, sometimes far off in the Aegean. A host of tritones (Realms of Power: Faerie) attends him, men above and dolphins below, their torsos mostly covered in small hard scales; the swiftest, the centaur-tritones, have a horse's forelegs in place of arms. They are his warriors, messengers and servants.

Customs. Aegaea makes much of ceremony and of the old myths, Poseidon's above all. The few visitors are often cast in a role in some elaborate rite or re-enactment on arrival, and in an eccentric mood Lucian sets them a small quest before he will see them. Most Redcaps have cut these welcomes down to a bearable nuisance, but Lucian still names each of them after a child of Hermes (Pan, Tyche, Hermaphroditus, Rhodos and so on). Lucian writes to other covenants in the Theban way, in tales whose meaning must be read between the lines.

Founded: the book says about two centuries ago; 1020 is assumed.
covenants.summary:
One of the Tribunal's most splendid covenants, of the Aegean phyle, and one of its strangest and hardest to reach: a sanctuary under the sea in what is thought to be Poseidon's palace, devoted to keeping and studying the legends of the Tribunal, old and new. It is an Autumn covenant with strong magic at hand, but its magi are thought to wield little power beyond their sea floor, and many Theban magi wave it aside for its Faerie aura and the faerie leanings of most of its members.

Orithyia of Merinita founded it about two centuries ago. By her own account (her lively books of fantastic journeys are half legend in the Tribunal), returning from Arcadia she was guided through the sea by a mighty golden man with a dolphin's tail, whom she took for Triton, Poseidon's herald, and made a pact with him to stay with her followers; the palace, she reasoned, could only be Homer's Aegaea, and she named the covenant for it. The Tribunal doubted her until Redcaps vouched for the place, and its splendour, and its patron.

Ever since, Aegaea has been a little-understood, aloof presence, distrusted by many; hardly any magi but Redcaps have seen it, though most who have speak well of their welcome. Under Lucian it has earned a fair name as a fickle ally whose loyalties shift like the sea, though it has sometimes served the Tribunal by dealing with menaces under the waves. Lucian has gathered about half a dozen magi, mostly Merinita and Bjornaer, cast in his mind as members of Poseidon's court. Every magus needs some Aquam to come and go; non-Merinita who live long here, eating faerie food and using faerie materials, become heavily Warped.
covenants.what_matters:
Boon: Powerful Ally (Triton, the covenant's patron)
Boon: Regio (the palace, Faerie aura 8); Fantastic Environment (air-like water, constant sunlight); Inhuman Residents (the tritones and nereids); Wealth (faerie treasure, real only inside the regio)
Hook: Faerie Aura; Hermetic Politics (Lucian's shifting alliances); Warping to a Pattern (non-Merinita are heavily Warped)
Income: almost none needed; the tritones furnish food, furniture, tools and clothes, and only parchment, ink and some laboratory rarities come from outside
Devices: items lent to visitors, such as a necklace that turns the wearer into a sea lion and a floating orb in a bubble of air; a magic conch on permanent loan to the Tribunal's Redcaps calls the covenant from up to a league away
Turb: no human servants or grogs; an army of warrior tritones in need
Horses: faerie-blooded horses bred in the palace stables, given as gifts
Tension: blamed for every shipwreck, and thought treacherous; predictable only in defending Faerie sites and rebuking those who abuse them
Tension: Lucian's Children of Olympos and his secret Mysteries
Tension: it says loyalty to Triton, lord of the tritones, keeps it out of the battle for the Stone Ship of Corfu's vis (see Greece), and it enjoys coaxing other magi into trying
covenants.secrets:
They probably could do real harm to other covenants' shipping if they ever cared to.
Lucian is the only magus with an Olympian Pact; he is mystagogue of every member of his league who has Elysian Ecstasy, and may be channelling pretenders, faerie or infernal, rather than gods.
Proximios means to have the nosy Delfini falsely accused of diabolism by the League of the Vigilant, and to set Celaenea of Hedyosmos against Lucian.

Library: a surprisingly good one, excellent in Faerie Lore and Aquam, and a peerless collection of ancient Greek and Byzantine poetry

covenants.name: Favonius
covenants.notes:
The patron. Dryops was once a mere woodpecker spirit, one of the Fauni (Realms of Power: Magic), whose ambition and restlessness made it genius loci of a mountain wood; but as a bird it had roamed, and now it was fixed in place. Jumping at Memnos's plan, it gave up being a Daimon and genius loci by Transformation and became a wandering spirit again. Each use of its Regio power costs it 15 points of Might for good, which it bears gladly for the adventures it has as the fleet's spirit. To Second Sight it is a woodpecker as big as a goose, spotted black and white with a red face, usually perched in some ship's rigging.

Customs. Favonius keeps off the main sea lanes to stay unseen, and has sailed to the Black Sea, Cyprus, Egypt and Sicily; the ships mostly keep together, while the small cogs scout ahead and watch shipping, warships above all. It will usually carry magi of other covenants, having seldom a destination of its own. The magi have sworn to find ways to give Dryops back its lost Might, which makes them slaves to its whims; it has recovered enough to agree to Memnos's fifth sanctum ship.

Covenfolk. Drawn from all round the Mediterranean, they speak the Lingua Franca among themselves; their numbers change with the season, as some spend the winter at home on one island or another. The flotilla counts a dozen little cogs and scores of skiffs and rafts. Basil of Andros, the chief companion, a merchant-adventurer (City & Guild) on his way to his own trading house, keeps the supplies coming and quarrels hotly with Verecunda. Peter Monocheiros, 'One Hand', a pirate who owes Aeliophanes his life, owns two of the vessels and commands eight of the best fighters.

Founded: the book gives no year, only that Memnos conceived the covenant about fifty years ago and spent decades on the first ship; 1190 is assumed for the Philomela's first voyage.
covenants.summary:
An unusual covenant of the Kretan phyle: a flotilla of four main ships with a train of others, forever sailing the Aegean, the creation of Memnos, one of the best-known living Verditii, and kept moving by its thrill-hungry patron.

Some fifty years ago, travelling in mainland Greece, Memnos met Dryops, a bored genius loci who longed to roam and see the world. Memnos offered it that in return for part of its power: he had its oak forest on a mountainside felled and carried to his workshop on Andros, the spirit with it, and after decades of planning began his great work, a ship of Dryops's wood which the spirit would inhabit and in which it would raise a Magic regio for a laboratory. While building it Memnos came to dread the sea, so his apprentice was the first captain. The Philomela sailed for many years, gathering ships for the covenant's companions and grogs; when the Procne joined her, the covenant took the name Favonius, for the kindly west wind. The Tereus and the Halcyon followed, and Memnos is building a fifth and final magical ship.

It has five magi: Memnos, who stays ashore at his shipyard; his filia Verecunda, the real leader, on the Philomela; Aeliophanes on the Tereus; and one more on each of those ships, whom the book leaves to the storyguide (or the sancta may be empty, and with the fifth ship coming the covenant could be a home for a troupe's magi).
covenants.what_matters:
Boon: Powerful Ally (Dryops, the covenant's patron)
Boon: Magical Fortress (the four enchanted ships); Regio (a laboratory regio on each sanctum ship); Hunters or Sailors
Hook: Constantly Mobile; Indebted (a great debt to Dryops)
Income: trade by the Procne under Basil of Andros; a third of Peter Monocheiros's plunder
Services: passage for other magi, sometimes for a shard neutralised for one of their members
Expansion: a fifth sanctum ship of three laboratories is being built at Memnos's shipyard
Tension: Basil wants profitable voyages; Verecunda and Dryops want adventures
Tension: the patron's notion of excitement often puts the fleet in real danger
covenants.secrets:
Peter Monocheiros pays the covenant a third of his plunder for its protection; Basil sells anything traceable in distant ports.
Peter's crew wear masks at their 'work', and his ships are enchanted to change their look, so nothing can be traced to Favonius.

Library: no books named

covenants.name: Ingasia
covenants.notes:
The patron. Mosychlos, the volcano's moody genius loci, took little notice of the magi, who were happy to live off his aura like parasites; when the Theban Tribunal was founded and every covenant needed a patron, they made a formal pact with him. He is crabbed and cantankerous: his grumbles shake the ground and sometimes bring down tunnels, and in a rage he floods the passages near the core with lava. His oath binds him to keep this rare, but it still happens, so the magi have made devices that stop the magma and shore up the tunnels; while they stay in place, he is no danger.

The covenant. Stone houses on the slopes, one for each magus; a great stone hall as meeting room and the way into the labyrinth beneath, where the laboratories, vis stores and library lie, the magi using only the tunnels to rooms they know. Life runs as regularly as a weavers' guild: forge-companions and magi work by day, Stouritus and his autocrat plan, and vendatores sell the items. Redcaps call often with the Tribunal's needs, news from Verdi and gossip about the Theban Verditii. Stouritus handles every inner and outer affair so the others can stay at their forges, and has announced that Ingasia welcomes new Verditius members, to show the Order a welcoming, well-run house against a narrow, quarrelsome Verdi.

Covenfolk. Few are islanders. Most are karkinoi, descendants of a tribe Hephaistos found when he fell to Lemnos: amphibious, born and raised in the sea before they walk on land, with pincers for hands. They live in three stone houses by the coast joined to the covenant by tunnels, two for the karkinoi and one for the mundane forge-companions. A dozen covenfolk serve as maids, cooks and servants. The autocrat, Theodorus, has his own house and keeps the accounts of money and vis.

Founded: the book gives no year: in law after Verdi; the pact with Mosychlos dates from the Tribunal's founding.
covenants.summary:
An Autumn covenant of the Aegean phyle on Lemnos and, if a House's domus magna is wherever its primus lives, the domus magna of House Verditius: Stouritus, primus since lately, has stayed here rather than move to Verdi. Most Verditii, wrapped up in their own work, hardly care, but the question will matter more as the Verditius Contest of 1234 draws near.

Gifted smiths have worked here since long before the Order. In the age of the gods Hephaistos built a forge on Lemnos and trained Gifted helpers; they stayed when he left, living apart to dull the distrust they felt for one another, and kept up their craft and their apprentices without ever growing rich. With the Order and the Parma they could truly work together, and their number grew from two to three to six and more. In law Ingasia was founded after Verdi; in history it was Hephaistos's first forge, and its magi think it the older and nobler. It stayed neutral in every war of Thebes and every quarrel of the Order, selling enchanted items to all sides alike.

The fall of Constantinople strained that neutrality. Venice has held Lemnos since 1204 and seized its products, the Lemnian Earth above all, so the magi have had to raise the prices of the items they sell. Its stated purpose is to carry on House Verditius's traditions, serving the whole Tribunal by staying strictly neutral and selling to anyone who can pay. Its six magi are all Verditius: Stouritus, Theorus the Old, Hydatius, Eudoxia, and the twins Gemma and Bobila.

Boon: Powerful Ally (Mosychlos, the covenant's patron)
Boon: Aura (Magic 4); Vast and Labyrinthine (the tunnels under the volcano); Famous Resident (the primus); Prestige (Verditius domus magna in all but name)
Boon: a shared forge laboratory at the Forge of Hephaistos, +8 to Rego and +5 to enchanting
Hook: House Covenant; Natural Disaster (the volcano's tempers); Inhuman Covenfolk (the karkinoi)
Income: enchanted items sold to all sides through vendatores; five a year may go to mundanes, Items of Quality not counted
Income lost: the Lemnian Earth, seized by Venice
Duty: the Forge of Hephaistos under Olympos (see Greece), kept by Theorus the Old
Plans: Stouritus's new buildings above ground and laboratories below, to host the Contest of 1234; Egyptian marble and Trebizond oak are on order, masons and labourers hired from the villages
Tension: pro-Verdi and pro-Ingasia factions of the House over the Contest's venue
Tension: suspected of a secret deal with the old doge, or of aiding the crusade, since Venice took Lemnos alone of the northern isles
covenants.secrets:
Gemma and Bobila sell more enchanted items than the law allows, and favour Nicaea, sworn enemy of Venice; Stouritus, busy with his buildings, has not noticed, and they raise the covenant's wealth slowly to avoid notice. Their long-term aims are unknown.
Theodorus has seen the twins' rising takings but says nothing, since the money will pay for Stouritus's building.
Proximios is using Hydatius and the League of the Vigilant to persecute innocent magi; a demon in Hydatius's likeness is to lead the league's members to attack.

Vis: a large store kept on hand for enchanting, unusual in the Theban Tribunal, kept by the autocrat

Library: no books named; kept underground in the labyrinth

covenants.name: Polyaigos
covenants.notes:
The patron. Unusually, a Faerie patron for a covenant of Magic aura whose magi care little for the fay: Varazes, a huge drakos, a faerie giant of great courage and strength, who thinks himself the island's guardian. He is a mighty ally, but his stupidity and clumsiness sometimes make him a burden; he visits when bored or lonely, and falls hopelessly in love with any handsome woman who comes, which takes tact to end peacefully. Angered, he may become a vast serpent, though his blocky, man-like head stays the same. At the Ceremony of Propitiation the magi recite the foes he has beaten.

Covenfolk. Many, mostly men given the covenant's bent, with a turb famous for its training, gear, strength and fitness; a handful of its soldiers are giants who must have drakos blood. A crew mans the warship. Several have wives and families on Melos.

Founded: the book gives only the eleventh century; 1050 is assumed.

params.detail: the Duke of Naxos covets its wealth

covenants.summary:
A strong Autumn covenant of the Kretan phyle, sworn to protect and defend the Theban Tribunal and its magi, whose members, undisputed masters of their island, have formidable martial and magical skill. Far from threatening other covenants they are widely valued for their tireless service: whenever magi are menaced by war, strife, renegades or hedge wizards, Polyaigos is first to stand up for the Order. Its good name, its famous school and its nearness to Delos bring it many visitors.

In the eleventh century a nest of stringles, foul crow-women (see the Infernal landscape), infested the island and plagued the Cyclades, Delos too. When a renegade Flambeau was found among them aiding their crimes, the Tribunal's Assembly demanded action, and the hoplite Quaesitor Laskaris fought his way ashore. There he met the native drakos Varazes and struck a quick alliance against the common foe: Laskaris duelled the renegade and shielded the giant, who clubbed the Flambeau to death. Having killed or driven out the witches and cleansed the site, he founded a covenant there named for the island, pledged to make the Tribunal strike harder and faster at such enemies.

It has since had several victories over the Tribunal's foes and won the trust of most, though not all, Theban magi, building its strength (now great) while taking care to work with nearby covenants rather than provoke them. With eight sancta its membership stays at eight, more than one of them Flambeau and more than one Guernicus, drawn by fighting or by teaching; several are hoplites, and the magi are often sent for when a battle is looming. It is run with military discipline under a leader chosen by the council of magi, who takes the rank and title of general.
covenants.what_matters:
Boon: Powerful Ally (Varazes, the covenant's patron)

Warship: a crewed war galley in the island's small harbour

Tension: Caterina's Venetian links make other Jerbiton distrust her
covenants.secrets:
Marco Sanudo, Duke of Naxos, overlord in name of the Cyclades, has heard of the school's wealth and envies it.
Caterina has met the duke, posing as a rich noblewoman, and is laying the ground for a quiet arrangement with him.
Satabus, newly arrived, is the duke's lost brother Pietro and has not yet written to him.
Proximios means to have Caterina falsely accused of diabolism by the League of the Vigilant.

Library: kept in the watchtower on the high peak; no books named

covenants.name: Michael's Tabula
covenants.notes:
The patron, Fylakas. When the founders fled into the catacombs in 1204, a mighty figure of living stone rose out of the ground to shield them from the crusaders and help them. They named it Fylakas, 'guard', and took it as their patron, but have never managed a long talk with it and know little of it. It commands the earth: it rules the catacombs' gateways and can shake the ground hard enough to damage or bring down buildings in the city. Most likely it is an ancient earth elemental.

Covenfolk. The covenant cannot yet afford to hire or house many. Its magi have instead gathered a motley crew of rogues, spies and mercenaries who serve part-time and lead double lives, so that the covenant itself stays mostly out of sight.

Founded: 1207, at the Tribunal after the fall; the oath was sworn in 1204. Season: the book gives none; it is a young covenant.

params.detail: the catacombs, sealed by walls only the magi's keys open
a part-time following of rogues, spies and mercenaries
its covert war on the Latins

covenants.summary:
The newer of the two covenants inside Constantinople, of the Propontian phyle: a close band of devout magi, mostly Jerbiton, who lived through the sack of 1204 and swore to stay. In public the covenant is pledged to restoring the city to its old glory; its real aim is to drive the crusaders out, and several sympathetic magi and covenants help it in secret.

Michael, a famed magus of Thermakopolis, led the Jerbiton who tried and failed to defend the city, and was the last of that covenant to fall, fighting. As he lay dying, he, his surviving apprentice Petros, Wilrich of Flambeau and three other Jerbiton magi, two of Moero's Garden and a city eremite, vowed their lives to the city's defence and swore never to leave it to the invaders. The oath was cut into a stone tablet, which named the new covenant. The survivors went down into the catacombs, some bitter and hungry for revenge, others praying for deliverance, made new sancta there and hid what magical resources they had left. The covenant was formally founded at the Tribunal of 1207, the first after the fall.

It still feels like an underground resistance, fervent but disordered: its councils are loud and chaotic, the magi split over how cautious or daring to be against the Frankish rulers, yet they close ranks round their cause. Some in the Tribunal, the Quaesitores among them, eye the covenant and its likely meddling with suspicion, but more sympathise with it.

About half a dozen magi, mostly Jerbiton and many living in the city since before the Fourth Crusade, all devout Christians, led by Petros, Michael's filius, and with Wilrich of Flambeau as its sword.

links.note: Two of the founders came from it

covenants.what_matters:
Boon: Powerful Ally (Fylakas, the covenant's patron)
Income: a generous gift of money and books every year or two, brought by a Redcap from a sponsor who stays anonymous
Boon: Hidden Ways (the catacombs, sealed by walls only the magi's keys open); Criminals (a part-time following of rogues, spies and mercenaries)
Hook: Urban; Mundane Politics (its covert war on the Latins); Poverty (too poor to keep many covenfolk); Fallen Temple (the mithraeum)

covenants.secrets:
Fylakas may instead be a demon loosed from its binding in the sack, deceiving the pious magi.
Despite their piety, one or more of the magi might stoop to demonic help if it would rid the city of the Franks.
The book leaves the anonymous sponsor's identity to the storyguide.

Vis: a few unnamed sources in the catacombs

Library: a young collection, partly old books saved from Thermakopolis, swelled by the anonymous sponsor's gifts

covenants.name: Xylinites
covenants.notes:
The patron, St. Loukia. The icon is set in a gilded frame only six inches by four, a mosaic of tiny squares of gold, silver and coloured stone: a lovely young woman seated in a meadow with a lamb, while thriving flocks, birds and even the fish of the brook at her feet gaze at her. It glows with life, and now and then, it is said, the figure lifts her arms and shrieks a warning in a tiny voice. That has happened three times since the covenant came by it: before the fire that burnt the orphanage and killed many children, before Manzikert in 1071, and once more in spring 1204. Words in demotic Greek on the frame call her 'Loukia, Herald of Last Things', and the Criamon watch it eagerly. She was likely a Montanist, of the early sect that sought direct experience of the spirit, whose founder claimed to be the Holy Spirit; a pantheist mystic of nature with a deep bond to every kind of beast, whose visions were of the Magic Realm, chiefly the part tied to the Form of Animal.

Covenfolk. A small staff of grogs runs the covenant's mundane affairs in elaborate Byzantine robes that mark rank and office: grey for tutors, blue for orphans, black for servants. The four eunuch priests among its companions live in the priests' house by the master's house.

Founded: 1074. The book dates the near-destruction to 1205 in places; the city fell in 1204.

covenants.summary:
A long-established covenant inside the walls of Constantinople, of the Propontian phyle: until 1204 a great Jerbiton covenant in the monastery and orphanage of St. Christopoulos, and now the Tribunal's only Clutch, three Criamon magi on the Path of the Body. Nearly destroyed when the city fell, it is fading into Winter with its new inhabitants. Its patron is St. Loukia of Berytus, a magical spirit held in a false icon.

In 1071 Tikh of Jerbiton, hired as a teacher at the orphanage school, saw that the monastery's icon of St. Loukia was strange, and knew her for Loukia of Berytus, a Montanist heretic who claimed to have entered paradise bodily through the Holy Spirit and was put to death for blasphemy in the fourth century. With the abbot's leave he moved the icon from the church to the schoolroom, was amazed to see a Magic aura slowly grow round it, and quickly took it to the schoolmaster's house where he lived. Wanting room for a laboratory, he found and partly drained the cistern beneath, founding Xylinites in 1074.

For 130 years its magi taught at the orphanage, which let them school many brilliant young men, find Gifted children left with the monks, and build strong ties inside the palace. The palace always wanted more eunuchs than it could find, and the school became a chief source of them; former pupils at court favoured the orphanage, and the Jerbiton lived well, studied freely and swayed the court at one remove, treading a fine line between serving the imperial court and great families and wielding political influence. The conquest ended that: three Jerbiton died fighting the attackers and the rest fled into exile, fearing the Tribunal's censure, while the court's officials scattered and the Latins, revolted by castration, stopped asking for eunuchs. The one magus who stayed, Artoud of Criamon, made the cistern a Clutch for mystical research. The Tribunal saw Xylinites turn inward and shut its gates to outsiders.

Its life is fragile. Artoud's Blatant Gift keeps him from teaching or even meeting the monks, who believe him and the two apprentices he trained to be holy hermits given to fierce mortification. The covenant's companions now teach the orphans and deal with the monastery for it; visitors come and go as in any Orthodox house, and the staff barely deal with the monks, still less with the hermits. Children are still left at the orphanage, and now and then a Gifted boy abandoned by frightened parents has won the Clutch some standing at Tribunal. How long this can last, no one knows.
covenants.what_matters:
Boon: Local Ally (St. Loukia, the covenant's patron)
Income: the orphanage, still paid for from the imperial treasury by the Latins, and taught by the covenant's companions
Allies: four eunuch priests among its companions, who say mass in nunneries across the city and have the ear of many retired noblewomen and at least one former empress
Boon: Hidden Ways (the flooded tunnels under the city); Literate Covenfolk (the tutors)
Hook: Urban; Monastery (the monks of St. Christopoulos, who must go on thinking the magi hermits); Infants (the orphans, some Gifted)
Hook: Heretics (its patron is a Montanist heretic in a false icon); Dwindling Resource (the eunuch trade that once fed it)
Tension: curious orphans keep sneaking into the vaults
Tension: Trasaricus's imperial blood and hatred of the Doukas family make him a danger in the city
Tension: Artoud gives fitful support to the League Against Idolatry's petition against the Ceremony of Propitiation
covenants.secrets:
Meditating on the icon works as a summa of Animal Ken, level 3, Quality 10. None of the magi has realised it, since they fear to meditate on it long, but the Criamon may find it out.
Loukia is not dead but caught in something like Twilight between this world and the Magic Realm, which is why the aura pours from her icon.
Artoud knows Trasaricus must soon be sent far from the city to avert disaster, but cannot bring himself to expel him.

Vis: the book names none

Library: the orphanage's library and scriptorium; St. Loukia's icon is unknowingly a summa of Animal Ken

covenants.name: Alexandria
covenants.notes:
The patron. Fides is an eidolon, the spirit of loyalty born of the steadfast devotion of Alexander's soldiers to their king. When he died and his empire fell apart she stayed among the troops, and found those posted at Smyrna the most devoted; the most loyal of them became ghosts, held by their slavish faith in Alexander's idea of empire, and she thrives among their tents on the regio's first level. Methodius bound her on the promise that the covenant would go on honouring Alexander and his empire, and tied that to the Tribunal: she is content with the 'Hermetic Empire of Thebes' in place of world conquest, and will stay as long as the members stay loyal to it and to the Order. Chapter three, in passing, instead says Alexandria reveres the spirit of a grove of myrrh trees; the covenant's own section names Fides.

The artifacts. Alexander's two relics belong to the covenant: any member may use them, and they may be lent to any Theban magus whose tokens outnumber his shards, against a deposit of vis or valued magic items that grows with the length of the loan, plus 1 pawn of vis a week, and must come back on time. The flying device is a two-wheeled chariot with waist-high rails and a long hitch, a mechanica with one power: it rises into the air as lightly as smoke but cannot be steered, drifting on the wind, unless flying beasts with a total Size of +8 are yoked to it (the hitch takes four, the car six riders of Size 0); the tale of Alexander's gryphons is unproven. Its horses, each shod with a magic flying shoe, escaped two years ago, shoes and all. The glass submarine is a living iron dolphin the size of an elephant, holding five riders, chained by six hundred feet of iron to a guarded ship in Smyrna harbour that is used like any other merchant vessel to avoid suspicion; only someone with Mechanica or Automata can repair it, which Catella lacks, though a few Theban Verditius have Automata. Redcaps keep the lesser items given to them: water-shedding cloaks, vis gauges, flasks that keep wine sweet.

Covenfolk. A dozen servants and cooks, not fighters, live in the inner regio; two dozen more work the warehouses, docks and ships in Smyrna on good pay and are fairly loyal. The covenant gives its staff a feast each year in a private house in Smyrna; most of the town workers have never been to Alexandria or met its strange-looking elders.

Founded: the site was chosen after Miphoria failed (by 1063) and the building was finished in 1075, the year given here.

Members: fifteen Redcaps and Catella. Leontius and Proximios are named; the book names none of the other Redcaps of Alexandria, kept here as thirteen unnamed members. Lysandros, Diantha and Niko, the Redcaps of chapter three, have no covenant in the book and may be among them.

params.detail: the Tribunal's records and the logothete's register
a Nicene garrison holds the outer citadel; food must be smuggled in and members slip in and out

covenants.summary:
The Mercere covenant of the Tribunal, of the Kretan phyle, and the hub of its bureaucracy and its news: home to most of the Theban Redcaps and a retreat for those too old or too Warped to ride any more. Its stone houses stand in a regio inside the ruined citadel on Mount Pagus above Smyrna, which a Nicene garrison now occupies. It is an Autumn covenant.

It is the second all-Mercere covenant of Thebes. The first, Miphoria, on the shore outside Smyrna, travelled by marvellous and open magic, riding giant magical sea turtles among other things; the Tribunal judged it drew mundane eyes to the Order and told it to lie low, and without its turtles it withered, most of its Redcaps living in other covenants by 1063. A central house had made the Redcaps' paperwork far easier, so a second was thought wise.

Methodius, then the best-loved Redcap of the Tribunal, who claimed Alexander's blood and had won fame by finding Alexander's flying device in Seljuk lands, chose the old fortress on Mount Pagus, with its Magic aura and regiones, though Alexander's ghostly soldiers haunted it. He bound an eidolon living among the ghosts as patron, left the broken walls alone to avoid soldiers' notice, built in wood in the aura and in stone in the regio, finished in 1075, and named the covenant after the many cities of his ancestor.

Centralised Redcap work and trade treaties with the nations round the Aegean made it rich; Seekers it paid found the glass submarine, a second of Alexander's relics, and the pair drew Philagrius of Verditius, who found both were mechanica made by Heron's heirs. But the strong Longevity Rituals its members took warped them: many lived very long and gathered magical Flaws, shunned the world and hid in the regio, and the covenant that had been known for bold merchant venturers and shrewd politicians came to be seen as a home for odd old Redcaps.

It still does its work, but the fall of Constantinople has cost it. Petronas, logothete for nearly a century, gave up the post at the Tribunal of 1207, and his successor Leontius has done badly, barely escaping ostracism in 1214; and the emperor's soldiers now sit in its outer houses. Its fifteen members are all unGifted Redcaps but one, the Bonisagus maga Catella: five elders past 130, much twisted by Warping, who live in the regio retelling old exploits, taunting the ghosts and needling each other; five in middle age (sixty to a hundred, Warping 3 to 5), who run the covenant, its trade and the Tribunal's records and hold the better posts; and five young ones who live in Smyrna or farther off and ride as messengers and heralds, building the standing for weightier work.

Boon: Powerful Ally (Fides, the covenant's patron)

Proximios, the likely next logothete and co-founder of the League of the Vigilant, is secretly an infernalist bent on the Order's downfall; his place at Alexandria lets him read the missives and private letters that pass through it (see his entry and An Enemy Within).

covenants.name: Moero's Garden
covenants.notes:
The patrons. Moero's ghost is still bound at the old site in Constantinople, but the Tribunal requires a covenant's patron to live within it, so Ionnia had to summon and bind a second, the ghost of Hipparchus, against its will. It is weak in Might and resents being woken from centuries of sleep, so it torments whoever it can, chiefly the covenfolk, the magi being too strong for it: pulling hair, knocking over wine bowls, snuffing lamps. When it grows unbearable Ionnia calms it by spending an evening with it watching the stars and talking astronomy, which settles it for a week or so.

Covenfolk. About forty craftsmen and servants work for the covenant. The autocrat Pastor runs its daily business and finances, now shrinking, and its ever smaller vis stores; to make up the losses he has used most of the treasury to back craftsmen and artists of Nicaea, who have grown rich and now give much of the covenant's income. Two of them can make enchanted goods: Nanno, who makes wondrous cosmetics, and Ampelius, who paints breathtaking religious murals. The magi like the money but shudder that it comes from craftsmen; Ampelius, being an artist, is held in better regard. Pastor's wife Viviana is the chief scribe and keeper of the library.

Apprentices: three of the Jerbiton have apprentices nearly ready for their Gauntlet; Syagricus's Pancratius hopes for his at the Tribunal of 1221 and will likely join as a full member.

Season: the book gives none; Autumn is the pack's reading of a covenant living on dwindling means away from its old riches.

Members: eight magi. Ionnia, Syagricus, Ziper, Trasaric and Helladius are here; Evantia, the most respected of the Seekers of the Fallen, is with the realms; the two other Jerbiton are unnamed. Krum the Swift of Aegaea was a member in Constantinople.

params.detail: the craftsmen and artists of Nicaea that its autocrat backs
the patron's ghost torments the covenfolk

covenants.summary:
A covenant of Jerbiton magi, of the Propontian phyle, living in the House of Hipparchus in Nicaea, the new capital of the exiled empire: aristocratic and effete, driven from their first home in Constantinople and longing to go back, filling the time with art and gracious living. It has eight magi, seven Jerbiton and one Tytalus with the Gentle Gift, and the League of Constantine meets here.

Ionnia of Jerbiton, a minor Byzantine noble with a love of women poets, founded it in 1163, in Manuel Komnenos's golden years, after seeking out the house of the poet Moero (about 300 BC) in the old quarters of Constantinople; it lay in one of the city's lacunae, and she summoned Moero's ghost to be patron. She gathered sodales, all Jerbiton of aristocratic family, to find the literature and art of the early Byzantine age, a task her House thinks very worthy. A member may not work for a living, like a Roman senator or Byzantine noble: income must come from land others till. It flourished, and its magi had leisure for letters and art.

In Constantinople its magi went to court functions but kept the imperial family and politicians at arm's length, spending their effort on their covenant, costly travel and visits to the Tribunal's old buildings and paintings, sure that staying out of the emperor's politics would keep them safe. When the crusaders took the city it escaped the first ruin, but fearing for its library and treasures it fled with most of the rich Greeks, carrying what it could and leaving most behind, to its chapter house in Nicaea, Hipparchus's old summer home, which is now all it has.

Its first purpose was to gather the finest art and writing of the past to show the calm, intellectual delight of beauty, cooling hot tempers and spreading serenity through the Order; since 1204 it also seeks to win back what it lost. Its magi think, like nobles, that they should not have to work, and that gets harder the longer they are away from Constantinople. Four of the seven Jerbiton belong to the League of Constantine and want the covenant to help the Nicene emperor retake the city; the youngest, Trasaric and Helladius, say it fell because the covenant idled; Ionnia and Syagricus answer that the city has come through disasters before and this occupation will pass too. The covenant is evenly split.

covenants.what_matters:
Purpose: to collect the art and literature of the past to show the harmony of beauty, and to recover what was lost in 1204
Boon: Local Ally (Hipparchus's ghost, the covenant's patron)
Boon: Secondary Income (the craftsmen and artists of Nicaea that its autocrat backs)
Hook: Urban (a merchants' quarter of Nicaea, in a Divine aura of 2)
Hook: Poverty (Minor) (its finances are dwindling); Dwindling Resource (its vis stores)
Hook: Refugee (driven out of Constantinople in 1204)
Hook: Resident Nuisance (the patron's ghost torments the covenfolk)

Allies: the League of Constantine, centred here

covenants.secrets:

Vis: its magi found the rite that makes the Serpent Column in Constantinople's Hippodrome yield 8 pawns of Animal vis a year
