Peroz, falling into a trench his enemies had dug, tore the pearl from his ear and threw it away rather than be buried with it; it has turned up now and then since, and whoever bears it near water soon meets the shark. The fishermen think the shark magical and the pearl mighty.

Vis: several of the plants would give vis each year if harvested properly. Unclaimed; Ingasia is buying Trebizond oak for its new buildings.

neighbours.name: The Hidden Shrine of Serapis at Sinope
neighbours.summary: Somewhere deep under Sinope, a heretical Christian sect meets in secret. The book gives no aura.
neighbours.secrets:
The sect has put Serapis in God's place. Alexander brought the god into Anatolia from Babylon; after his death Ptolemy took the cult statue to Egyptian Alexandria and blended Serapis with Egypt's gods to make one deity, and under Hadrian Egyptian Christians began worshipping him. The sect was thought stamped out in the fourth century, but the statue survived and its last followers smuggled it to Sinope, where it has stayed.

Serapis is a False God (see the Christians of Serapis).

neighbours.name: The House of Hipparchus
neighbours.summary:
The ancestral house of Hipparchus of Nicaea, the Greek astronomer of about 190 BC, in a merchants' quarter in a corner of Nicaea: three storeys about an outer and an inner courtyard, palatial by merchants' standards and squalid, cramped and undignified to the magi of Moero's Garden, who fled here in 1204 and have struggled to make it beautiful. Laboratories fill the top floor, the magi live on the second, the covenfolk on the ground floor, and the library and works of art are kept, to the magi's horror, in the basement.

It lies in a Divine aura of 2, no great obstacle to the magi but hard on their apprentices, who struggle to cast and to finish their training here.

neighbours.name: Emperor of Nicaea
neighbours.summary:
Theodore Laskaris, who fought bravely for Constantinople in 1204 and then fled to Nicaea, where so many great Byzantines followed that he could hold a court as splendid as the old one. He named Michael Autoreianos patriarch in 1205, and was crowned emperor in 1208; he has sworn to retake Constantinople and to keep the empire alive at Nicaea until he does. The book calls him Theodore II; history has him as Theodore I, so the pack does too.

Shrewd at turning neighbours to his use, he has been friend and foe in turn to the Latins, the Bulgarians and the Sultanate of Rum; Frankish mercenaries stiffen his army while he recruits native Anatolians. He is best known for beating the Sultan of Rum in single combat in 1211, for seizing and imprisoning his treacherous father-in-law Alexios III, and for driving along the Black Sea to check Trebizond. His cabinet rule is leaner than the old bureaucracy, the taxes that once went to Constantinople pour into Nicaea, his soldiers are content after years of victories, and art and learning flourish.

A staunch Orthodox, he is nonetheless open to Church union: he would put the Eastern Church under Rome for a time to win Constantinople, the pope has hinted that would do, and in 1220 he has gathered churchmen to end the schism, if he can bring the patriarch and Anatolia's bishops round. His peace with the Latins, sealed by marrying Marie de Courtenay in 1219, has broken, and he is about to fall on Holkos. His navy is based at Smyrna, and his favourite residence is the Palace of Nymphaeum; his soldiers occupy Alexandria's citadel.

neighbours.name: Sultan of Rum
neighbours.summary:
The Seljuk Sultanate of Rum holds the Anatolian plateau, lost to the empire after Manzikert, and in the north reaches the Black Sea at Sinope, splitting Nicaea from Trebizond. It drove north between them in 1214, killing David Komnenos, but could not reach Trebizond through the mountains. Its sultan Kaykhusraw I died at Antioch-on-the-Maeander in 1211, and the Maeander has been the border with Nicaea since. Trebizond still fears it.

The book names no sultan for 1220. History has Kaykhusraw's son Kaykaus I reign from 1211 to his death about 1220, followed by his brother Kayqubad I, who is named as ruler here.

neighbours.name: Governor of Sinope
neighbours.summary: Etoumes, a Greek and a vassal of the Seljuk sultan, though no Muslim himself, who governs Sinope and pays tribute to Rum. He is on good terms with Alexios of Trebizond. He has lately taken a new confessor.
neighbours.secrets: The confessor is a priest of the Christians of Serapis, to the demon's delight; nothing good can come of it.

neighbours.name: Emperor of Trebizond
neighbours.summary:
Alexios Komnenos, thirty-eight, grandson of the Emperor Andronikos Komnenos, who seized Trebizond with his brother David in 1204, the very year Constantinople fell, and calls himself 'Emperor and Autocrat of the Romans'. David pushed west into Paphlagonia and Heraclea, provoking Rum and then Nicaea, which won back most of his gains in 1212; Rum killed him in 1214. Alexios rules on, propped by Georgian troops and Latin and Seljuk mercenaries, cut off from Nicaea and still threatened by Rum, and also rules Cherson and Kerch across the Black Sea; Cherson pays him tribute.

He lives with his family in the castle behind the city. Like his grandfather he patronises art and letters, giving titles and stipends to astronomers, alchemists and experimental philosophers, and his Silk Road market and its taxes make Trebizond very rich.

neighbours.name: Nicene Governor of Amastris
neighbours.summary: Amastris, taken by Theodore Laskaris in 1214, marks the eastern end of the Empire of Nicaea on the Black Sea. It pays tribute to the emperor and governs itself as best it can; the book names no governor.

neighbours.name: The Orthodox Patriarchate at Nicaea
neighbours.summary:
Since Theodore Laskaris named Michael Autoreianos patriarch in 1205, the line of Orthodox patriarchs of Constantinople has carried on in exile at Nicaea. In 1220 the patriarch, Manuel I Charitopoulos, works hand in glove with the emperor; his authority is accepted in Trebizond, Epiros and the other Greek lands, and by many Orthodox under Latin rule who reject the Latin patriarch.

His cathedral is Nicaea's Haghia Sophia, at the centre of the city's grid of streets. The emperor's plan to submit the Church to Rome for a time, to win back Constantinople, needs the patriarch and the bishops of Anatolia, and the council he has called in 1220 must settle the procession of the Holy Spirit, unleavened bread and, hardest of all, the pope's primacy.

neighbours.name: Church of the Koimesis, Nicaea
neighbours.summary: The private chapel of the emperor and his family, in the south of Nicaea near the imperial palace.

neighbours.name: Church of St John the Apostle, Pergamos
neighbours.summary: The basilica serving the Christians who still live at Pergamos, one of the seven churches of Revelation; it stands over an older temple of Isis and Serapis, below the terrace of the Great Altar.

neighbours.name: Basilica of St John, Ephesus
neighbours.summary: Ephesus's cathedral, built over the tomb of St John, with a Divine aura of 5. With the houses of Mary and St John it makes the town a pilgrimage, and Ephesus has long drawn pillar saints and ascetics; their numbers give the rest of the town a Divine aura of 3.

neighbours.name: The Great Church of Philadelphia
neighbours.summary: The main church of Philadelphia, one of the seven churches of Revelation, which Greek theologians think was once the headquarters of the infant Church. Its Divine aura is 6, in a city whose own aura of 4 is unusually strong.

neighbours.name: Nicaea
neighbours.summary:
Always a great city of the empire, the emperors' summer seat and host of several Church councils, now capital of the Empire of Nicaea. Its straight streets run in a grid from the cathedral of Haghia Sophia at the centre; the palace and the Koimesis chapel lie to the south. Walls thirty feet high with over a hundred towers ring it, its three chief gates set midway along the northern, eastern and southern sides; on the west the lake of Ascania washes the wall, where small gates open on the docks. While Constantinople sinks under Infernal auras, Nicaea glows like a new dawn: revenues flow in, merchants and craftsmen thrive, scholars and theologians debate, Latin friars and papal envoys are welcome, and cypresses and peach orchards grow outside the walls. Moero's Garden lives in a merchants' quarter; the seven Demons of Nicaea hunt the roads outside but may not enter.

Relics: the exiles brought many of the smaller pieces of the True Cross from Hagia Sophia (a hand-sized piece is Faith 3 and heals a Medium Wound; a sliver is an ordinary relic).

neighbours.name: Nicomedia
neighbours.summary: A walled Roman city on the Gulf of Astacus, sixty miles east of Constantinople and a day from Nicaea, with a citadel, forums, an amphitheatre, aqueducts and cisterns, one of the few in Asia Minor the Turks have not held in a century. After 1204 a hundred Latin knights sailed over, the people fled to Nicaea, and the knights fortified the church and ruled for nearly a year until Laskaris drove them into it; Emperor Henry came to their aid, and the two traded the city for the French hostages. It has been Greek since. It suffers an earthquake about once a century, blamed by its people on St George's dragon.

neighbours.name: Holkos
neighbours.summary: The Latin-held port where the Hellespont meets the Sea of Marmara, which Theodore Laskaris is about to attack, meaning to make it a second base for his fleet against Venetian ships. History has him take it.

neighbours.name: Smyrna
neighbours.summary: Once a rival of Ephesus and Pergamos for the title of First City of Asia, it has declined since the capital moved to Constantinople, won and lost between Turks and Greeks for generations. Nicaea's strength has calmed its fears but not rebuilt it: over half the city is rubble, crumbling houses and overgrown streets leading nowhere. It is the royal port of the Nicene navy, which guards the Aegean; its war on Venetian merchants ended with the trade treaty of August 1219, and it will turn next to Chios, Lesbos and Rhodes. The harbour bustles with warships and merchantmen, Alexandria's three ships among them, and the city has the largest Jewish community in Anatolia. Alexandria's warehouses are here, its citadel on Mount Pagus above.

neighbours.name: Hagios Theologos (Ephesus)
neighbours.summary: Small but famous: one of Revelation's seven churches, the recipient of an epistle, an early centre of the faith where St Paul lived nearly three years and St John was martyred and buried, and the seat of the Third Ecumenical Council in 431, which condemned Nestorius. The Turks held it for almost forty years until the empire won it back in 1100 and renamed it Hagios Theologos. Its harbour has silted up and only a few hundred people remain, guarded by a small garrison and no wall, so a Turkish raid would go hard with it. Pilgrims and monks give it a Divine aura of 3, 5 in St John's Basilica.

neighbours.name: Pergamos
neighbours.summary: The small Christian town that survives below the ruined acropolis, by the Caicus, served by the Church of St John; its only weight with the Greeks is as one of Revelation's seven churches. Locals have chased off magi using the Great Altar as demon worshippers.

neighbours.name: Philadelphia
neighbours.summary: A strong fortress city on a high plateau at the foot of Mount Tmolus over the Maeander valley, the march against the Turks of Rum and the bulwark against their advance; its finest hour came in 1211, when Laskaris led its men out to beat Sultan Kaykhusraw. Its archers are said by the Nicenes to be the best in the world. One of Revelation's seven churches, it has a Divine aura of 4, rising to 6 in its main church. A terrible earthquake in AD 17 nearly levelled it, and since then its people have lived outside the walls, going in only when an enemy comes.

neighbours.name: Amastris
neighbours.summary: A fortified Black Sea port, Nicaea's eastern limit since 1214, with its market outside the walls, old Greek families and many foreigners, more of Scandinavian blood than elsewhere since it was once the end of the road for mercenaries coming from Russia. It pays tribute and governs itself.

neighbours.name: Sinope
neighbours.summary: A fortified port where Paphlagonia meets Pontus, the Seljuks' window on the Black Sea, much like Amastris: a market outside the walls, old Greek families and a good mix of foreigners, here more of Persian descent. Under its Muslim overlords it is unusually tolerant, letting its people be Christian, Muslim or Jewish as they please. Its Greek governor Etoumes pays tribute to Rum. A heretical sect hides beneath it.

neighbours.name: Trebizond
neighbours.summary:
The capital of the Empire of Trebizond, on ground sloping to the Black Sea with the Pontic mountains behind and a ravine on either side, beautiful and strong, with massive walls and two tall towers guarding the bridges over the ravines; the castle stands apart behind a narrow valley and its own walls. Its weak points are the harbour beside a short promontory and the market outside the walls. At one end of the Silk Road, it sells the East's goods to Western merchants and taxes every sale, and is very rich. Leaving dogma and the schools to Nicaea, its scholars pursue esoteric learning and look kindly on Persian and Arabic wisdom; among its libraries is a clean copy of Ptolemy's Geography, put back into Greek from Arabic, which no magus of Anatolia knows of, though any student of celestial magic or Ptolemy's magical coordinates would give a great deal for it. Its gardens hold magical plants, bardi wail before deaths, and a great shark haunts its docks.

Saint: Eugenios, the city's patron (an area saint, Divine Might 50).

neighbours.name: The Christians of Serapis
neighbours.summary: A heretical Christian sect hidden beneath Sinope, about two hundred strong, led by a dozen priests, who keep an ancient cult statue smuggled out of Egypt. Its priests dress and act like Orthodox clergy, never quarrelling with the Church's own priests, the better to win converts quietly.

details.wants: New followers, and a hold over Sinope's ruler
details.offers: Hidden supernatural gifts to the faithful

neighbours.secrets: Serapis is a False God, a demon. Few followers know what they worship, and he masks the Infernal nature of the Supernatural Abilities he grants them with his power to shroud the stench of the Pit. Etoumes, Sinope's Greek governor, has lately made one of its priests his confessor, to the demon's joy.

neighbours.name: The Council of Union at Nicaea
neighbours.summary: The churchmen Theodore Laskaris has gathered at Nicaea in 1220 to heal the schism between the Eastern and Western Churches. Besides the doctrinal quarrels over the procession of the Holy Spirit and unleavened bread at communion, they must settle the political question of the pope's primacy. The pope has hinted that a temporary submission would do; the emperor still has to win over the patriarch and Anatolia's bishops.

details.wants: An end to the schism of East and West, and with it Constantinople
details.offers: Imperial favour to the churchmen who agree

neighbours.name: Erythrae
neighbours.summary:
A small town on the Ionian coast facing the island of Khios, home of Demophile, the Erythraean Sibyl. Of the ten sibyls she speaks most nearly as a Christian would, and so she is the best known of them; her answers come as riddles, very often acrostics, a form she is said to have devised, in which the first letters of each line spell out the meaning.

Every sibyl sits in a strong Magic aura or regio (the book gives no number) and cannot go far from it without risking Acclimation and the loss of her sight; she seldom lives alone, and keeps guardians, mortal or otherwise. For the sibyl's character guide, see the Bestiary.

links.note: the sibyls of Ionia, Phrygia and the Hellespont

neighbours.secrets: Sibyls are magic humans, immortal and truly far-seeing, though few know it; 'sibyl' may be an office handed on rather than one woman. Their daughters by visitors, the sibyllides, are magic kin gifted in prophecy and second sight, who must come home every ten years to tell their mothers how the world goes; at least one is a magus of the Order, with a natural bent for Intellego.

neighbours.name: The Cave of the Samian Sibyl
neighbours.summary: A cave in the hills of Samos, where Phyto, the Samian Sibyl, lives among the shepherds' grazing; she is the easiest of the sibyls to approach, and the herdsmen bring her gifts. A question put to her must be framed as a rhyming riddle, but her replies are plain spoken. She lies in a strong Magic aura (no number is given) that she cannot leave without losing her gift.

neighbours.name: Dardania on Mount Ida
neighbours.summary: The slopes of Mount Ida in the Troad, where Amalthea, the Hellespontine Sibyl, has her seat; she came from Troy itself. Anyone born a Trojan may have a true prophecy of her, but on Troy, or the town that stands there now, she will say nothing at all, not since she foretold the war that killed so many of her people. Her home is a strong Magic aura (its number is not given).

neighbours.name: The Haunt of the Phrygian Sibyl
neighbours.summary: Somewhere in the Phrygian uplands of the Anatolian plateau lives the sibyl called Lamia, of ill repute even if she is probably not the child-eating faerie who shares her name. She gives no prophecy freely: a questioner must wrestle her down and force the words from her, and she is far stronger than any of her sisters. The prophets of Lamites (1123 to 1127) took her as their covenant's patron and did not live long.
neighbours.secrets: Whether the sibyl or the faerie Lamia killed the magi of Lamites is the storyguide's to say; each had cause.

neighbours.name: Akgah's Battlefield
neighbours.summary:
Open country about twelve miles from Constantinople, where nothing marks the way into an Infernal regio, the lair of the demon prince that wrecked the Fourth Crusade (see the Bestiary). Akgah takes the shape of a two-headed leopard the size of an elephant, with golden wings and fragrant gold-and-black fur, a twisted mirror of Venice's winged lion; greed, lust and battle-madness take hold of those around it.

In the spring of 1204 it fought the Hagka, the Divine two-headed eagle that guarded the city, among the statues of the Hippodrome, and broke part of the arena in the struggle. The Hagka fled wounded; crusaders who saw the fight took it for a vision of St Mark's lion winning, and fought the harder. The Hagka, Divine Might 40, now keeps to the wild mountains of Asia Minor as the protector of Nicaea, its white feathers soiled and its wounds open until the empire is made whole; it shelters any pious Greek loyal to the empire and is the enemy of every unrepentant crusader.

levels.name: The Blasted Field
levels.notes: A ruined battlefield where Akgah lolls on heaps of rotting dead, plunder and defiled relics, feeding at leisure; hundreds of pikes about it carry the bodies of suicides, ravished nuns and other lost souls. The book gives the regio no aura number.

links.note: the demon of the Fourth Crusade, laired outside the city

neighbours.secrets: Akgah planned the Fourth Crusade and the fall of the city, which raised it high among the princes of Hell. It now works to keep the successor states at war, feeding their greed and mistrust of one another. Before it, Andronikos Komnenos sold his soul to a demon in a woman's shape for the throne he took in 1182, and his massacre of the Latins set Venice and Montferrat against the empire; the excommunication of the crusaders after Zara let demons walk among them, and several of their lords made pacts for protection, fame or gold. Like Andronikos, most of the crusade's leaders were dead within a few years.

neighbours.name: The Karakalou Monastery
neighbours.summary: One of the monasteries of the Holy Mountain. A drakos in the shape of a vast serpent once crawled out of the sea and made its home here, and the monks simply kept it as their house snake (see the Faerie landscape: many drakoi can take a serpent's form, now and then with a man's head, and some grow huge).

neighbours.name: The Monastery of Hosios Loukas
neighbours.summary: A monastery on the slopes of Mount Helicon in Boeotia, built around the tomb of Saint Luke the hermit (Hosios Loukas), who lived here in the tenth century and is its patron, a local saint of Divine Might 25.

neighbours.name: Rufinianae
neighbours.summary: A monastic complex a few miles from Chalcedon, on the Asian shore of the Bosporus, where the imperial family often broke a journey. Its patron is Saint Hypatios, a local saint of Divine Might 25.

neighbours.name: The League of Constantine
neighbours.summary:
A Hermetic league that would set the empire back on its true road: a rightful Greek emperor in Constantinople and the Church out from under the pope. Earlier conquerors of the city married into its great houses and carried on the Roman line; the Latins did neither, and they bent the Church to Rome as well. Its members are all Jerbiton, though nothing requires it, and each has an apprentice near the Gauntlet from the antigones, more warlike than their masters. It is centred at Moero's Garden, where four of the seven Jerbiton belong and the two youngest blame the city's fall on their elders' idleness.

Its members have found that Infernal powers helped bring the city down, and they believe the missing hagka is the key to setting things right. The emperor's divine authority rests on three things: his battle standard (a bronze staff topped by a gold eagle, its purple silk bearing the imperial sign, last seen when Isaac Angelos's army broke before the Bulgarians in 1190; borne beside the emperor it gives his troops +3 to Discipline and Morale), his crown (made for each emperor and of no power alone, but needed to wake the others; the Latins took every old crown), and the hagka itself, a bronze two-headed eagle on a lance with an icon of the Virgin hung from it, which gives its bearer Magic Resistance 10. Together they spread that resistance to every friendly troop in sight and raise the bonus to +6. Today the Bulgarians have one, the Latins another, and the third is lost: Alexios V Doukas Mourtzouphlos left both crown and hagka behind when French knights routed him near Philia early in 1204. The league is now searching Bulgarian lands for the standard.

details.wants: A Greek emperor back on the throne of Constantinople and the Church freed of Rome; first, the lost battle standard, as a clue to the hagka
details.offers: Magi and their martial apprentices for the Nicene cause

neighbours.secrets: The league is right: the city has lost Divine favour, and the hagka's return would bless a truly devout emperor, Greek or not, with Solomon's wisdom, David's strength and St Paul's mercy. But the demons have hidden from its spells; it knows the fall was Infernal work but not whose hands, and so cannot tell friend from foe. The hagka may be whole or broken, in a crusader's treasury, a Greek monastery, the burned Venetian quarter's rubble or the bed of the Bosporus.

neighbours.name: The Children of Olympos
neighbours.summary:
A small, odd Hermetic league gathered round Lucian the Scholar of Merinita, of Aegaea. It holds that the Order should turn from the waning Divine and Infernal to an older footing: magical beings care nothing for mortals, but faeries are drawn to the fates of men, and the Greek gods have outlasted every rival. It wants each covenant's patron to be one of the old gods. It has sympathisers but few true members, most of them Merinita; its existence is open, its methods are not.

Lucian has invented two Mysteries by which a person channels a chosen god, who possesses her and lends her his Personality Trait and Sympathy Traits: Elysian Ecstasy (Minor) and the stronger, riskier Olympian Pact (Major, with a Major Personality Flaw fitting the god, and a share of the god's powers at a Warping Point a use). The initiation needs no Merinita cult lore: the initiate wins a boon from twelve mighty beings, each standing for one Olympian, then performs a rite in an Olympian's shrine as Sirius rises, taking Susceptibility to Faerie Power with the gift. Lucian has been mystagogue for every member who knows Elysian Ecstasy; he alone has the Pact.

Seekers commonly match the Houses to the Olympians: Bjornaer to Poseidon, Bonisagus to Zeus, Criamon to Hestia or Dionysos, Ex Miscellanea to Demeter, Flambeau to Apollon, Guernicus to Hera, Jerbiton to Aphrodite, Mercere to Hermes, Merinita to Artemis, Tremere to Athena, Tytalus to Ares and Verditius to Hephaistos; Diedne was Demeter, later Hades. Some say Trianoma chose the Founders to fit the pattern, and that a House was bound to fall once Ex Miscellanea made thirteen.

details.wants: The old Greek gods as the covenants' patrons, bound by lasting pacts
details.offers: Initiation into Elysian Ecstasy, with Lucian as mystagogue

neighbours.secrets: Under it lies Lucian's unspoken hope that Faerie will replace the Magic auras of the Theban covenants and bring back the worship of the gods. He believes the gods feed on their epic stories, which must be lived again, and he has cast many of the Tribunal's magi and covenants as players in his great re-enactment: his sudden, seemingly treacherous shifts at Tribunal are attempts to push them into their parts. He may be channelling impostors, faerie or Infernal; he has yet to win any god as a patron; and his Twilight Scars make him forget who he is while a god rides him. Proximios means to set Celaenea, who loves Hermes, against him, and to slip an infernalist into the league so that it calls up a False God.

neighbours.name: The League of the Vigilant
neighbours.summary:
A new league of demon hunters. Most magi know Infernal powers rode with both Latin and Greek armies when Constantinople fell, and many fear the Order is tainted too. Hydatius of Ingasia leads it, and Proximios of Alexandria pays for it and supplies it. It is still small, with no home or meeting place; the founders want magi from outside the Tribunal, fresh eyes to spot the rot, and keep the other members' names secret while they court help openly themselves. Knowing Hermetic magic cannot find a demon, they rely on patient watching for a slip.

The Tribunal tolerates it as it does every league, but doubts it will work; the cautious recall how witch hunts grow, while others think it needed. The founders' fine names keep its critics quiet.

details.rules: Members other than the two founders are kept secret
details.wants: To find any demon's servant hidden in the Order

neighbours.secrets: Proximios is an infernalist and founded the league as the first move of his plan to bring the Order down, starting in Thebes. He will steer it against innocents who look guilty (Caterina da Vigonovo of Polyaigos, the young magi of Erebos, and inquisitive Delfini of Aegaea), never leading in person: a demon wearing Hydatius's face will give the order to strike. As he gains ground he will use the league ever more openly as his shock troops. See the story An Enemy Within.

neighbours.name: The League Against Idolatry
neighbours.summary: Magi who would strip the last pagan rites out of the Order's customs, working mainly through the Legislative Board. In 1220 it is the magi of Oikos tou Eleous and Gigas, with fitful, lukewarm help from Artoud of Xylinites. Its target now is the Ceremony of Propitiation: the altars kept and the vis offered to patrons on Delos in Tribunal years go, it says, past the honour due to a being (proskynesis timetike) into worship (latreia), a mortal sin that brings God's anger on all who take part and on their sodales. The rite is ancient, the quarrel bitter and still unsettled.

details.wants: An end to the Ceremony of Propitiation and to the Tribunal's recognition of patrons

neighbours.name: The New Iconophiles
neighbours.summary: Valnastium's league within House Jerbiton, heirs in spirit of the old League of Iconophiles from which the House grew (see Houses of Hermes: Societates). In Thebes its member is Syagricus of Moero's Garden, who goes to Constantinople at least once a year hunting the covenant's lost works of art.

details.wants: The holy art scattered by the sack of 1204 found and saved

neighbours.name: The Seekers of the Fallen
neighbours.summary:
A loose handful of magi who think the titans, made by God before man as governors of time and nature, will bring back a golden age of magic if they are freed. To them Eden was the Magic Realm, and Adam and Eve carried shards of it out into the world, which survive as auras; so they pore over Magic auras, regiones and gates into the Magic Realm. They have repaired the lion arch at Dodona, and hunt the lost Julian Library.

The name was Lucian's, coined in a sneering speech four Tribunals ago that mocked all three factions of titan scholars; it stuck, and the younger members now use it themselves. None of the three is yet a formal league.
neighbours.ruler: Evantia of Moero's Garden, most respected

details.wants: The titans restored, and with them a new age of magic

neighbours.name: The Legion of Atlas
neighbours.summary:
Perhaps the most radical faction in Thebes: where the Seekers would save what is left of the Magic Realm, the Atlasians would raise it again by bringing down the faerie gods, after Atlas, who led the titans' war once the gods drowned Atlantis. It is perilous work: the gods are strong, and the Oath forbids molesting the fae. Kristophoros of Bonisagus speaks for them, from his own hatred of idolatry.

The name was Lucian's, coined in a sneering speech four Tribunals ago that mocked all three factions of titan scholars; it stuck, and the younger members now use it themselves. None of the three is yet a formal league.
neighbours.ruler: Kristophoros of Bonisagus, its rallying point

details.wants: The faerie gods undermined and the Magic Realm built anew

neighbours.name: Kampe's Lovers
neighbours.summary:
Magi who draw on the titans' power though the titans lie chained: some say all magic reaches men through them, and that Hermes first learned to tap it without loosening the chains. They want a closer bond with the Magic Realm's primal spirits, not the gods' fall, and are named for Kampe, the she-dragon who keeps Tartaros and has been the living chain of the gods since Zeus killed her. The faction draws Tytalus magi, for its aims echo the Titanoi's (Houses of Hermes: Societates); Tisiphon of Hedyosmos is its best-known member, and the threskeia geine of Hedyosmos is its heart.

The name was Lucian's, coined in a sneering speech four Tribunals ago that mocked all three factions of titan scholars; it stuck, and the younger members now use it themselves. None of the three is yet a formal league.

details.wants: A closer bond with the imprisoned titans, and Hades' hold on their prison loosened

neighbours.secrets: The binding magics of old (the epanankoi) are almost forgotten; some think Kampe's power fed them. Some ancient bindings still hold, and magi fear they could not mend one: the defeated giants buried under mountains and islands, the monsters of the Persian Wars sealed in objects, the oaths beneath the old leagues, and the rumoured Jar of Pandora. Delos's binding to the sea floor has already failed.

neighbours.name: The Witches of Thessaly
neighbours.summary: The old stygian witches of the mainland (Realms of Power: The Infernal), perhaps Trianoma's own native tradition. Those who joined the Order lead Erebos, whose head has always been one of them, of Cyra's line; others still work their binding magic outside it and quarrel with Erebos over land and vis. Binding is called the 'Stygian Art' in Thebes and is widely thought suspect, even Infernal, since goetia leads the field; Polydegmon of Hedyosmos practises a binding tradition of his own, unique until he trains an heir. Greek wizards of old hired the Witches to bind the monsters of the Persian Wars.

details.wants: Their mainland grounds and vis kept from rivals

links.note: A Witch of Thessaly, leader of Erebos

neighbours.secrets: Mainland magi call the slander rites (diabolai) witchcraft. Anyone with the right Lore and a personal tie to a being that has taken a place or a matter under its care (a village's nymph, an old shrine's god, Asklepios for a physician, a mythic forebear) can shame it into using one of its powers on a chosen target, by burning or soaking its effigy or reversing its rites: Presence + Realm Lore + modifiers + stress die against 9 + Might/5. Failure angers it for a month; a bad failure turns its power on the caller.

neighbours.name: The Daughters of Erictho
neighbours.summary: Witches of Thessaly who refused the Order and hide in the Cambunian mountains, Erebos's nearest enemies (Realms of Power: The Infernal). Some folk-witch covens have joined them, usually with the Infernal witches in charge, which is why folk witches have so bad a name in the empire.

details.wants: Erebos ruined and their mountains to themselves

neighbours.name: The Folk Witches of Hekate
neighbours.summary:
Folk witches (Hedge Magic) of the mainland rather than the isles, many of them secret worshippers of Hekate, titaness of witchcraft, who claim an unbroken line from classical times. Some covens have allied with the Strigae or the Daughters of Erictho, mostly to their cost. The nightwalkers oppose such covens.

Greek peasants also know the Folk Magic Virtue: scraps of ceremony for warding, divining, healing or the evil eye, cast through a Realm Lore at a Fatigue level each. Magi mostly think it beneath notice.

neighbours.name: The Nightwalkers
neighbours.summary: Remnants of an ancient Greek nightwalking cult (Hedge Magic), in pockets across the empire, often cunning folk as well. They fight folk-witch covens, above all those allied to Infernal witches, and are the sworn foes of the stringles. Light-shadowed ones (alaphroiskiotoi, born on a Saturday, most with Second Sight and all with power over the vrykolakes) who sleepwalk, the parmenoi, may go with them to their night battles or be nightwalkers themselves.

details.wants: The fields and children kept safe from witches

neighbours.name: The Cunning Folk
neighbours.summary: The learned magicians' rural kin (Hedge Magic), as common in the countryside as the folk witches, who deal with the faeries and nymphs of their place to guard their villages. Mathematici are rare, for Byzantium has no universities, and those there are mostly came with the Venetians. Alchemists flourish in Constantinople, heirs of a great body of learning, generously paid before the fall for their work on Greek Fire and other arms.

details.offers: Protection for their villages, through the local nymphs and faeries

neighbours.name: The Apostles of Apollonius
neighbours.summary: Elementalists (Hedge Magic) devoted to Apollonius of Tyana, scattered through the Greek islands and Asia Minor and in touch with their Arab fellows to the south and east. Command of water and wind is worth much to sea peoples, and merchants sometimes hire them for a safe voyage.

details.offers: Fair winds and calm seas, for hire

neighbours.name: The Makhai
neighbours.summary: Rumoured sorcerers who serve Ekhidna and Typhon, the monsters Earth bore to avenge the titans on the faerie gods; a Greek kin of the Muspelli (Rival Magic). The storyguide may fold them into the Pelasgian wizards below, or use them in their place.

details.wants: Vengeance on the gods for the titans' prison

neighbours.secrets: A Greek version of the gruagachan could be drawn from the Pelasgians before the Hellenes: worshippers of the titans, descended from the serpent-tailed giants, with power over curses and blessings tied to what is allowed and forbidden, some goetic spirit magic in place of tattoos, and perhaps a store of Defixio Lore. Giant-blooded Greeks take Mythic Blood (Gigantes), usually with a Focus in strength or Terram and the Rebellious Flaw; Large, Snake Legs and needing to touch the ground are common. Magi also comb the islands for katadesmoi, the cursing tablets of Katadesmos (Defixio) Magic, which struck at any range and set conditional curses; it is why Leadworker turns up among hedge wizards, though among magi it is Tremere's secret.

neighbours.name: The Cult of Orpheus
neighbours.summary: A native Greek tradition now within Ex Miscellanea (Houses of Hermes: Societates), with power over the bonds between people. Members live at Erebos, and Zacharias tends the cult's holy grove of Orphykia on Lesbos. They take a keen interest in adelphopoiesis, the oath-bound brotherhood rite (a True Friend Virtue or Flaw and a Sympathetic Connection), which some Jerbiton magi have sworn, even with mundanes.

neighbours.name: The Pharmacopoieans
neighbours.summary: The herbalist tradition of Ex Miscellanea (Houses of Hermes: Societates), native to Greece; its members live at Erebos, and Galla of Epidauros was trained in it.

neighbours.name: The Stringles
neighbours.summary: Witches of the Byzantine lands (an Infernal tradition like the Strigae) who look like any other woman, save that in time their wrists and ankles twist, so the old ones hide them; many a husband has found after years that his wife, and usually her mother, is one. They meet in covens of thirteen in rocky clefts and echoing gorges. Mykonos is said to swarm with them, and some small islands are full of their covens; Polyaigos was a nest of them until Laskaris cleared it.

details.rules: Covens of thirteen; each witch takes the Infernal Blessing on joining
details.wants: The Church's power and men's rule over women broken

neighbours.secrets: Each coven has a bodiless demon, a Watcher of the Deluders, who speaks to them as a voice and teaches maleficia. A new witch takes the Infernal Blessing, and her coven's leader can give her one more power: flight on gathered winds, healing herself with another's blood, or a breath that blights crops. Witches elsewhere can call a Mykonian stringles demon for a yearly tithe of one infant.

neighbours.name: The Cult of Heroes
neighbours.summary: House Mercere's Mystery cult of the heroes, many of whose members claim descent from a champion of the mythic age; it keeps a close eye on Greece, where the heroes' tales are still told and some heroes, in faerie form or the real thing, may still walk. Akhilles' blood brings Greater Immunity to metal and Fury; Bellerophon's, power over wild beasts and Pride; Kastor's or Polydeukes', a twin's haunting; Daidalos's, invention and Touched by Faerie; Helen's, unearthly beauty and the Curse of Venus; Odysseus's, seamanship and a supernatural plague; Perseus's, one of his gifts' powers working through a fit tool; Theseus's, warcraft and a Code of Honour.

neighbours.name: The Hesychasts
neighbours.summary:
Orthodox mystics who repeat the Jesus Prayer without end and hold perfectly still for hours, with special breathing, drawing the mind down into the heart in search of God; they shun ecstasies and visions as dangerous counterfeits. The practice is as old as the Desert Fathers and known from St John of Sinai's Ladder of Divine Ascent, still disputed, and spreading: besides the hermits who live apart, a newer movement brings it into the monasteries' daily offices, above all on Mount Athos.

As a holy tradition (Realms of Power: The Divine), the ascetics favour Meditation, Purity, Transcendence and Understanding, the monastics Ceremony, Meditation, Transcendence and Understanding; all are prone to the Divine Gloom from their first ascent.

details.rules: Only monks, perhaps some nuns; no Latins

neighbours.name: The Society of Cyprian and Justina
neighbours.summary:
A small, devout holy society (favoured Abilities Holy Magic, Invocation, Sense Holy and Unholy, and Wonders) under the patron saints of repentant magicians: Cyprian, the third-century wonder-worker of Antioch whose demons fled from the Christian Justina when he was paid to win her for a suitor, so that he burned his books and became a priest, and she a deaconess, both later martyred. Holy Magic is found among magi too, mostly Jerbiton, with Sol Invictus societies and Jewish Kabbalists, Baal Shem and Karaites.

Showy magic is deadly in Greek towns: the mob may kill an amulet-wearer or a suspected sorcerer before the Church, whose laws are mild, can try him. Jerbiton magi pass as natural philosophers if they keep their spells quiet, and the Gentle Gift is precious here.

details.wants: The enemies of God fought with prayer and miracle

neighbours.name: The Paulicians
neighbours.summary: A heretic sect of the great cities, above all Constantinople, Philippopolis and Thessaloniki, free to worship since 990 and left alone by the Orthodox Church. Its Manichaean creed sets Satan and God at endless war and its folk alone as the chosen; outwardly austere and devout, it seems harmless. The holy magae of Oikos tou Eleous preach and argue against it, and most people take them for bigots.

details.rules: Only the inner circle knows the creed is Infernal
details.wants: Rebel armies, as in the ninth century; for now, harm to Christians and Jews

neighbours.secrets: The sect is an Infernal tradition (favoured Abilities Ceremony, Debauchery, Diablerie and Malediction). Holding the world to be Satan's, its leaders hate Church and synagogue alike, slander and denounce both, and strike at them with Infernal powers when they can; a diabolist ring tied to it worked in Thessaloniki after 1185. Its communities grow, but cannot yet raise an army.

neighbours.name: The Cult of Eleusis
neighbours.summary: Greece's foremost Mystery of old, still kept by a dwindling secret few at Eleusis near Athens: initiates lose their fear of death and, in its Christian dress, grow sure of Heaven, though the Church calls it heresy. Candidates gather in the Athenian agora and walk the Sacred Way through Daphni, whose monks long favoured the cult until the Cistercians took the house in 1205. At Eleusis they drink the kykeon and Hekate seems to meet them, choosing the epoptai who go on; the Lesser Mystery is held each March, the Greater every fifth year in late August. (Eleusis itself is in Greece.)

details.rules: A sponsor; no barbarians, blood-guilty or harlots; secrecy on pain of death
details.offers: Freedom from the fear of death (the Lesser Mystery, Self-Confident); for some, Death Prophecy (the Greater)

neighbours.name: An Enemy Within
neighbours.summary:
Most magi know that demons marched with both armies when Constantinople fell, and many fear the Order caught the same rot. Hydatius of Ingasia and Proximios of Alexandria have answered by founding the League of the Vigilant: Hydatius is its general, Proximios its paymaster and quartermaster. They want recruits from outside the Tribunal, fresh eyes to find what is foul, and they keep every other member's name secret. Since Hermetic magic cannot reveal a demon, the league watches its sodales and waits for one to give himself away.

The Tribunal accepts the league as it accepts any, though its quieter magi remember how hunts for witches grow beyond anyone's control; the two founders' good names silence most critics. Proximios, the Redcap whose idea it was to make the logothete's post permanent, is the Redcaps' choice to follow Leontius in 1221. He neither seeks the post nor refuses it, and most magi call that humility.

A saga frame as well as a threat, and the book's own choice for a saga's chief enemy. Let it build over years: at full strength it would overwhelm young magi before the saga had found its feet.

details.antagonist: Proximios of House Mercere, a Redcap secretly in league with Hell

stages.title: The Vigilant recruit
stages.clues: Through 1220 Hydatius and Proximios sound out magi new to the Tribunal: Frankish incomers, metoikoi, the newly Gauntleted. A recruit is asked to keep an eye on a sodalis and report anything strange. Proximios supplies vis and equipment but never leads anyone in person.
stages.ignored: The league grows unseen, its members strangers to one another, and becomes Proximios's tool.
stages.stopped: The troupe declines to join, or learns who the members are and makes the league's methods known before it acts.
stages.turned: Player magi join and watch the league from within, where in time they may notice that not every order really comes from Hydatius.

stages.title: The new logothete
stages.clues: On Delos in 1221 Leontius steps down and the Redcaps put Proximios forward. He accepts with every sign of unwillingness, and takes charge of the register of tokens and shards and of where every Redcap is sent.
stages.ignored: The Tribunal's records, messengers and letters are all in his hands.
stages.stopped: Another Redcap is chosen, or a later vote of no confidence among the Redcaps removes him.
stages.turned: The troupe backs him and finds its tally of tokens kindly kept, at the price of owing him.

stages.title: False accusations
stages.clues: League members are sent to look into three suspects: Caterina da Vigonovo of Polyaigos, a Venetian newcomer; the young magi of Erebos, whose witchcraft looks sinister; and Delfini of Aegaea, whose questions are taken for prying. In the field, a demon in Hydatius's shape tells them to strike.
stages.ignored: Innocent magi are attacked, or charged with diabolism before the Judicial Board, and their accusers are rewarded with tokens.
stages.stopped: The troupe proves the accused innocent, or exposes the false Hydatius.
stages.turned: Clearing one of the accused earns lasting gratitude, and the first real hint that someone is steering the league.

stages.title: Hedyosmos turned on Gigas
stages.clues: Hints reach Aiakia that the Tremere of Gigas had a hand in Constantinople's fall and mean to strike at Hedyosmos next; Boustaphan will never let her read Gigas's records. Tisiphon, easier to lead, is told the Tremere slipped past the justice they deserved.
stages.ignored: Aiakia moves against Gigas and the volatile Tisiphon declares Wizard's Wars, waking the old enmity of the Sundering.
stages.stopped: Someone shows the evidence to be forged before blood is spilled.
stages.turned: The troupe arranges an exchange of records or oaths, and wins the trust of both covenants.

stages.title: Celaenea set against Lucian
stages.clues: Celaenea of Hedyosmos, whose love of Hermes borders on obsession, hears from a well-wisher that Lucian of Aegaea means to raise the forgotten gods. Meanwhile Proximios hunts for an infernalist to slip into the Children of Olympos.
stages.ignored: Celaenea turns on Lucian and his league; if Proximios places his man, the god they summon and bind is a False God (see Lucian's Pacts).
stages.stopped: Celaenea and Lucian compare what they were told and see that a third hand set them at odds.
stages.turned: The trail of whispers leads back to the logothete himself, and the troupe holds the proof.

links.note: Its young magi to be accused

neighbours.secrets:
Proximios is an infernalist. He has mastered the Unholy Method of Incantation and the Unholy Power of Diablerie and holds a long list of demons' True Names; the Tempters and Evil Spirits he calls up spy for him, bait his traps and urge his sodales into sin. He wants the whole Order brought low, beginning with Thebes, and works slowly and covertly because the Tribunal is full of magi who would spot a clumsy Infernal plot. The letters that pass through Alexandria show him where each covenant is weak.

He set Hydatius at the league's head so that its mistakes would be someone else's. He will steer it toward magi who look like diabolists and are not, send its members out to investigate without going himself, and once they are in the field a demon wearing Hydatius's face will order the attack. Other infernalists have told him that an infernalist planted among Lucian's Children of Olympos would probably raise a False God for them to bind instead of a faerie; finding such a magus is the hard part.

In 1220 all this is still taking shape in his mind. He will take the logothete's post, making a show of reluctance so that no blame sticks to him when his plans come apart, and as keeper of the register of tokens and shards he can favour those who help him. He has no Hermetic accomplices yet, but has noted a few magi he thinks could be tempted. Each scheme is built to look like another's work; as he gains ground he will use the Vigilant more openly, as shock troops for a Tribunal remade to suit him.

neighbours.name: The Tribunal of 1221
neighbours.summary:
A saga frame. The Tribunal meets on Delos in 1221, seven years after the last meeting; the book names no season, and Summer is assumed. Its business runs in fixed order: the phylai's candidate dinners and two days of apprentice interviews, then the four phases (Hermetic Assembly, Law Council, People's Court, Council of Archai), and last the Rite of Dismissal and the Ceremony of Propitiation at the sacred lake. Which phyle is principal this time is left to the storyguide. Aiakia of Hedyosmos presides as archon.

Sixteen years after the fall of Constantinople, Frankish magi who have settled in Thebes mean to change its ways, and Gigas campaigns for Latin over Greek. Cases that might reach the People's Court include Formosos's charge that Passara serves the Latin emperor, and the riddle of the mysterious knight who saved the Nicene emperor in 1211.

stages.title: Pancratius's Gauntlet
stages.clues: Syagricus's apprentice Pancratius hopes to pass his Gauntlet at the meeting and join Moero's Garden. Trasaric and Helladius count on his voice to commit the covenant to the Nicene emperor's cause.
stages.ignored: He becomes a full member and the covenant leans toward the League of Constantine.
stages.stopped: His Gauntlet is delayed, and the covenant stays split.
stages.turned: The troupe befriends the new magus, a polites from his first day.

stages.title: Caterina's citizenship
stages.clues: In the Hermetic Assembly Caterina da Vigonovo of Polyaigos, a metoikos, may seek a decree of citizenship: without it she can earn no tokens, and without tokens the Tribunal will never sponsor the Longevity Ritual her waning vigour now demands. She needs evidence of service to the polity, a home at an established covenant (she has one) and an arche to sponsor her. Many Jerbiton magi distrust her as a Venetian.
stages.ignored: No arche will sponsor her, and she looks for a ritual elsewhere, perhaps through her dealings with the Duke of Naxos.
stages.stopped: The Assembly votes the decree down.
stages.turned: An arche of the troupe sponsors her, and she becomes a polites in its debt.

stages.title: Nanno and Ampelius
stages.clues: Ziper of Moero's Garden wants two of the covenant's craftsmen admitted to House Jerbiton: Nanno, who makes wondrous cosmetics, and the painter Ampelius, whose murals carry small enchantments. Neither has the Gift. Proximios supports the idea, pointing to his own House of unGifted members. The rest of the covenant, Syagricus apart, is appalled, less at the missing Gift than at the thought of artisans as sodales. The pair threaten to sail to Delos and put their case to the whole Tribunal.
stages.ignored: The petition embarrasses Moero's Garden in public, whichever way it goes.
stages.stopped: The craftsmen are talked out of it, or the Assembly refuses.
stages.turned: The troupe finds them a place that keeps everyone's dignity, and wins two grateful artisans.

stages.title: The petition against the Propitiation
stages.clues: Before the Law Council the League Against Idolatry, the magae of Oikos tou Eleous and the magi of Gigas with lukewarm help from Artoud of Xylinites, asks that the Ceremony of Propitiation be banned as worship of false gods. The Legislative Board demands an alternative ruling, and two archai are drawn by lot to argue for and against. Kristophoros of Bonisagus may lend his tongue to the petitioners.
stages.ignored: The ceremony goes on as ever, and the quarrel grows angrier.
stages.stopped: The petition is defeated and the rite stands.
stages.turned: A new ruling draws the line between veneration and worship in words both sides can accept.

stages.title: The logothete
stages.clues: Leontius, who escaped ostracism by a whisker in 1214 after records went missing and the register of tokens and shards was found faulty, resigns. The post falls vacant for the first time since it was made permanent, and the Redcaps propose Proximios.
stages.ignored: Proximios becomes logothete (An Enemy Within).
stages.stopped: Another Redcap is chosen.
stages.turned: The troupe puts the faulty register right before it changes hands, and learns whose tallies were wrong.

stages.title: The sortition
stages.clues: In the Council of Archai the outgoing archai are thanked and paid two tokens each; Maria Laskarina, polemarch since 1207, takes five and Aiakia three. Each phyle's Redcap reads out its candidates, starting with the principal phyle, and the logothete draws four names from the jar for each. The sixteen new archai choose an archon, then a polemarch, most likely Maria once more.
stages.ignored: The lot falls where it falls.
stages.stopped: A polites refuses candidacy, and takes a shard for it.
stages.turned: A player magus is drawn as an arche, and the troupe has a seat on a board for seven years.

neighbours.secrets: The logothete's election is the second stage of An Enemy Within. Gemma and Bobila of Ingasia have quietly sold Nicaea more enchanted items than the Code's five a year allow; if that comes out, Ingasia's neutrality is in question.

neighbours.name: Epiros against Thessaloniki
neighbours.summary:
Theodore Komnenos Doukas, who rules Epiros from Arta, is carving up the Kingdom of Thessaloniki. He has taken most of Thessaly, Ohrid and Pelagonia, and in 1217 captured the Latin emperor Peter on the Via Egnatia, who has not been seen since. His army is largely Frankish mercenaries; King Demetrios, fifteen years old, defends his Frankish kingdom with a largely Greek one, and the fighting is heavy and constant. Count Oberto of Biandrate still works for the claim of William of Montferrat, and the new Latin emperor, Robert, will not reach Constantinople before 1221. Few think the city can hold much longer.

Thessaloniki's patron, Saint Demetrios, has risen to save his city before, most recently against Tsar Kaloyan in 1207, but only when its cause is just. The magae of Oikos tou Eleous are sworn to the young king's protection and to the city's survival, which may draw them over the line into mundane affairs. Erebos's valley already lies in Epirote Thessaly, and the Frankish covenant of Novocastrum died resisting Epiros in 1212.

details.antagonist: Theodore Komnenos Doukas, ruler of Epiros

stages.title: The noose tightens
stages.clues: Epirote columns close on Thessaloniki from the north and the west. Refugees crowd the roads; Frankish lords weigh which side will leave them their estates.
stages.ignored: Town after town of the kingdom goes over to Epiros.
stages.stopped: The kingdom finds allies, or the new emperor sends help in time.
stages.turned: A covenant that shelters refugees or a threatened monastery is owed by whoever wins.

stages.title: Serres and the hinterland
stages.clues: If history holds, Theodore takes Serres and most of the kingdom's remaining towns, and the city is left almost alone behind its walls.
stages.ignored: Thessaloniki is cut off by land.
stages.stopped: The Epirote advance stalls before the city's hinterland.
stages.turned: The troupe profits from the shifting borders: a vis site or a road that no lord now watches.

stages.title: The king looks west
stages.clues: If history holds, Demetrios leaves for Italy to plead for help from the pope and the western emperor, and his regents hold the city in his name.
stages.ignored: Help is promised from the west but comes slowly, if at all.
stages.stopped: The king stays, and the city rallies around him.
stages.turned: Oikos tou Eleous, or the troupe, finds the king friends abroad, at the risk of a charge of interference.

stages.title: The fall of Thessaloniki
stages.clues: If history holds, the city yields to Theodore after a long siege, and the Latin kingdom of Thessaloniki ends. Whether Saint Demetrios rises depends on whose cause is just.
stages.ignored: Epiros holds the empire's second city, and Oikos tou Eleous lives under a new and harsh lord.
stages.stopped: The saint, a relief army or the city's own stubbornness keeps Theodore out.
stages.turned: The covenant eases the surrender, sparing the city a sack like 1185, and is remembered by its people.

stages.title: An emperor at Thessaloniki
stages.clues: If history holds, Theodore has himself crowned emperor at Thessaloniki, a rival to Nicaea in the race for Constantinople.
stages.ignored: Two Greek emperors now claim the Queen of Cities, and the successor states turn on each other.
stages.stopped: The crowning is delayed or denied by the churchmen.
stages.turned: The troupe's friends at court shape what the new emperor wants from the magi, and from the Church.

neighbours.secrets: The book tells the war only to 1220. The later stages follow history in broad strokes; a troupe whose saga takes another road changes them.

neighbours.name: Nicaea against the Latins
neighbours.summary:
Theodore Laskaris, who fled Constantinople in 1204 and was crowned emperor at Nicaea in 1208, has sworn to win the city back. His peace with the Latins, sealed in 1219 by his marriage to a niece of Emperor Henry, has broken: in 1220 the two empires are at war again. Many of the Latin knights who held the Troad are away fighting the Bulgarians, and Theodore has gathered his forces to take Holkos on the Hellespont as a second naval base against Venetian shipping. Bithynia's coastal castles, which have changed hands many times, wait to see who comes next.

Theodore is also ready to put the Eastern Church under Rome for a while if it buys him the city, and has called churchmen together to end the schism. A small Nicene garrison, sent to guard Smyrna against the Turks, has taken over Alexandria's ruined citadel and shut the covenfolk out, knowing nothing of the regiones within. At Moero's Garden, members of the League of Constantine want the covenant to back the emperor.

details.antagonist: Theodore I Laskaris, Emperor of Nicaea

stages.title: The landing at Holkos
stages.clues: Troops mass along the Bithynian border, and a Nicene fleet gathers. The army crosses into the Troad and falls on Holkos while its Latin lords are away.
stages.ignored: Holkos falls and the Nicene navy has a base on the Straits.
stages.stopped: The Latins return in time and the attack fails.
stages.turned: The covenant helps one side through a crossing or a siege, and must hope the Tribunal never hears of it.

stages.title: The council of union
stages.clues: Bishops and papal envoys argue at Nicaea over the Holy Spirit's procession, leavened bread and the pope's primacy. The patriarch and the Anatolian sees must be won over.
stages.ignored: The talks founder, as such talks always have.
stages.stopped: The bishops reject union outright.
stages.turned: A covenant with friends among the clergy learns which churchmen can be moved, and why.

stages.title: The Latins sue for peace
stages.clues: Pressed from the north and leaderless until Robert of Courtenay arrives, the Latin regency asks for terms.
stages.ignored: Nicaea keeps its gains, and the Latin empire shrinks toward its capital.
stages.stopped: The war drags on without a peace.
stages.turned: The peace talks need go-betweens, and magi with the Gentle Gift are in demand.

stages.title: A new emperor at Nicaea
stages.clues: If history holds, Theodore dies and his son-in-law John Doukas Vatatzes takes the throne. Theodore's brothers, passed over, flee to the Latins and bring the war back.
stages.ignored: The succession is fought over in the field.
stages.stopped: The brothers are reconciled and the peace holds.
stages.turned: The covenant earns the new emperor's goodwill, and the Tribunal's watchful eye.

stages.title: Poimanenon
stages.clues: If history holds, John beats the Latin army at Poimanenon and takes almost all their lands in Asia; the Latin empire is left with little beyond the city.
stages.ignored: Nicaea becomes the strongest of the Greek states, and the League of Constantine's hopes rise.
stages.stopped: The Latins hold their Anatolian lands.
stages.turned: The covenant gains land, rights or a vis site on the new border.

links.note: A Nicene garrison in its citadel

neighbours.secrets: The book calls him Theodore II; history has Theodore I Laskaris. It says the invasion succeeded and the Latins, harried from the north, sued for peace in 1221. The later stages follow history in broad strokes.

neighbours.name: Akgah's War
neighbours.summary: The magi of Thebes know that the Infernal had a hand in the Fourth Crusade, though not whose: demons stood behind Andronikos Komnenos's massacre of the Latins in 1182, behind the sack of Zara and the crusaders' excommunication, and in the hordes that came over the walls in 1204. Since then the successor states have fought one another without pause.

details.antagonist: Akgah, the demon of the Fourth Crusade

stages.title: Treaties broken
stages.clues: Envoys are murdered on the road, a truce breaks over a petty slight, and each court blames the other's treachery.
stages.ignored: The successor states bleed one another white.
stages.stopped: The troupe shows a broken treaty to be the work of a third hand.
stages.turned: Both courts owe the covenant for keeping a peace.

stages.title: The lion's visions
stages.clues: Soldiers of one army or another see a winged beast in the sky before battle and fight like madmen; the plunder afterwards is savage.
stages.ignored: Infernal auras spread across the battlefields of Thrace and Bithynia.
stages.stopped: The visions are exposed as the demon's work.
stages.turned: The troupe learns the beast's true name, and the way to its lair.

stages.title: The blasted field
stages.clues: Searchers for the relics lost in 1204 trace some to a regio outside the city, where the stench of corpses carries for miles.
stages.ignored: Akgah grows mightier, and its war spreads to the Order's covenants.
stages.stopped: Akgah is driven from its lair, perhaps with the Hagka's help, and the relics are recovered.
stages.turned: Recovered relics win the Church's gratitude and some holy power for the covenant.

neighbours.secrets:
It was the design of Akgah, a prince of Hell with an Infernal Might of 50 and the Hagka's enemy and mirror: a two-headed winged leopard the size of an elephant, a mockery of the lion of Venice, gold and black with golden wings and a sweet smell, whose company fills men with greed, lust and battle-madness (see the Bestiary). In 1204 it fought the Hagka in the Hippodrome, wrecking part of the arena, and drove it off wounded; crusaders who saw it thought they had seen Venice's lion triumph by God's will.

Its success has raised it high among the princes of Hell. Now it keeps the old empire's heirs at war and feeds their distrust and greed. Its lair lies about a dozen miles outside Constantinople, an Infernal regio like a ruined battlefield, where it gorges on heaps of corpses among looted treasure and defiled relics, with hundreds of bodies hung on pikes around it.

neighbours.name: Lucian's Pacts
neighbours.summary:
The Children of Olympos, a small and eccentric league led by Lucian the Scholar of Aegaea, want the old Greek gods as the covenants' patrons. Lucian argues that the Divine and the Infernal have used the Order badly, that Magic's creatures care nothing for men, and that the gods, faeries who live on the hearts of men, have outlasted every rival. Its members are mostly Merinita; it has sympathisers, and few members.

Lucian believes stories feed the power of Faerie, and that the old myths must be lived, not just retold. He has cast many of the Tribunal's magi and covenants in parts of his great reenactment and nudges them toward their roles, which explains the sudden turns in his politics that others take for treachery. Lucian and his league prize the Great Altar at Pergamos, which powers rituals without vis.

details.antagonist: Lucian the Scholar and the gods he channels

stages.title: A part in the story
stages.clues: Lucian suddenly backs the troupe at Tribunal, or turns against it, and greets a player magus by the name of a hero from myth.
stages.ignored: The covenant is steered, unknowing, toward the fate of its part.
stages.stopped: The troupe sees through the casting and refuses it.
stages.turned: The troupe plays its part well, and Lucian's favour follows.

stages.title: Twelve boons
stages.clues: An initiate travels the Tribunal asking boons of twelve mighty beings, each standing for one Olympian; a player magus or the covenant's patron may be one of them.
stages.ignored: The league gains another initiate.
stages.stopped: The troupe refuses the boon, and the initiation fails.
stages.turned: The troupe learns the Mystery's script, and may seek initiation itself.

stages.title: A god for a patron
stages.clues: A channelled god agrees to become a covenant's patron; the covenant's Magic aura begins to take on a faerie glamour.
stages.ignored: Faerie spreads through the covenants, and the Propitiation becomes worship in earnest.
stages.stopped: The pact is broken before the god takes hold.
stages.turned: The covenant gains a mighty patron on terms it can live with.

stages.title: A False God
stages.clues: The god that answers the league is colder and hungrier than the myths, and its initiates' sins grow.
stages.ignored: A demon sits on a covenant's plinth at Delos, fed with vis at every Propitiation.
stages.stopped: The deceiver is unmasked and banished, and the infernalist among the initiates exposed.
stages.turned: The trail leads the troupe to Proximios.

neighbours.secrets:
Lucian has devised two Mysteries, Elysian Ecstasy and the Olympian Pact, by which a person channels a god who possesses him; in the end the god may overwhelm the channeller and walk the earth in his body. He has initiated every member who knows the first, and holds the only Olympian Pact himself. Beneath his plan lies a hope he does not voice: that Faerie auras will replace the Magic ones of most covenants, and the old worship return.

He thinks he channels the gods themselves, but they may be pretenders, faerie or Infernal; his Twilight Scars make him forget who he is when a god rides him. No channelled god has yet agreed to be a patron. Proximios knows of the plan and wants an infernalist among the initiates, so that what the league binds is a False God (An Enemy Within).

neighbours.name: Kampe's Lovers and the Titans
neighbours.summary:
Three loose factions study the imprisoned titans, all named in mockery by Lucian four Tribunals ago: the Seekers of the Fallen, who would restore them to usher in a new age of magic (Evantia of Moero's Garden is their most respected member); the Legion of Atlas around Kristophoros of Bonisagus, who would bring down the faerie gods; and Kampe's Lovers, named for the she-dragon who keeps the gates of Tartaros, who draw on the titans' power and want a closer bond with them. Tisiphon of Hedyosmos, a Tytalan Quaesitor of the Titanoi, is the best known of these.

Hedyosmos sits over a gate to the Underworld guarded by its patron, the nymph Minthe, and the Terram aura of the labyrinth beneath it strengthens the deeper one goes. Rumour has always tied the covenant to the Sundering of 848, when Typhon is said to have been loosed on Dorostolon and then bound again.

details.antagonist: The threskeia geine of Hedyosmos and Kampe's Lovers

stages.title: Deeper in the labyrinth
stages.clues: Earth elementals wander up from the lower passages of Hedyosmos, the ground shakes in Elis, and the covenant's grogs are forbidden levels they used to patrol.
stages.ignored: The cult's work below goes on unseen.
stages.stopped: The Tribunal learns of the cult's aim and the Judicial Board takes an interest.
stages.turned: The troupe trades help for a share of the cult's Terram lore.

stages.title: A binding fails
stages.clues: One of the giants buried under a mountain or an island stirs; Nicomedia's century of quiet ends early; the Legion of Atlas and the Seekers both rush to the spot.
stages.ignored: A titan's child walks free, and the land suffers.
stages.stopped: The binding is renewed, at great cost in vis.
stages.turned: The troupe learns a fragment of the lost epanankoi, the binding magic of the ancients.

stages.title: The gate of Tartaros
stages.clues: Minthe grows strange and distant; the aura at the bottom of the labyrinth rises past anything known.
stages.ignored: The gate opens, the titans' power floods into the world, and the gods, and every faerie patron, are shaken.
stages.stopped: The gate is sealed and the cult's leaders brought to account.
stages.turned: The troupe passes the gate into the Magic Realm, and returns changed.

neighbours.secrets: In Thebes the threskeia geine of Hedyosmos is the heart of Kampe's Lovers: it has taken over Hades's old offices without honouring him, and quietly works to loosen his grip on the titans' prison, hoping to bring them back and begin a golden age of magic. Minthe's gate is the key to that plan. Since 1204 many ancient bindings across the Tribunal have failed, and no living magus could mend the greatest of them.

neighbours.name: Klymene's Prison
neighbours.summary: On the acropolis of Pergamos stands the Great Altar, its friezes showing the gods' war with the titans; Christians shun it as Satan's throne. It has a Faerie aura of 4, and any Hermetic ritual cast from its top needs no vis, though a botch is tainted as if with faerie vis and even a good casting can go oddly. The locals have driven magi off before, taking them for devil-worshippers, and with vis so plentiful few bother. Lucian's league is drawn to it.

stages.title: Rituals for nothing
stages.clues: Word spreads that rituals at Pergamos cost no vis; the Children of Olympos and thrifty magi come to cast them, and the townsfolk grow angry.
stages.ignored: The altar is used more each year.
stages.stopped: The Tribunal discourages its use.
stages.turned: The troupe learns what powers the altar, and can use it wisely or warn others.

stages.title: The altar cracks
stages.clues: After a year of heavy use, fissures run through the friezes and the altar hums at night.
stages.ignored: The altar splits and Klymene is released.
stages.stopped: The rituals stop in time and the bonds renew.
stages.turned: The troupe parleys with the waking titaness before she is free.

stages.title: Klymene unbound
stages.clues: A great presence settles on a mountaintop, or roams the Tribunal seeking her imprisoned sisters.
stages.ignored: She frees other titanesses, overturning the land and its people.
stages.stopped: She returns to the Magic Realm, leaving a ruined altar.
stages.turned: She becomes a mighty, unpredictable friend.

neighbours.secrets: The altar is the lock on the prison of Klymene, titaness of fame, a Kosmokrator Spirit of Magic Might 50 (see the Bestiary), one of the titanesses who stayed out of the war and was bound somewhere kinder than Tartaros. The free rituals draw on her. Her bonds have a strength of 50, renewed every year, and each ritual cast there wears them down by the pawns it would have cost; if they reach nothing within one year, the altar splits in two and she goes free. She thought her cell a mercy shared with her sisters, and freed she has nowhere to go.

neighbours.name: The Estate of Hades
neighbours.summary: Hedyosmos stands on the ruins of an oracle of the dead, once one of the few places where Hades was worshipped. Its magi honour the nymph Minthe, never the god.

details.antagonist: Askalaphos, the owl of Hades, and his priest Vrakos

stages.title: Offerings in the dark
stages.clues: Milk and honey go missing from the stores, a black ram is bought and never eaten, and a screech owl calls near the ruined oracle.
stages.ignored: The cult grows among the covenfolk.
stages.stopped: Vrakos is found out and the owl driven away.
stages.turned: The troupe turns the cook, and learns what Askalaphos wants.

stages.title: Within the Aegis
stages.clues: A servant of the cult asks to bring a bird into the covenant, or a token is slipped among the Aegis's ritual offerings.
stages.ignored: Askalaphos is invited within the Aegis.
stages.stopped: The Aegis is cast clean, and the faerie stays out.
stages.turned: The troupe sets a trap for the faerie at the ritual.

stages.title: The temple reclaimed
stages.clues: Lamps fail in the forbidden passages, covenfolk refuse orders, and the magi's sancta are tampered with.
stages.ignored: Hedyosmos's people rise for Hades, and the covenant must fight its own household.
stages.stopped: The cult is broken and its faerie patron banished.
stages.turned: A bargain with Hades's servant gives the covenant a new and dangerous ally below.

neighbours.secrets: Vrakos, the covenant's cook, beneath the magi's notice, has been won over by Askalaphos, a faerie servant of Hades whom Demeter cursed into a screech owl for betraying that Persephone ate the pomegranate seeds. Vrakos now holds secret rites in the covenant's depths as a priest of Hades, asks for milk, honey and the blood of a black ram, and is cautiously recruiting among the servants. Askalaphos means in time to take the covenant back as a temple of his lord and be rid of the magi. The Aegis of the Hearth bars him, and he is looking for a way to be invited into its ritual.

neighbours.name: The Tremere Appeal of 1228
neighbours.summary: The League of Advisors, Greek magi who after 1185 lived at the emperor's court and claimed they only advised, lost many members with Thermakopolis in 1204 and broke up under charges of meddling with mundanes. The Tribunal failed to convict its survivors. House Tremere, which Thebes has distrusted since the Sundering and which blames Theban magi for the empire's war on Bulgaria in 1014, has appealed to the Grand Tribunal of 1228 to try the two surviving members again.

stages.title: Lobbying on Delos
stages.clues: Allectores of Gigas courts magi at the meeting, and Gigas presses its case for the Order's common ways over Theban custom.
stages.ignored: The Tremere gather friends for the appeal.
stages.stopped: The Tribunal resolves to defend its verdict as one.
stages.turned: The troupe trades its support to Gigas for favours.

stages.title: Witnesses sought
stages.clues: Tremere agents search for anyone who saw the Advisors at court, and for letters from the fallen palace.
stages.ignored: The appeal arrives at the Grand Tribunal with new evidence.
stages.stopped: The witnesses are found first, or their tales discredited.
stages.turned: The troupe holds the evidence that decides the case.

stages.title: The Grand Tribunal
stages.clues: The Grand Tribunal hears the appeal; Theban magi who travel there earn a token for the service.
stages.ignored: The verdict is overturned, and Thebes's right to judge its own is in doubt.
stages.stopped: The appeal fails and the polity's verdict stands.
stages.turned: The troupe's advocacy wins a ruling that guards every Tribunal's independence.

neighbours.secrets: If the appeal succeeds, a Grand Tribunal will have overturned a Tribunal's own verdict, which bears on every Tribunal's independence and on the Theban polity most of all. Boustaphan of Gigas, Tremere's voice in Thebes, holds proxies from the House's younger magi.

neighbours.name: The Verditius Contest of 1234
neighbours.summary: Stouritus of Ingasia, newly primus of House Verditius, has chosen to stay on Lemnos rather than move to Verdi, which makes Ingasia the domus magna in all but name. Ingasia's magi say their forge, Hephaistos's own, is older than Verdi. Stouritus wants the next Contest, due in 1234, held there: he has plans drawn for grander buildings above ground and more laboratories below, Egyptian marble and Trebizond oak on order, and masons hired from the villages, and he has opened Ingasia to new Verditius members to show the Order a welcoming house beside a quarrelsome Verdi. The House is split between the two covenants' partisans.

details.antagonist: The rivalry of Verdi and Ingasia

stages.title: Death of an Artificer
stages.clues: Simon of Newmarket, a Verditius bound for Ingasia to discuss the Contest, is found hacked apart in a disused well in Constantinople's back streets. Each faction suspects the other; the characters may be suspects, archai or foreign Quaesitores.
stages.ignored: The House's quarrel turns murderous in rumour.
stages.stopped: The truth comes out: a frightened mob killed him for the runes on his brooch, his Gift and his open spellcasting, and no magus was to blame.
stages.turned: The troupe's finding calms the House, and both factions owe it.

stages.title: Building on Mosychlos
stages.clues: Shiploads of marble and oak arrive on Lemnos and gangs of workmen dig into the volcano's slopes, stirring its ill-tempered spirit.
stages.ignored: Mosychlos rumbles, tunnels collapse and lava creeps into the labyrinth.
stages.stopped: The work is scaled back to keep the patron calm.
stages.turned: The troupe helps shore up the works, and is welcome at the Contest.

stages.title: The Contest
stages.clues: The House decides where the Contest of 1234 will be held, and Verditius magi from across the Order look to Lemnos or to Verdi.
stages.ignored: The choice is made without the Tribunal's say.
stages.stopped: The Contest stays at Verdi, and Ingasia's pride is hurt.
stages.turned: The Contest comes to Thebes, and with it rare trade and a gathering of the Order's finest craftsmen.

neighbours.secrets: Ingasia's neutrality, and so its trade, would suffer if Gemma and Bobila's secret sales to Nicaea came out.

neighbours.name: Talos of Candia
neighbours.summary: Talos, the bronze bull-headed giant that Hephaistos made for King Minos, guards Candia again. Medea once drained the ichor from his single vein by pulling the nail in his ankle, and a local alchemist later brewed him new blood. Byzantine magicians bound him for centuries in a cellar of the ruined Labyrinth of Knossos, but the spell failed lately. He runs round the island three times a day, stones any hostile ship, and seizes landing parties in a red-hot grip (see the Bestiary).

details.antagonist: Talos, the bronze guardian of Candia

stages.title: Ships lost off Candia
stages.clues: Venetian galleys come home holed by boulders or not at all, and sailors tell of a bronze giant striding the shore.
stages.ignored: Candia's trade withers.
stages.stopped: Ships learn to keep clear, and Talos's war cools.
stages.turned: The troupe finds a way to pass his watch unharmed.

stages.title: The Venetian bounty
stages.clues: The duke of Candia's reward draws hunters, adventurers and at least one magus who sees seven pawns of Ignem walking the beaches.
stages.ignored: Talos is slain or captured, and his secrets are lost.
stages.stopped: The hunters fail, or are warned off by the Tribunal.
stages.turned: The troupe takes Talos alive, for study or as an ally, and must answer for it to the Venetians.

stages.title: A guardian for a covenant
stages.clues: Magi talk of founding a covenant on Candia with Talos as its patron.
stages.ignored: Another group founds it first.
stages.stopped: The bronze man refuses every pact.
stages.turned: The troupe's new covenant has the mightiest of guardians, and the Venetians as neighbours.
