neighbours.secrets: The Venetians who now rule Candia have put a fat price on the head of this demon, as they call him. House Verditius would give a great deal to learn how he was made, and he might serve a new covenant on Candia as its patron. His ichor holds 7 pawns of Ignem vis.

neighbours.name: The Duke of Naxos
neighbours.summary: Marco Sanudo, nephew of the doge Enrico Dandolo, took the Cyclades between 1207 and 1212 and rules them as Duke of Naxos, a vassal of the Latin emperor in name and a friend of Venice in fact. Polyaigos lies within his duchy, and he has heard tales of the riches behind its famous school and envies them. Caterina da Vigonovo, who runs the covenant's mines and trade, has met him in the guise of a wealthy noblewoman and begun to arrange a quiet understanding.

stages.title: The duke's envy
stages.clues: Ducal officers ask who works the mines of Sifnos, and a new tax falls on the goods Polyaigos buys on Melos.
stages.ignored: The duke presses harder for a share.
stages.stopped: The officers are put off with gifts and answers.
stages.turned: The troupe wins the duke as a trading partner.

stages.title: Caterina's arrangement
stages.clues: Caterina's dealings with the duke deepen; a rival at Tribunal wonders aloud whether a Venetian maga meddles in a Venetian lord's affairs.
stages.ignored: The arrangement holds until someone brings it before the Judicial Board.
stages.stopped: Caterina ends it before it becomes a crime.
stages.turned: The troupe shapes a deal the Code allows.

stages.title: A brother found
stages.clues: Satabus writes to the duke at last, or the duke's agents trace Pietro to the island of many goats.
stages.ignored: The duke has a brother inside the covenant, and the covenant a hostage to the duke's affection.
stages.stopped: Satabus keeps his secret.
stages.turned: The reunion makes the duke Polyaigos's friend, if the magi can keep it within the Code.

neighbours.secrets: Polyaigos's wealth comes from its quarry on Argentiera and from the old gold and silver mines of Sifnos, which it has reopened in secret. Satabus, the Verditius maga who has just joined Polyaigos from Ingasia, is the duke's younger brother Pietro, an odd and scholarly boy whom Dandolo placed somewhere before he died. Marco still wonders what became of him. Satabus knows of his brother's rise, still loves his family, and has not written.

neighbours.name: The Lost Hagka
neighbours.summary:
Three things stand for the emperor's God-given authority: his battle standard, his crown and the hagka, a bronze two-headed eagle on a long lance with an icon of the Virgin hung from it. Together they are a great Divine power. In 1220 they are scattered: the standard was last seen when Isaac Angelos's army fled the Bulgarians in 1190, the crowns are the conquerors' loot, and the hagka has vanished. Alexios V lost it, with his crown, to a band of French knights outside Philia in 1204. Many say the empire will not mend until one emperor holds all three.

The League of Constantine, Jerbiton magi centred on Moero's Garden with martial apprentices near their Gauntlets, wants a Greek emperor back on the throne. It has learned that demons brought the city down, and is searching Bulgarian lands for the standard in hope of a clue to the hagka.

details.antagonist: The demons who hid the empire's fall, and time

stages.title: The standard in Bulgaria
stages.clues: League magi travel the Bulgarian lands asking about the battle of 1190 and a golden eagle on a bronze staff.
stages.ignored: The league's search draws the tsar's suspicion.
stages.stopped: The standard proves to be lost for good.
stages.turned: The troupe finds the standard, and its holder's price.

stages.title: Where the eagle fell
stages.clues: A lead points to Philia, to a Latin lord's treasury, a monastery's crypt or the waters of the Bosporus; others, not all of them human, hunt the same trail.
stages.ignored: Someone else finds the hagka first.
stages.stopped: The trail goes cold.
stages.turned: The hagka, whole or in part, is in the troupe's hands.

stages.title: Three in one hand
stages.clues: Standard, crown and hagka are brought together for one emperor; which one is the question.
stages.ignored: Whoever holds them gains holy strength, and the magi who helped are suspected of meddling.
stages.stopped: The relics stay apart and the empire stays broken.
stages.turned: A devout emperor is made whole, and the Hagka's wounds begin to heal.

neighbours.secrets: The league is right: the city suffers for losing God's favour, and the hagka, restored to a truly devout emperor, would give him Solomon's wisdom, David's strength and Paul's mercy, though not necessarily a Greek throne. But the demons hid themselves from the league's spells, and it cannot tell friend from foe. The icon may be whole or broken, in a crusader's treasury, a Greek monastery, the burned Venetian quarter or the bed of the Bosporus. The living Hagka, a Divine eagle of Might 40 wounded by Akgah, guards Nicaea from the wilderness of Asia Minor.

neighbours.name: The Christians of Serapis
neighbours.summary: Sinope, a Seljuk port on the Black Sea, is known for its tolerance: Christians, Muslims and Jews worship as they please under its Greek governor, Etoumes, a vassal of the sultan but no Muslim.

stages.title: A new confessor
stages.clues: Etoumes's household grows strangely devout; a priest no bishop ordained is seen at his side.
stages.ignored: The governor falls under the priest's sway.
stages.stopped: The priest is exposed to the governor.
stages.turned: The troupe finds the sect's hiding place.

stages.title: Converts in the port
stages.clues: Sailors and merchants speak of a church where the liturgy is almost right; small miracles follow its faithful.
stages.ignored: The sect spreads along the trade routes of the Black Sea.
stages.stopped: The cult statue is found and destroyed.
stages.turned: The troupe turns a priest, and learns the demon's nature and weakness.

stages.title: Sinope under the idol
stages.clues: The governor's edicts begin to favour the sect, and its enemies disappear.
stages.ignored: A city falls to a False God, and its tolerance becomes its ruin.
stages.stopped: Serapis is cast down and the city's faiths freed.
stages.turned: The covenant earns the thanks of three faiths, and a demon's enmity.

neighbours.secrets: Hidden beneath the city is a heretical sect that worships Serapis in God's place. Alexander brought the idol to Anatolia; Ptolemy took it to Egypt and blended it with Egyptian gods; under Hadrian some Egyptian Christians took it up. Everyone believed the sect wiped out some nine hundred years ago, yet its idol was saved and carried in secret to Sinope. Serapis is a False God, a demon. About 200 follow him, led by a dozen priests who dress and serve like Orthodox clergy and convert quietly; few know what they worship, and Shroud the Stench of the Pit hides the Infernal taint of the powers he gives them. Etoumes has just taken one of the priests as his confessor, to the demon's delight.

neighbours.name: The Return of Zeno
neighbours.summary: The Church of the Holy Apostles, once the resting place of emperors and patriarchs, was stripped by looters in 1204 and keeps only a weak Divine aura. Magi of the city once hid occult books in its crypts, trusting the ghosts of dead emperors to guard them, and necromancers called up those emperors' unquiet souls there. Hermetic legend says many of both never came back up.

stages.title: Night in the church
stages.clues: A sacristan or a thief is found half-eaten among the empty tombs; the priests lock the doors at dusk.
stages.ignored: The deaths go on, and the church empties.
stages.stopped: The church is reconsecrated and its aura grows.
stages.turned: The troupe learns what lurks below, and when.

stages.title: Treasures of the crypt
stages.clues: An old Hermetic letter names a tome hidden beneath the Holy Apostles; rival magi want it too.
stages.ignored: Others go down after it, and do not return.
stages.stopped: The crypt is sealed for good.
stages.turned: The troupe overcomes Zeno and carries off the prize.

stages.title: Zeno abroad
stages.clues: As the Infernal grows in the city, the dark aura creeps out from the church into the streets.
stages.ignored: Zeno can walk wherever the city's corruption reaches.
stages.stopped: He is destroyed in his tomb.
stages.turned: The troupe uses his hunger against a worse enemy.

neighbours.secrets: Beneath it lies Zeno, the Isaurian chieftain Tarasicodissa who ruled as emperor from 474 to 491 and was buried alive by his enemies. He did not die. Demon-blooded and proof against hunger and age, he lies in his open sarcophagus by day, while the church's Dominion holds an Infernal aura of 3 in check, and at night, when the Dominion weakens to 3 and the Infernal rises to 4, he climbs out to roam the church, killing and eating anyone he catches. Outside an Infernal aura he cannot live, so he cannot leave. Whatever lies in the crypts, he guards.

neighbours.name: Thermakopolis Refounded
neighbours.summary: Thermakopolis, the great Jerbiton covenant of Constantinople, swore to protect the city and promised the Tribunal all was well until the Latins were at the walls. Its Mentem magic could not sway crusade leaders who bore protections won from demons, and its magi's spells on the walls frightened the defenders more than the enemy. Four of the five died, and Michael with them; Mathieus fled west. It is still House Jerbiton's deepest shame.

details.antagonist: The Latin city, and the demons who still haunt it

stages.title: A charter drafted
stages.clues: Young Jerbiton magi, Trasaric and Helladius among them, seek sodales and a patron for a new covenant in the city, and ask the troupe to join.
stages.ignored: The plan waits for another Tribunal.
stages.stopped: The Conciliatory Board finds the charter wanting.
stages.turned: The troupe becomes part of the founding.

stages.title: A patron in the ruins
stages.clues: Among the burned ruins of the old covenant, a spirit of the city stirs; so do things less friendly.
stages.ignored: The ruin's Infernal taint deepens.
stages.stopped: No willing patron is found, and the founding fails.
stages.turned: A worthy patron swears to the new covenant.

stages.title: A covenant in the Queen of Cities
stages.clues: The decree of founding is put to the Assembly; the Latin authorities, and Akgah, take notice.
stages.ignored: The new covenant's zeal drags it toward the meddling that damned the old one.
stages.stopped: The Assembly votes the decree down.
stages.turned: Thebes has a covenant in Constantinople again, wiser for its predecessor's fall.

neighbours.secrets: Many Jerbiton magi, above all the apprentices close to their Gauntlets, long to plant a covenant in the city again; Michael's Tabula already holds the city's defence as its cause. The Tribunal cannot decide whether to encourage it, and most would wait and see. A founding needs a declared purpose, a willing patron living on the site, a charter and the Conciliatory Board's review, then a decree. The old site is the obvious ground.

neighbours.name: In Search of Wilusa
neighbours.summary: In 1109 the Tribunal let Droserius of Merinita and four others found Wilusa at Ilion, where he said the spirit of the Scamander had promised to be their patron. By the next meeting covenant and magi were gone without trace, and since then the Tribunal has easily refused every proposal for a second covenant there. The plain of Troy is a tangle of overlapping Faerie regiones, each replaying a scene of the war, and its faeries snatch any visitor for their tales.

stages.title: Tales of a lost covenant
stages.clues: A Merinita brings back word of a Troy where men in Hermetic robes defend the walls.
stages.ignored: The tale is forgotten for another century.
stages.stopped: The Tribunal forbids any search.
stages.turned: The troupe takes up the search.

stages.title: The wrong Troy
stages.clues: Faeries of Ilion lead searchers into their own stories; a Hektor or an Akhilles claims the troupe for his tale.
stages.ignored: A searcher is lost in a regio.
stages.stopped: The troupe escapes the faeries' stories.
stages.turned: Deep Faerie Lore points to the true regio.

stages.title: The siege that never ends
stages.clues: Inside Odysseus's regio the final assault begins again, and the defenders take the troupe for Greeks.
stages.ignored: The troupe becomes part of the siege.
stages.stopped: Odysseus is outwitted, the regio opened, and Wilusa's magi come home a hundred years late.
stages.turned: The troupe gives Odysseus a new tale to tell, and wins a strange faerie friend.

neighbours.secrets: Wilusa was raised by magic in a Faerie regio of aura 4, but not the one holding the Scamander's spirit: a faerie who calls himself Odysseus tricked Droserius, sealed the regio and made the covenant look like Troy. Ever since he has put it through the war's last assault, and the magi defend it by reflex. He has bent time so that more than a century has passed outside while the magi think it a few months. Odysseus is very aware, and hopes to gather vitality enough to change his own story. Other regiones copy the fall of Troy too, so the troupe may beat the Greeks and find it is the wrong city. Rescued, Droserius and his sodales will not want to leave, until they learn how long they have been gone.

characters.summary:
Epidauros's leader in name, simply as its eldest, looking a hundred and seven: a magus aegrotus, a leper magus, like all his kind among the Tytalus deeply gifted for healing and longevity, and probably the Tribunal's greatest expert in both. He seems a scruffy old man in a ragged leper's robe, a linen veil over his face and gloves to the elbow hiding how old and shrivelled he is, and a bell on his robes clanks constantly to warn of his disease.

Though heavily marked by Twilight he is easy enough to approach, if anyone does: the prejudice against lepers is not only a mundane one, and no magic cures leprosy.

Lame and silver-haired in a plain grey shawl, she walks awkwardly with her talisman staff, and her snake familiar noses out herbs in the hills. She is usually the one who deals with visitors.

She knows the magic of defixiones, curse tablets, and specialises accordingly in Perdo and Corpus. Elegant, athletic and black-haired, she would be handsome but for the ritual scars across her face, thought to come from a Mystery ordeal.

characters.summary:
Leader of Gigas and senior Tremere of the Tribunal, one of the few of his House to hold his own sigil, looking a robust sixty-four. As his House's Tribune in Thebes he uses the proxy votes the young Tremere give him to reform the Tribunal as Coeris directs; he keeps carefully above the quarrels his covenant and House pick with Theban custom, though he almost surely backs most of them.

He dresses as a minor noble and is often out hunting with a hawk on his wrist; the locals take him for an exile from fallen Constantinople. His silver wolf Čovek is the covenant's patron in name. He seeks immortality through his line and has trained apprentice after apprentice since he could Open the Arts, gladly taking at the Apprentice Presentation the children no one else wants, and giving them a place in the service of his House.

characters.summary:
Looks forty-two. His parents had him made a eunuch to help him to a fine career in the palace bureaucracy; his Gift awoke quickly enough for him to stop the surgery before it was finished. Boustaphan, who kept spies in the imperial palace, found him and brought him to Gigas to train.

Perhaps because he so nearly became a man of ink and parchment, he is fiercely anti-intellectual: he will not read, studies the Arts mostly from vis, and holds that the Order has lost its intuitive bond with magic to the written word, dry logic and endless philosophy. He has made friends in House Criamon and, rumour says, in some esoteric Mystery Cults. His Form is Ignem, which he treats as a search for the light of the soul.

characters.summary: Gigas's chief negotiator and envoy, and the easiest of its magi to talk to, looking thirty-three. His role may seem at odds with a martial House, but the Tremere know diplomacy matters as much as readiness for war, and value him; he plays up his seeming misfit in the House's ranks to win sympathy from those he deals with. He is said to carry a faerie blessing that makes everyone he meets think well of him.

characters.summary:
'The Listener', leader of Hedyosmos since his mater left the post fifty years ago, and head of the Terrae Cult in the Tribunal, looking eighty-eight; a remarkable Longevity Ritual keeps his body sound. Statuesque, snow-haired, he is wholly blind, his eyes white without iris or pupil, and often paints eyes on his lids as on a marble statue; his skin is cool and he wears a plain tunic with an embroidered hem. He moves as little as he can and can freeze so still that strangers take him for a statue, standing for hours or days; that he does so more and more makes some think Twilight is swallowing him. His familiar is an imago, a spirit of sound, bound through the Mystery of the Spirit Familiar.

He is reckoned the Tribunal's greatest master of Terram, and his books are famous far afield. His mater has vanished from the Tribunal; he says she will not come back, but not whether she died or passed into Final Twilight.

characters.summary: The archon of the Tribunal, elected by the archai in 1214, looking fifty-three. Ausculator's youngest filia, she is being groomed to succeed him when Twilight finally takes him: not the cult's most powerful member, but the one who knows its rituals best. Her speciality is caves and underground ways; she has explored many cave systems in the Tribunal and beyond and brought back secrets she only half understands. She also has a remarkable mastery of earth elementals, and casts rituals such as Conjuring the Mystic Tower for others at the price of the vis and a shard's neutralisation.

He takes up cases where a magus seems to have escaped the Order's justice, and tries to set them right by fierce speeches at Tribunal, by petition after petition to the Legislative Board, and, failing all else, by Wizard's War. His spirit familiar is an Aspect of the Erinyes, the threefold Daimons of vengeance. The Titanoi leave him little time for the Terrae Cult, of which he is a member in name only.

She is obsessed with the legends of Hermes, keeps a hidden laboratory on Mount Cyllene where the god was supposedly born, and believes that divining his nature will lay bare the roots of magic itself.

Chapter nine names him; the book gives no House or age (Tytalus, among the covenant's Tytalan theurgists, is assumed here).

characters.summary:
Mother Anna, looking sixty-two, spiritual head of Koukoubiou, a small retreat of the kind Byzantine ladies found when they would rather not enter a great convent; she and her sister founded it straight after the sack of 1185 and laboured to rebuild the city and heal its wounds, the spiritual ones above all. Strong-willed and clear of purpose, having seen at first hand what sin and the Infernal do, she rules her nuns with an iron hand, thinks herself a soldier of the spirit, and has no patience with stupidity, cowardice or compromise.

When she must she can be civil, even play the meek servant, while skewering her betters with a dry wit inherited from her grandfather, a celebrated scholar and courtier. She serves the city and God only, and some say in that order.

characters.summary: Anna's younger sister, looking sixty-three, who has always lived in her shadow: as kind and self-effacing as Anna is bold, but strong in her own quiet way. A brilliant scholar of Neo-Platonic philosophy with a deep grasp of theology, above all the Cappadocian Fathers on the Holy Trinity, she holds the covenant together with her patient, loving calm.

characters.summary: Nonna's twin, a Seirene, looking twenty-two. Her music works on courage, but a Restriction stops her ever using it on a man she is drawn to, a real trouble for one so romantic. She waits on the queen's household at court. She has kept a Longevity Ritual since just after her Gauntlet to keep her looks, a vanity the other magae think sinful.

characters.name: Nonna

characters.summary: Nereida's twin and her opposite in all but looks, which are nearly identical but for their apparent ages (Nonna looks her age), to much confusion at court. Men do not interest her at all. A close friend of Queen Margaret of Hungary, now living in Athens, she is fond of King Demetrios but would rather have seen Margaret rule. She has just come back from years at Empress Yolanda's court in Constantinople, and her drive to empower women and barely hidden scorn for men's failings may set her against her sister and the others; she would fight any man's admission to the covenant.

characters.name: Lucian the Scholar

description.biography: The Sundered Eagle: The Theban Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
Aegaea's unchallenged leader and the last filius of its founder Orithyia, looking sixty-five: a famous scholar of Byzantine and ancient Greek letters who can recite dozens of long poems by heart and studies the power of story and rhetoric. He is believed to know several Mysteries, among them the Folk Mystery of Story Magic. White-haired and kindly of face, he wears loud dark blue robes embroidered with scenes of Greek and Byzantine legend. Unlike most of his covenant he travels widely and cares little for the sea.

He is an active politician with obscure, eccentric aims, liable to switch his support at once to any magus he sees acting heroically or in keeping with old stories and traditions, though Aegaea's name for treachery blunts his influence. He leads the Children of Olympos, who want the old Greek gods as the covenants' patrons, and coined the names of the three titan factions (the Seekers of the Fallen, the Legion of Atlas and Kampe's Lovers) in a mocking speech four Tribunals ago. He claims to have met the infant Zeus on Ida, and enjoyed young Proximios's acrobatics when the Redcap brought messages.

His Twilight Scars are hidden: some mental flaws, above all lapses in which he forgets who he is and claims to be someone else, usually a hero of Greek legend.
characters.secrets: He devised two Mysteries, Elysian Ecstasy and Olympian Pact, through which a person is possessed by a Greek god, and he alone holds an Olympian Pact. His changeable politics are a plan: he has cast the Tribunal's magi and covenants in roles in a grand re-enactment of the myths and steers them toward their parts, hoping Faerie will one day replace the Magic auras of the covenants. He may be duped by pretenders, faerie or infernal, and Proximios hopes to slip an infernalist into his league so that it raises a False God.

characters.summary: Charming and lovely, looking twenty-five and younger every year: born with the blood of the sea nereids, she has tail fins for feet and purple eyes, and her Twilight Scars are making her less human and more nereid. The latest has given her a crab's pincers at her temples, mostly hidden in her blue-green hair. Lucian hails this as a sign that she will become the faerie Amphitrite, Poseidon's bride, and urges her toward the Inner Mystery of Becoming; she is of two minds about it, but has begun wearing queenly white robes trimmed with gold. She often rides her dolphin familiar, Hippothoon, named for a mortal son of Poseidon.

characters.summary: A plain, earnest woman who looks forty-three, whose heartbeast, as her name says, is a dolphin: she joined Aegaea for the water, not for any love of Faerie. Friendly and curious, she likes to swim beside ships carrying Redcaps to trade gossip (sailors think a dolphin alongside lucky). Most magi like her for her open ways, but some think her a busybody and distrust her.
characters.secrets: Proximios has marked her as one of the innocents the League of the Vigilant is to be steered into accusing of diabolism.

characters.summary: A tall, athletic Bulgarian who looks forty, with a stallion heartbeast. As a young magus of Moero's Garden in Constantinople he loved racing in the Hippodrome. After the sack and that covenant's flight to Nicaea he met Lucian at the Tribunal of 1207, who filled his head with tales of Poseidon, maker of the horse and inventor of riding and racing, and Krum joined Aegaea on the spot, a sharp change of scene. He now means to grow his heartbeast into one of the golden-maned sea-horses that drew Poseidon's chariot.

characters.summary:
Founder of Favonius and designer of its wonderful ships, looking fifty-eight: a hale man, black-bearded and curly-haired, his skin browned by life on the shore and his body hugely muscled from heaving beams, a fine climber with sure balance. A lifelong lover of ships, he specialises in enchanting them and is famous as a builder of sea-going vessels, nearly always busy with a commission. He is best in Rego and in craft magic, which eases his labour; four forge-companions work with him, and his laboratory on Andros is richly specialised.

He belongs to the Mystic Fraternity of Samos (The Mysteries Revised Edition), or whatever cult teaches Hermetic Architecture in your saga.
characters.secrets: An initiation gone wrong left him with a Death Prophecy, that he will die with the sky above and the sea below; so he has never sailed on any of his own ships.

characters.summary: Memnos's filia and the covenant's real leader, looking thirty-eight: a lithe woman who dresses as a sailor, far handier than robes on deck, and holds the title of Gubernatrix, chief helmsman of the fleet, captain of the Philomela. Her enchanting is in ropes, knots, cords and twine, very useful aboard but no way to win steady customers for items. Her familiar is a monkey she found on one of the fleet's longer voyages, often seen keeping watch from the Philomela's rigging. She and Basil of Andros argue endlessly over profit against adventure.

characters.summary:
Captain of the Tereus, where his sanctum is, though he spends most of his time in a one-man sailing boat he paid Memnos to build. A monster hunter who chases creatures for their vis: the Tribunal knows that if a covenant has a monster too much for it, Aeliophanes will kill it, if he can be found. He is after glory, not helping, yet he is likeable, and the grogs love his dash and his Gentle Gift.

He looks nineteen, a dark-haired young hero with a neat beard, and is Unaging. His talisman is his spear, enchanted to strike home despite the Might of his quarry. Peter Monocheiros owes him his life and is utterly loyal.

characters.name: Stouritus

description.biography: The Sundered Eagle: The Theban Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
Primus of House Verditius, looking ninety-three, and a rare thing in his House: a humble man. Long expecting to be primus, he shunned most of the Inner Mysteries that feed pride and studied instead the House's history, members and rulings. To him Verditius is the one House to outlast time, since a magus dies but an enchanted item may last for ever. He has made Ingasia a model Verditius covenant.

He would like to forbid vendettas among its members but has no power to, so he leads by example and refuses what he sees as a violent, divisive custom of his House; Hydatius follows him. He has taken part in the Tribunal's government for some seventy years and is known as honest and fair. His long cause has been how many items a Verditius may sell to mundanes: the Order only demands intermediaries, and many Tribunals follow Rome's one a year, but he has raised Thebes's limit to five and persuaded it that Items of Quality are not enchanted items and do not count. He is determined that the Contest of 1234 will be held at Ingasia.

characters.summary: A magus of Ingasia who follows Stouritus's example and will not join in vendettas. With Proximios of Alexandria he has just founded the League of the Vigilant to hunt out infernal corruption in the Order, he as its general and the Redcap as its purse and supplier. They want members from outside the Tribunal, fresh blood to root out the bad, mean to keep the others' names secret while they themselves seek help openly, and watch their fellows patiently for a slip. Their fine reputations make the league respectable, and its critics hold their tongues.
characters.secrets: Proximios, an infernalist, founded the league through him and talked him into leading it, meaning to turn it on innocents (Caterina, the young magi of Erebos, Delfini). He will urge Hydatius to send members after the suspects, and a demon in Hydatius's shape will order them to attack.

characters.summary: A maker of enchanted mosaics who looks forty-two, one of the Confraternity of Irene (see Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults). Spiteful and proud, she has lately been initiated into the Inner Mystery of automata, and works to unlock the secrets of two statues from the Hippodrome's rows that she has got hold of. (The book once spells her Euxodia.)

characters.summary:
Conjoined twins, joined at the spine so that they always face away from each other, who look thirty-five. Stouritus trained them, and they make most of Ingasia's enchanted items, forever at work. They long ago learned to live with their bodies: their laboratories are joined and mirror each other, forge for forge and bench for bench, so each can work her own enchantment at the same station as her sister. Each has her own vendator and team of forge-companions and runs her own Hermetic business. They take a season off only to study vis.

Her twin is Bobila.
characters.secrets: Unknown to Stouritus, they sell more items than the law allows, and favour Nicaea, Venice's sworn enemy; they enrich the covenant slowly so as not to be noticed, and their long-term plans are unknown.

characters.summary: The Tribunal's polemarch, elected in 1207 and again in 1214: a sturdy grey-haired woman who looks fifty-eight and dresses as an ancient Greek soldier. Filia of Laskaris, the founder, and named for him, she is a seasoned hoplite known for ruthless efficiency, a master of Rego and Terram whose trademark is a crushing hail of stones. Her familiar Hadrianus, a fierce wild goat of the island and sure-footed on its rocks, patrols it hard and butts any suspicious newcomer down the cliffs into the sea.

characters.summary: Drakos blood makes him huge, strong and brave, and he is held to be Varazes's own grandson, heir to his mythic strength, and to the drakoi's dreadful stupidity: hardly a grog on Polyaigos is duller, and he reduced his long-suffering master to tears. He has had to give up most book learning, and subtle Arts like Mentem and Vim are nearly beyond him, but the raw force of his simple earth and fire magic makes up for it. Honestly pious, like many of his House, he looks forty-four and has fought in more than one Wizard's March.

characters.summary: A lanky, fair-haired eunuch in plain white robes, looking forty-one. Bought as a castrated slave, he was educated for the imperial court like many eunuchs until a Jerbiton maga of Moero's Garden found him; she wanted him for her apprentice, but a Bonisagus of Trianoma's line saw his fine mind and claimed him at Tribunal. He has served twice on the Council of Magistrates, a brilliant administrator there and at home, and in his second term was chosen archon, a rare honour for so young a magus.

characters.summary:
A Venetian maga trained in the Roman Tribunal, newly come to Thebes, the reverse of many of her House, who have gone the other way; she looks her age. Her apparent ties to Venice, chief author of the crusade that took Constantinople, make the Theban Jerbiton deeply distrust her. Polyaigos has put her in charge of running and growing its mines and trade, for which she has a true Venetian gift.

Like many Jerbiton she long refused a Longevity Ritual, but failing vigour has made her accept she needs one; she hopes the Tribunal will sponsor it, and is working to build a good name and earn tokens. As a metoikos she can hold none until her citizenship is decreed.
characters.secrets: She has met the Duke of Naxos in the guise of a rich noblewoman and is preparing a discreet arrangement with him. Proximios has marked her as an innocent for the League of the Vigilant to accuse of diabolism.

characters.summary: A young Verditius, trained at Ingasia, who has just moved to Polyaigos. The book gives no age or traits.
characters.secrets: He was born Pietro, younger brother of Marco Sanudo, Duke of Naxos, and nephew of Doge Enrico Dandolo: a pleasant, clever, bookish boy with something deeply strange about him, who made his brother uneasy. Among his last acts Dandolo found him a place, which was apprenticeship at Ingasia. At Polyaigos he has learnt of Marco's rise; he keeps a warm love for his family but has not yet got in touch, while Marco often wonders what became of him and hopes for news.

characters.name: Petros

characters.summary:
The leader of Michael's Tabula, a man of thirty-six in the body of a boy of eleven. His apprenticeship went wrong twice: his pater Michael botched his own Longevity Ritual, which took hold of the apprentice instead and stopped him growing; then Michael died defending the city just before Petros was to swear the Oath. Young and untried as he was, the covenant chose him as its leader out of respect for his pater.

He is a sad man caught in a child's body. His prayers to grow up go unanswered, and he carries the shame of the city's fall and of Thermakopolis's end. At his lowest he has thought of entering a monastery, but he stays to honour Michael's cause.

characters.summary:
A Saxon from the Holy Roman Empire who looks forty-three, one of the handful of 'Frankish' magi in the Tribunal, and one who fits the type: big, burly, fair and bearded, rough in his manners, and speaking Greek with a heavy accent. Under the bluster lies deep faith.

He went on the Fourth Crusade as a knight in the following of the bishop of Halberstadt, having sworn, to quiet the Quaesitores, to use no magic while it lasted. Along the way he came to doubt the crusade's righteousness, and when the city fell he left the assault to defend the innocent and fight demons, ending up beside the dying magi of Thermakopolis and saving Petros. A formidable swordsman, he is the covenant's most martial magus and the keenest in its military plans. As a magus trained outside the Tribunal he is a metoikos.

links.note: Saved him in the fall of the city

characters.summary:
Brother Artoud, leader of Xylinites, looking about seventy-one. Most of his life passed in central Anatolia's hills, in the Levant Tribunal, in a Criamon Clutch destroyed in the wars between the Sultanate of Rum and the empire. He is fanatically loyal to his House and cares little for the wider Order, which he thinks run by ignorant, boorish Frankish barbarians. His Gift is blatant. As a magus trained outside the Tribunal he is a metoikos.

He has turned down Repose to stay and serve his House, and gives sporadic, half-hearted support to the League Against Idolatry.
characters.secrets: His body is in better shape now than at twenty-one: he does not age, shrugs off injuries quickly and moves with more than human grace, the fruit of long mastery of the flesh on the Path of the Body (Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults). He hides it, passing off the pale scars on his tanned skin as the marks of mortification, feigning a stoop and a slight limp among mundanes, and moving as little as he can.

characters.summary: A Criamon of the Clutch who looks forty-three, trained by Artoud. He is the orphanage's official castrator and, known for his medical skill, has often been called on to carry out blindings at the palace and across the city. With his deft Corpus magic and his mastery of Perdo Corpus he does it by magic, painlessly and safely, and he holds his work to be philosophically right: it serves Harmony where the likely alternative, execution or murder, would only add to Strife.

characters.summary: The only member of Xylinites born in the Tribunal, Artoud's apprentice and a nephew of the deposed emperor Alexios IV Angelos, who was killed in 1204. Gelded as a small child because he was politically dangerous, he hates the Doukas family without mercy. His imperial blood fascinates Artoud, who will not expel him, though he sees that the young man must soon be sent far from Constantinople before he brings disaster.

characters.summary:
The logothete, the Tribunal's Chief Redcap since Petronas stepped down in 1207: a tall, thin, unGifted man with a receding hairline and a long grey moustache, who looks eighty-two. An old Supernatural Virtue gives him the full benefit of a Longevity Ritual as a magus would have it, but Warping has lately given him his first Major Flaw: to his shame, the Curse of Lycaon. He turns into a wolf not at the full moon but when he grows too anxious.

He regrets ever taking the post. For all his efforts, records have gone astray, lists have vanished, and the register of tokens and shards, the most important book of all, has been found wrong; he scraped past ostracism in 1214, knows the Tribunal is unhappy, and means to resign at the next meeting.

characters.name: Proximios

description.biography: The Sundered Eagle: The Theban Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
An unGifted Redcap who looks forty-two: broad in the shoulder, handsome, his dark hair neatly combed. He is of the blood of Andreas, a mythic hero of Justinian's Persian Wars, a gymnast rather than a soldier, who beat two armoured Persian champions hand to hand; from him Proximios has astonishing gifts, near-legendary feats of tumbling among them. As a young messenger he dazzled the magi he carried letters to with his acrobatics, and Lucian of Aegaea loved the show.

He is known as a quick, capable politician, though he has never held office and has always been somebody's assistant; so deep in Tribunal business is he that for twenty years he has been let off ordinary Redcap duty and carries no messages. It was his idea, in 1186, to make the logothete's post permanent instead of seven years, for continuity and so no newcomer need learn the records afresh, and it pleased those who complain the Tribunal's officers change too often. Many Redcaps want him as the next logothete and will propose it in 1221; he neither seeks nor refuses it, and most think that is humility.

With Hydatius of Ingasia he founded the League of the Vigilant, paying for it and supplying its magic while Hydatius leads it. He backs Ziper's wish to take the craftsmen Nanno and Ampelius into Moero's Garden, pointing to how well his own House of unGifted folk serves the Order.
characters.secrets:
Proximios is an infernalist, unknown to anyone: a master of the Unholy Method of Incantation and the Unholy Power of Diablerie, with a long list of demons' True Names. He uses summoned demons as spies and lures, and sets Tempters and Evil Spirits to drive his fellows to sin. He means to bring down the Order, starting in Thebes, and works slowly and covertly among magi who would spot anything blatant, seeking a weak link in every covenant; his post at Alexandria shows him the letters and missives passing through. Neither Method nor Power is on his generated sheet: the storyguide adds them.

He set up the League of the Vigilant to aim it, in time, at innocent magi who look like diabolists (Caterina da Vigonovo, young magi of Erebos, nosy Delfini of Aegaea), sending league members to look into them, never going himself, and then having a demon dressed as Hydatius order an attack. He would turn Aiakia, or more easily the hotter Tisiphon, against Gigas by blaming its Tremere for Constantinople's fall, and set Celaenea, who adores Hermes, against Lucian's Children of Olympos; other infernalists have told him an infernalist planted in that league could make it raise a False God in place of a faerie.

In 1220 these plans are only forming. He will take the logothete's post, seeming reluctant so the blame falls elsewhere when things unravel, and use the register of tokens and shards to reward those who cooperate. He has not yet recruited magi, but has his eye on a few who might be tempted. His plots always look like someone else's work; the book suggests him as a saga's chief enemy, his threat growing slowly over the years (see An Enemy Within).

links.note: Co-founder of the League of the Vigilant, which Hydatius leads
Backs Ziper's proposal to take Nanno and Ampelius into Moero's Garden
Delighted Lucian with acrobatics as a young messenger

characters.summary:
The only Gifted member of Alexandria, who looks thirty-nine. She came straight from her Gauntlet, two years before Constantinople fell, while the covenant's name was still good, drawn by Alexander's artifacts; in some twenty years of study she has got little further with them.

Because of that interest she was made keeper of the artifacts and their loans, which both thrills and galls her: she loves having charge of them but hates that they are often out when she wants to study them. Alexandria has chosen to lend them freely, and she abides by it even when it upsets her own plans. She has no Mechanica yet, so cannot mend the glass submarine. She would also dearly like Hagia Sophia in Constantinople studied for insights from Heron's theories, and will fund any magus with a way to do it.

characters.summary:
The founder: a tall maga with thin white hair and dull blue eyes, who looks ninety-one and wears rich robes, gold necklaces, jewelled rings and bracelets crusted with gems. Before Moero's Garden she won a great name in House Jerbiton by collecting every poem of Kassia, the ninth-century nun who is the empire's most famous woman poet. A master of Rego and Mentem, she summons and questions ghosts in her hunt for old poetry.

Longevity Rituals have never worked well for her, and she is very frail and near her end, which does not trouble her: though she grieves for the old site, she is content with idle pleasures, letters to her two living daughters and early evening company. She has served the Tribunal before but says she is too old for politics now; still, she means to go to Delos for the next meeting to offer vis to the covenant's patron. She soothes Hipparchus's ghost with evenings of star-gazing.

characters.summary:
The oddest Jerbiton of the covenant in body and temper, who looks forty-three: a true hermaphrodite, medically proven, proud of it, who dresses to show both natures, with a full beard and a gown that shows off his bust. He calls his nature beautiful and will not hide it; his sodales accept it but wish he spoke of it less. He takes his Longevity Ritual gladly, a daily draught of herbs and powders at noon, and is hale.

He shares his sodales' love of art, manners and comfort, but cares more for winning back the covenant's lost art than for pleasure: he belongs to Valnastium's league of New Iconophiles and goes to Constantinople at least once a year to hunt for the missing pieces. He sides with Ionnia against the League of Constantine, and is the only one besides Ziper not appalled at taking in Nanno and Ampelius. His apprentice Pancratius is due his Gauntlet at the Tribunal of 1221 and will probably join; Trasaric and Helladius hope he will vote with them.

characters.summary:
The eldest of Moero's Garden, who joined only after it moved to Nicaea, a Tytalus with the Gentle Gift. Stooped, wrinkled and wholly bald, in white robes under a red toga, he looks sixty-five and venerable, but has the energy and sharpness of a young man.

He thinks the covenant too small to carry weight in the Tribunal and has proposed taking the craftsmen Nanno and Ampelius in as members of House Jerbiton: they are not magi, but can put minor enchantments in their work. Proximios of Alexandria backs him. Everyone else but Syagricus is appalled, less because the pair are unGifted than because they are craftsmen. The book once calls Ziper a maga but elsewhere 'he'; the pack follows the latter.

characters.summary:
The oracle of Delphi: a lone Criamon maga living in the Temple of Apollon, which is her laboratory, under the ancient oracle's ceremonial name. Each Pythia chooses her successor, often her filia, who takes the name after initiation into the oracle's Mysteries without telling anyone, so Pythia is treated as one enduring person. Magi consult her before founding a covenant, adopting a patron or a great Tribunal decision; she breathes the omphalos's vapours to prophesy and gathers Delphi's Intellego and Creo vis for the Tribunal after taking her own share. She sees supplicants only between spring and autumn.

The book gives no age; her present self is not described.
characters.secrets: In the Absent Oracle a girl claiming to be her apprentice meets visitors with the news that Pythia is gone.

Passara filia Bacauda filius Aella, a maga of Verditius with the Gentle Gift and of no covenant, who keeps the automata of the Palace of Magnaura safe from time and wear as her lineage's founder Aella did. She lives in apartments in the palace that the emperor's autocrat gave her, and, proud of her lineage and its mysteries, will live nowhere else. The book gives no age.

Formosos of Guernicus believes she works for the Latin emperor and does more than tend the automata, and means to prove it.
characters.secrets: The book leaves whether she truly serves the emperor to the storyguide.

Formosos thinks Vaanes's part in that was criminal, and his pride will not let the matter rest: he is set on proving that Passara, Aella's heir in the Magnaura, is working for the Latin emperor and not merely keeping the automata, and will try to recruit player magi to look into her and her mundane dealings in secret. characters.summary:
A Bonisagus preacher who holds the First Commandment above everything. To him the pagan survivals all through the Tribunal's customs are a creeping evil, and he means to scrub every trace of idolatry out of Hermetic practice in Thebes. Oddly he has no quarrel with the titans, who ask no worship, only with the faerie gods who hunger for it. The book names no covenant for him.

That makes him the rallying point of the Legion of Atlas, whose aims match his though their reasons do not; his eloquence has more than once saved magi who harmed faeries from conviction, so player magi may find him an ally at Tribunal, wanted or not.

rooms.name: As the book describes it
rooms.description: The Sundered Eagle p. 86: the ancient forge at the volcano's heart, made a Hermetic laboratory shared by the magi, +8 to Rego and +5 to making enchanted items

rooms.name: As the book describes it
rooms.description: The Sundered Eagle p. 63: the shared laboratory specialized in longevity and healing; +6 to a Longevity Ritual's Lab Total for one who sleeps here, who also gains +12 to the next Wound Recovery roll

books.name: The library of Epidauros
books.description: No books are named. Narrow by design: the finest collection on Medicine anywhere, with outstanding books on Creo and Corpus, and little beyond its healing work.

books.name: The books of Erebos
books.description: No books are named. Each magus keeps his own, mostly in the lore of his own native tradition, and the leader shares out what the covenant holds in common.

books.name: The library of Gigas
books.description: No books are named. The covenant keeps its records of the Tremere in Thebes and its reports for Coeris, which Boustaphan opens to no outsider.

books.name: The works of Ausculator on Terram
books.author: Ausculator of Guernicus
books.description: Ausculator's books on Terram, famous across the Order and dear for their exceptional quality; a genuine copy is known by the glitter of mica dust worked into the parchment. The book gives no titles, levels or Qualities.

books.name: The records of the Sundering
books.description: Hedyosmos's records of the years of the Sundering. House Tremere officially cares nothing for its details, but many of its magi would dearly like to read them.

books.name: The books of the Ladies of Thessaloniki
books.description: No books are named, and as holy magae the sisters need few. Theocharista's own reading in Neo-Platonic philosophy and the Cappadocian Fathers on the Trinity is the nearest thing to a library.

books.name: The library of Aegaea
books.description: The book names no books. Built up over two centuries, it is strong in Faerie Lore and Aquam and holds an unrivalled collection of ancient Greek and Byzantine poetry; Orithyia's own colourful accounts of her travels are among the Tribunal's half-legendary texts.

books.name: The library of Favonius
books.description: The book names no books. Whatever the covenant keeps is stowed in the sancta of the Philomela and the Tereus, and its costliest and most delicate goods in the Halcyon's hold.

books.name: The libraries of Ingasia
books.description: The book names no books. The libraries lie underground in the labyrinth of Mosychlos beside the laboratories and vis stores, and as befits the House's chief covenant Stouritus has long studied its history, members and rulings.

books.name: The library of Polyaigos
books.description: The book names no books. The library is in the watchtower on the high peak, with the council chamber, and serves the covenant's school of Greek, Latin, philosophy and the liberal arts as well as its magi.

books.name: The library of Michael's Tabula
books.description: The book names no books. The covenant has begun a library, some of it old volumes saved from the fall of Thermakopolis, added to by the money and books an anonymous sponsor sends by Redcap every year or two. Some of the magi may hold knowledge or relics of Heron of Alexandria's legacy (Ancient Magic).

books.name: The icon of St. Loukia
books.description: A tiny mosaic icon of St. Loukia of Berytus, the covenant's patron, given to the monastery by Romanos III in 1031. Not a book: meditation on it teaches the Supernatural Ability Animal Ken as a summa, which the magi have not yet realised.

books.name: The orphanage library of St. Christopoulos
books.description: The book names no books. Beside the master's house stand the orphanage's scriptorium and library, kept up through the Jerbiton era when the covenant's magi taught there; what the fleeing Jerbiton took with them in 1204 is not said.

books.name: The records of the Theban Tribunal
books.description: The book names no books. Alexandria's stone houses in the inner regio are the storehouse of the Tribunal's records, kept by its middle-aged Redcaps, and the logothete keeps the register of every polites's tokens and shards and of each neutralization a Redcap has witnessed. Under Leontius records have gone astray, lists have vanished and the register has been found faulty.

books.name: The poems of Kassia
books.author: Kassia
books.description: Ionnia's famous collection of the complete poetry of Kassia, the ninth-century nun who is the best-known woman poet of the empire, the heart of the covenant's library. Its gathering made Ionnia's name in House Jerbiton. Much of the library was left in Constantinople in 1204; what came is kept in the basement by the scribe Viviana.

books.name: Ionnia's summa on Rego
books.author: Ionnia of Jerbiton
books.description: One of the several summae and tractatus on Rego and Mentem Ionnia has written; the book gives no levels or qualities.

books.name: Ionnia's summa on Mentem
books.author: Ionnia of Jerbiton
books.description: Ionnia's summa on the Art of the mind, by which she calls up and questions ghosts; the book gives no level or quality.

books.name: Ionnia's tractatus on Rego and Mentem
books.author: Ionnia of Jerbiton
books.description: Ionnia's tractatus on her two Arts, entered as one record; the book gives neither their number nor their quality.

books.name: Ionnia's poems
books.author: Ionnia of Jerbiton
books.description: Tractatus of Ionnia's own poetry, kept with the covenant's great collection of verse.

creatures.name: Baskanos
creatures.how_many: swarms, unseen in the air wherever envy breeds
creatures.weakness: Abhorrent Material (an amulet against the evil eye)

powers.name: Coagulation
powers.description: Takes on a solid body, which it can let dissolve whenever it likes.

powers.name: Obsession
powers.description: Costs 1 to 3 points: plants the Obsession Trait Envy in its victim, as Realms of Power: The Infernal describes.

creatures.appearance: A shrivelled little man the size of a rat whose head is nothing but one huge, unblinking, lidless eye.
creatures.notes:
A kakodaemon, as the Greeks call this kind of demon. Baskanoi hover like clouds of flies, waiting for a chance to sour good fortune into resentment; most cases of the evil eye are their work, though some people cast it themselves by Folk Magic or the Hex Ability. Their Restriction is that the Hex reaches only someone who has been praised or envied, so they use Obsession to make such targets. Wound ranges: Light 1, Medium 2, Heavy 3, Incapacitated at 4, Dead from 5.
The surest ward is a blue glass amulet with an eye painted on it, worn on the neck or wrist or hung over a cradle or a byre; the few who can make them are much sought after. A horned sign made with the left hand after careless praise wards only for a moment.
creatures.source: The Sundered Eagle: The Theban Tribunal p. 47

creatures.name: Arge, Nymph of Delos

powers.name: Donning the Corporeal Veil
powers.description: Makes herself a body with these statistics and lets it go at will. If the body is killed it leaves the vis behind, but only this Aspect dies, not the spirit.

powers.name: Strike of the Cornered Game
powers.description: Anyone her arrow hits is held paralysed until she lifts the power or the sun next rises or sets (ReCo 25: base 5, +1 Touch, +2 Sun, +1 ended at will; Greater Power, -1 Might cost, +4 Init).

powers.name: Outstanding Distance
powers.description: Her arrow can reach a target as far as seven leagues off with no penalty for range, on a normal missile Attack, so long as she can see it with nothing in the way (ReHe 25: base 3, +1 Touch, +4 magnitudes for the distance; Greater Power, +5 Init).

creatures.equipment: Short bow of ivory, full heavy leather armor.
creatures.appearance: One of three severe young women with their hair pulled tightly back, in leather armor with ivory bows, plainly displeased; the three are hard to tell apart.
creatures.notes:
One of the three Hyperborean nymphs who came to Delos with Apollon and Artemis and now keep its shrines; each embodies part of archery, and Arge rules its distance. Their sisters Hyperoche and Laodice left Delos for home with sacred gifts and were never heard of again, and the three long for news of them. They appear when someone damages the island's ruins or relics, and give the culprit a few breaths to explain before they start shooting; their victims are mortally hurt but do not die until they have left Delos. Their bow gives Defense as not applicable. Wound ranges: the usual ones for Size 0, Light 1-5 to Dead from 21. Their Personality Traits are Essential Traits. Tethered Magic (Houses of Hermes: True Lineages) lets them carry their powers on their arrows.
They are Aspects of Daimons of the Magic Realm: one slain forms again a day later. They keep to the shrines where the aura is strongest, so Acclimation does not wear down their Might. They speak Hyperborean and could tell a seeker of Hyperborean magic much, but they are unfriendly and want proof of worth first.
creatures.source: The Sundered Eagle: The Theban Tribunal p. 75

creatures.name: Opis, Nymph of Delos

powers.name: Donning the Corporeal Veil
powers.description: Makes herself a body with these statistics and lets it go at will. If the body is killed it leaves the vis behind, but only this Aspect dies, not the spirit.

powers.description: Anyone her arrow hits is held paralysed until she lifts the power or the sun next rises or sets (ReCo 25: base 5, +1 Touch, +2 Sun, +1 ended at will; Greater Power, -1 Might cost, +4 Init).

powers.name: Unequaled Aim
powers.description: An arrow that hits strikes the body part she chooses: normal damage, and the part is useless, giving a Minor Flaw (Lame, Missing Eye or Missing Hand, say) until the wound heals. A struck hand lets go of what it held. A Greater Power, +7 Init, matching PeCo 15 (+1 Part, +1 Touch, base 5).

creatures.appearance: One of three severe young women with their hair pulled tightly back, in leather armor with ivory bows, plainly displeased; the three are hard to tell apart.

powers.name: Donning the Corporeal Veil
powers.description: Makes herself a body with these statistics and lets it go at will. If the body is killed it leaves the vis behind, but only this Aspect dies, not the spirit.

powers.description: Anyone her arrow hits is held paralysed until she lifts the power or the sun next rises or sets (ReCo 25: base 5, +1 Touch, +2 Sun, +1 ended at will; Greater Power, -1 Might cost, +4 Init).

powers.name: Peerless Trajectory
powers.description: Her arrow bends round corners, walls and shields: if she knows where the target is, cover doesn't stop a normal missile Attack, range counts along the arrow's real path, and the target's Defense leaves out any shield. A Greater Power, -1 Might cost and +8 Init, matching ReHe 5 (+1 complexity, +1 Touch, base 3).

creatures.equipment: Short bow of ivory, full heavy leather armor.
creatures.appearance: One of three severe young women with their hair pulled tightly back, in leather armor with ivory bows, plainly displeased; the three are hard to tell apart.
