creatures.name: Demon of Nicaea
creatures.how_many: seven, prowling the highways round Nicaea

powers.name: Coagulation
powers.description: Takes a solid body (Realms of Power: The Infernal).

powers.name: Endurance of the Enraged
powers.description: The Furies' power to fight on in a rage (Realms of Power: The Infernal).

powers.name: Obsession
powers.description: Costs 1 to 3 points: imposes the Obsession Trait Wrath.

creatures.appearance: A big, wild-coated, savage dog with drool on its snarling jaws, always slinking low as if on the hunt, ears flat and growling; its glowing red eyes terrify its prey.
creatures.notes: Long ago the people of Nicaea begged Saint Andrew to rid them of seven demons killing travellers outside the city; he drove them off, and they came to him as slavering dogs. Days later they killed a young man in his bed in another town, and the apostle prayed him back to life. The seven still haunt the roads but may not enter Nicaea. They strike at dusk or just after, mostly at lone travellers (a solitary Redcap is just their prey), about once a month; most townsfolk blame bandits or skirmishers. They can speak but seldom do, fight as a trained pack, and will run from a stronger group or a formidable foe. Wound ranges: the usual ones for Size 0, Light 1-5 to Dead from 21.
creatures.source: The Sundered Eagle: The Theban Tribunal p. 105

creatures.name: Anima, the Glass Submarine

powers.name: Supple as a Fish
powers.description: An instilled effect that lets the iron body swim as easily as a fish: ReTe 34 (+2 Sun, +2 metal, +3 Size, base 3, +1 complexity, +1 for two uses a day, +3 for a sunrise and sunset trigger).

powers.name: Transparent Skin
powers.description: Makes its hide almost clear, so it is hard to see and its riders can look out (MuTe 24: base 1, +2 metal, +3 Size, +2 Sun, +1 for two uses a day, +3 for a sunrise and sunset trigger).

powers.name: Habitable Bowels
powers.description: Keeps a light breeze moving inside it, so the riders can breathe in some comfort: CrAu 19 (+3 Structure, +1 Touch, base 1, +2 Sun, +1 for two uses a day, +3 for a sunrise and sunset trigger).

creatures.appearance: An enormous dolphin wrought of iron.
creatures.notes:
Legend calls Alexander's undersea vessel a glass bell hung from a ship; in truth it is an awakened simulacrum, a thinking mechanica of iron shaped like a dolphin as big as an elephant, made long before Alexander found it. It thinks and feels like a dolphin, and its powers were instilled in it, so they cost no Might. Up to five people of Size 0 ride inside (a tight fit) through a sealed hatch where a blowhole would be. Alexandria keeps it chained, on six hundred feet of iron chain, to one of its merchant ships at Smyrna, under guard and sailed as often as the others; the chain comes off when it carries riders. Like the flying device, it may be lent to a magus whose tokens outnumber his shards, for a deposit and a pawn of vis a week.
Being iron, it has no Wound Penalties but 15 Damage Levels (City & Guild): when damage beats its Soak it rolls Stamina plus a stress die against the excess, losing a level on a failure and one more per botch, with no penalty until the last goes and it bursts apart. Only someone with Mechanica or Automata can repair it, that score in levels a season; Catella has neither, but a few Verditius in the Tribunal know Automata. Nine of its twelve vis slots are used, so a mechanician could add more; studying it gives each investigator three Insights toward integrating its craft.
creatures.source: The Sundered Eagle: The Theban Tribunal p. 115

creatures.name: A Sibyl
creatures.how_many: a character guide for any of the ten sibyls, half of them in the Tribunal
creatures.appearance: A woman of the land she lives in, a girl or a withered old woman, her face behind a thin veil or a blindfold.
creatures.notes:
The book prints Magic Might 25+; most sibyls have more, which leaves room for openly magical powers beside their Divination (The Mysteries Revised Edition), Premonitions and learning. Divination is 10+2 with Puissant Divination. The Area and Organization Lores are the storyguide's to choose. Her Virtues and Flaws come to only 5 points, so there is room to tailor her; some sibyls are Transformed Humans instead. Enigmatic is an Essential Trait: magic to make her speak plainly simply fails. Wound ranges: the usual ones for Size 0, Light 1-5 to Dead from 21.
The sibyls are ageless magic humans with true sight, each bound to a strong Magic aura or regio she cannot leave without losing her gift to Acclimation, and seldom without guardians. Those in the Tribunal: Demophile the Erythraean at Erythrae, across from Chios, who speaks in acrostics; Herophile the Delphic, who is not the Pythia and answers only those of royal blood, however thin; Phyto the Samian in her cave, who wants questions in rhyme but answers plainly; Amalthea the Hellespontine at Dardania on Mount Ida, who will not prophesy of Troy; and Lamia the Phrygian, who must be overpowered before she speaks and is terribly strong. Their daughters, the sibyllides, are magic kin with powers of sight who come home every ten years to report on the world.
creatures.source: The Sundered Eagle: The Theban Tribunal p. 121

creatures.name: A Stoicheion
creatures.how_many: a character guide: every village and landmark has one

powers.name: Extended Glamour
powers.description: Always on: it knows all that happens within the domain it has chosen, being one with that place; Might 10 covers a room, more Might a wider land. The domain yields Might/10 pawns of Animal vis a year as objects, which may be taken without harm if bargained for.

powers.name: Guardian of the Bounds
powers.description: Costs 1 to 5 points, 1 per 5 levels of the matching spell: walking the village's bounds and drawing a circle, it raises a ward like Ward against Faeries of the Water, of the Realm and Form it picks each time (Faeries of the Wood against crop blight, Demons of the Mind against the evil eye). Wards are kept low to penetrate; at Might 20 a level 10 ward costs 2 points and has Penetration 15.

powers.name: Loosely Material
powers.description: Over a round it puts on glamoured flesh: Size +2 with the physical scores in the notes, the only form in which it can attack, kept as long as it likes. Slain, the body leaves the vis. Going back to spirit takes an unbroken round and returns the Might spent; a new body starts unwounded.

powers.name: Strike Dumb
powers.description: Gives the victim the Mute Flaw. Made permanent, it costs Might score as well as Might Pool; temporary, the points come back only when it is lifted. Improved Powers has been applied.

creatures.appearance: Mostly unseen; to Second Sight, an outsized beast of the kind it has taken.
creatures.notes:
Might 20 in its own village, where its warding is stronger. In material form: Str +2, Sta +3, Dex +3, Qik +2. Pick the one attack that suits its beast. Its Focus Power is Guardian of the Bounds, its Ritual Power Strike Dumb, its Lesser Power Loosely Material and its Personal Power Extended Glamour. Wound ranges: Size +2, steps of 7, Light 1-7 to Dead from 29. With 15 points of Virtues and 7 of Flaws it is too strong for a player unless taken at a magus's level, but it makes a good covenant ally or guardian bought as a Boon; it may take up to 3 more points of Flaws for 2 Virtue points each. Its usual Traditional Ward is that it dies if it leaves the land or people it guards; slain, it comes back in time, a little changed.
Stoicheia are spirits of places. In the wilds every odd boulder, lone tree, river and mountain has one, a genius loci; near people, faeries take the part, guarding the community for offerings of eggs, figs, milk and honey, and may desert or turn on a village that slights them. Kinds: the koukouvaounes, huge white owls with red eyes that fight evil faeries and demons, drink the milk left out for them, and may turn strong villagers into rams, oxen, horses or bulls to help; church stoicheia as a white calf, a red horse or a black cock; the basiliskos, a snake-shaped house spirit tied to a family, often with a Focus Power for housework; the pergalio, a black child with blue eyes bound to one building and given to jealousy; and the kalotyches of trees, which turn to murderous vengeance when their tree is felled, unless a stone is set in the cut.
creatures.source: The Sundered Eagle: The Theban Tribunal p. 129

creatures.name: Vrykolakas
creatures.how_many: a kind, feared all over Greece
creatures.weakness: Protected Group (those born on a Saturday)

powers.name: Form of Wickedness
powers.description: Shows its true, dreadful shape to spread panic (Realms of Power: The Infernal).

powers.name: Form of Man
powers.description: Wears the dead man's likeness (Realms of Power: The Infernal).

powers.name: Contagious Obsession
powers.description: One point for each victim (Realms of Power: The Infernal).

powers.name: Obsession
powers.description: Costs 1 to 3 points: imposes the Obsession Trait Fear.

powers.name: Burning Spittle
powers.description: Spits liquid fire up to five paces for +10 damage; anything that parries it is eaten through and ruined. A natural attack, which Magic Resistance does not stop.

creatures.appearance: Looks like anyone else until it shows its powers and its true shape: a hunchback with black hands and long nails, a peeling blood-red face, the teeth of a cat or wolf, and wild hair and beard, its skin glossy black or glowing in the dark. In Thrace it is worse still: goat-skinned, with an elephant's trunk and one enormous eye. As a shapeshifter it is mostly a cat, a goat or an owl.
creatures.notes:
The Greek vampire, also called timpanios, alitos or katakhanas in some regions. Greeks dig up their dead after three years to box the bones; if the flesh has not rotted, a demon has eaten the corpse and taken its shape, and it bursts out in its Form of Wickedness. Those likeliest to rise are people who died alone, had a cat leap over the body, ate mutton from a wolf's kill, or were cursed as they died (some wicked folk curse themselves). It settles in a village where no one knows it, preys first on the dead man's kin, then further afield, on beasts and people by night, and the district sickens. It likes to take a lone victim, grapple and bite, and may keep someone alive for nightly feeding with scuffle damage. Its Spittle has Defense not applicable. Wound ranges: the usual ones for Size 0, Light 1-5 to Dead from 21.
Holy symbols drive it off, but its true foes are the alaphroiskiotoi, the Saturday-born: it cannot hurt them, and those of them with Second Sight always know it in human or spirit shape.
creatures.source: The Sundered Eagle: The Theban Tribunal p. 141

creatures.name: Smerdaki
creatures.how_many: many, each haunting its own pasture or ruin

powers.name: Coagulation
powers.description: Takes a solid body, but only from its illusory or physical form.

powers.name: Obsession
powers.description: Costs 1 to 3 points: imposes the Obsession Trait Terror.

powers.name: Illusionary Form
powers.description: Makes a moving image of its body that it steers; it must be in this form or a real body to use Coagulation.

powers.name: Shout of Pan
powers.description: Up to ten animals bolt in terror, and the fear runs through the rest of a herd; enough goats or sheep make a deadly stampede.

creatures.appearance: A man shaggy with hair from head to foot, a ram with black marks on its brow, or a red-skinned child with a cat's eyes.
creatures.notes: Smerdos is the Greek word for anything foul or unclean, from spoiled wine and rotten meat to the unbaptised, children of mixed birth and bastards; the polluted may gain the evil eye or become masters of maleficia, but the belief that they become smerdaki is only peasant talk. The demons haunt pens, hedges, ruined houses and the places where flocks rest, scattering the beasts, causing miscarriages and maiming prized studs. Shepherds say nothing can harm them; that is because they so seldom leave their illusory form for a real body. Since each keeps to its haunt, shepherds move pasture and silence their bells so the demon doesn't notice. Wound ranges: Size -2, steps of 3, Light 1-3 to Dead from 13.
creatures.source: The Sundered Eagle: The Theban Tribunal p. 142

creatures.name: The Gorgona
creatures.appearance: A mermaid rising from the waves, at times in a chariot drawn by dolphins, with a lyre.
creatures.notes: Powers (no stat block): she ranges over the whole northern Aegean, most often near Thessaloniki's harbour and at midnight in rough seas. Meeting a ship, she asks a sailor whether Alexander lives. Told he is dead, she sighs, plunges beneath the hull, swells to a monstrous size and lifts a wave with her hand to overturn the ship; told he lives and reigns, she lets it go and calms the sea with her lyre.
creatures.source: The Sundered Eagle: The Theban Tribunal p. 54

creatures.name: Talos, the Protector of Candia
creatures.appearance: A giant bronze man with a bull's head (he is not the Minotaur).
creatures.notes:
Powers (no stat block): Hephaistos made him for King Minos. Each day he runs three times round Crete, hundreds of miles, throwing great rocks at hostile ships; enemies who land he grips in a deadly embrace after heating himself red-hot. One vein of green ichor runs from his neck to his ankle, stopped by a bronze nail: Medea pulled it and he bled out, until a local alchemist brewed him fresh blood.
Bound for centuries in a cellar of the ruined Labyrinth at Knossos in Byzantine times, he is free again now the old spell has failed, and he is a plague to Venetian ships; Candia's new rulers offer a fine reward for taking or killing the "demon". His true nature would fascinate House Verditius, and he could serve as the patron of a covenant on Candia.
creatures.source: The Sundered Eagle: The Theban Tribunal p. 81

creatures.name: Klymene
creatures.appearance: A titan-goddess, the titan of fame.
creatures.notes: Powers (no stat block): a Kosmokrator Spirit (Realms of Power: Magic). Neutral in the war of the titans, she was bound not in Tartaros but under the great altar at Pergamos, which is the lock of her prison; she thought the cell a kindness, shared with her sisters. A flaw in the binding lets a Hermetic magus standing on the altar cast a ritual without vis, drawing on her power; such spells risk odd side effects, and a botch is tainted as if with faerie vis.
creatures.source: The Sundered Eagle: The Theban Tribunal p. 106
creatures.secrets: The Theban magi do not know she is there. The bonds have a strength of 50, renewed each new year; every ritual cast from the altar wears them down by the pawns it would normally need. If they reach 0 within one year the altar splits and Klymene is free, and unhappy about it, with nowhere to go: she may go back to the Magic Realm, settle on a mountaintop and upset all around her, or roam the Tribunal freeing other bound titanesses. Lucian's Children of Olympus are drawn to the altar.

creatures.name: Belisarius of the Serpent Column
creatures.appearance: The great general as an urban faerie plays him, at the head of his imperial guardsmen.
creatures.notes: Powers (no stat block): an incognizant faerie who lives in a regio (Faerie aura 4) above the Serpent Column in the Hippodrome, a vision of the arena in its old glory as big as the real one, entered by walking round the column against the sun with a Roman-style sword in hand. He gives the column its Faerie aura and leads a troupe of city faeries who re-enact, over and over, the end of the Nika Riots, with Belisarius and his guard crushing the rioters: a lesson, to him, that change is bad and lawful rule and old ways are best. He needs mortals for his play, so he sends his followers into the city to lure watchers in.
creatures.source: The Sundered Eagle: The Theban Tribunal p. 95

creatures.name: Akgah, the Demon of the Fourth Crusade
creatures.appearance: A two-headed winged leopard the size of an elephant, a mockery of the winged lion of Venice, with sweet-scented fur mottled gold and black and great golden wings.
creatures.notes:
Powers (no stat block): a prince of Hell, foe and counterpart of the Hagka, the Divine two-headed eagle. Those in its company are seized by greed, lust and battle frenzy. In spring 1204 it fought the Hagka in the Hippodrome, wrecking part of the arena, and won; the eagle fled wounded, and crusaders who saw it took it for a holy vision of Venice's lion. The fall of the empire was its design, and won it great standing among Hell's princes; now it works to keep the successor states at war, distrustful and greedy.
Its lair is an Infernal regio about a dozen miles from Constantinople, like a blasted battlefield, where it lolls eating from reeking heaps of corpses among treasure and plundered relics, with hundreds of bodies on pikes around it.
creatures.source: The Sundered Eagle: The Theban Tribunal p. 139

creatures.name: The Druj of Xerxes's Hill
creatures.notes: Powers (no stat block): Obsession (Realms of Power: The Infernal), with the Obsession Trait Doubt. Artabanos, Xerxes's sorcerer in the Persian Wars, made her raise the man-made hill near Abydos in one day, then bound her under it to sharpen the king's sight, but her malice seeped out and filled Xerxes with doubt and gloom. The marble throne is gone. Anyone on the hill (Infernal aura 3) sees the whole Hellespont as if with Keen Vision, and is open to her Obsession.
creatures.source: The Sundered Eagle: The Theban Tribunal p. 106

source: The Sundered Eagle: The Theban Tribunal, by Atlas Games, content under the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 licence; summarised, not quoted.

lysandros.name: Lysandros
lysandros.summary: An unGifted Redcap and perhaps the finest authority on the Code of Hermes in the Tribunal. He always serves an arche of the Judicial Board, and every arche comes to him over hard points of law; but he is rude and pedantic beyond bearing, and answers precisely the question put to him, adding nothing the asker did not think to ask for.

diantha.name: Diantha
diantha.summary: An unGifted Redcap, beautiful and charming, who makes friends of men and women alike, so that the logothete has to field several requests for her each term. She is most use to archai whose work brings them among mundanes, for she can bring almost anyone round to her view of a matter.

niko.name: Niko
niko.summary: A young, keen Redcap, son of a magus and raised inside the Order, for whom the red cap seemed the natural calling. He has never yet assisted an arche and longs for his first posting.

aristides.name: Aristides
aristides.summary: One of the Redcaps in the logothete's own service, nearly sixty but still vigorous, and widely thought to carry the blood of Odysseus. He has certainly travelled everywhere: his little fishing skiff, which he sails alone, is hardly ever still, and he seldom sleeps two nights running ashore.

xenias_the_leper.name: Xenias the Leper
xenias_the_leper.summary:
Epidauros's leader in name, simply as its eldest, looking a hundred and seven: a magus aegrotus, a leper magus, like all his kind among the Tytalus deeply gifted for healing and longevity, and probably the Tribunal's greatest expert in both. He seems a scruffy old man in a ragged leper's robe, a linen veil over his face and gloves to the elbow hiding how old and shrivelled he is, and a bell on his robes clanks constantly to warn of his disease.

Though heavily marked by Twilight he is easy enough to approach, if anyone does: the prejudice against lepers is not only a mundane one, and no magic cures leprosy.

galla.name: Galla
galla.summary: An herbalist of the Pharmacopoiean tradition, looking fifty-two: a Root-Cutter, she can lower the vis cost of healing rituals, a great help to her covenant. Lame and silver-haired in a plain grey shawl, she walks awkwardly with her talisman staff, and her snake familiar noses out herbs in the hills. She is usually the one who deals with visitors.

destasia.name: Destasia
destasia.summary: A Witch of Thessaly descended from Cyra, looking thirty-seven, who has lately inherited the rule of Erebos young. She knows the magic of defixiones, curse tablets, and specialises accordingly in Perdo and Corpus. Elegant, athletic and black-haired, she would be handsome but for the ritual scars across her face, thought to come from a Mystery ordeal.

megethia.name: Megethia
megethia.summary: Destasia's mater, a Witch of Thessaly and the former leader of Erebos, still at the covenant but more and more absent in long episodes of Twilight. The book gives only her name.

boustaphan.name: Boustaphan
boustaphan.summary:
Leader of Gigas and senior Tremere of the Tribunal, one of the few of his House to hold his own sigil, looking a robust sixty-four. As his House's Tribune in Thebes he uses the proxy votes the young Tremere give him to reform the Tribunal as Coeris directs; he keeps carefully above the quarrels his covenant and House pick with Theban custom, though he almost surely backs most of them.

He dresses as a minor noble and is often out hunting with a hawk on his wrist; the locals take him for an exile from fallen Constantinople. His silver wolf Čovek is the covenant's patron in name. He seeks immortality through his line and has trained apprentice after apprentice since he could Open the Arts, gladly taking at the Apprentice Presentation the children no one else wants, and giving them a place in the service of his House.

links.note: Found him and brought him to Gigas to train

monorchis.name: Monorchis
monorchis.summary:
Looks forty-two. His parents had him made a eunuch to help him to a fine career in the palace bureaucracy; his Gift awoke quickly enough for him to stop the surgery before it was finished. Boustaphan, who kept spies in the imperial palace, found him and brought him to Gigas to train.

Perhaps because he so nearly became a man of ink and parchment, he is fiercely anti-intellectual: he will not read, studies the Arts mostly from vis, and holds that the Order has lost its intuitive bond with magic to the written word, dry logic and endless philosophy. He has made friends in House Criamon and, rumour says, in some esoteric Mystery Cults. His Form is Ignem, which he treats as a search for the light of the soul.

allectores.name: Allectores
allectores.summary: Gigas's chief negotiator and envoy, and the easiest of its magi to talk to, looking thirty-three. His role may seem at odds with a martial House, but the Tremere know diplomacy matters as much as readiness for war, and value him; he plays up his seeming misfit in the House's ranks to win sympathy from those he deals with. He is said to carry a faerie blessing that makes everyone he meets think well of him.

ausculator.name: Ausculator
ausculator.summary:
'The Listener', leader of Hedyosmos since his mater left the post fifty years ago, and head of the Terrae Cult in the Tribunal, looking eighty-eight; a remarkable Longevity Ritual keeps his body sound. Statuesque, snow-haired, he is wholly blind, his eyes white without iris or pupil, and often paints eyes on his lids as on a marble statue; his skin is cool and he wears a plain tunic with an embroidered hem. He moves as little as he can and can freeze so still that strangers take him for a statue, standing for hours or days; that he does so more and more makes some think Twilight is swallowing him. His familiar is an imago, a spirit of sound, bound through the Mystery of the Spirit Familiar.

He is reckoned the Tribunal's greatest master of Terram, and his books are famous far afield. His mater has vanished from the Tribunal; he says she will not come back, but not whether she died or passed into Final Twilight.

aiakia.name: Aiakia
aiakia.summary: The archon of the Tribunal, elected by the archai in 1214, looking fifty-three. Ausculator's youngest filia, she is being groomed to succeed him when Twilight finally takes him: not the cult's most powerful member, but the one who knows its rituals best. Her speciality is caves and underground ways; she has explored many cave systems in the Tribunal and beyond and brought back secrets she only half understands. She also has a remarkable mastery of earth elementals, and casts rituals such as Conjuring the Mystic Tower for others at the price of the vis and a shard's neutralisation.

tisiphon.name: Tisiphon
tisiphon.summary: A Quaesitor with a misguided sense of honour, looking fifty-one, and a member of the Titanoi, the Tytalan Mystery Cult; he is the most prominent of Kampe's Lovers. He takes up cases where a magus seems to have escaped the Order's justice, and tries to set them right by fierce speeches at Tribunal, by petition after petition to the Legislative Board, and, failing all else, by Wizard's War. His spirit familiar is an Aspect of the Erinyes, the threefold Daimons of vengeance. The Titanoi leave him little time for the Terrae Cult, of which he is a member in name only.

celaenea.name: Celaenea
celaenea.summary: A Seeker of the direct line of Lucian Triamonae, who founded the Seekers, which she thinks should win her the respect of her peers (it does not), looking forty-four. She is obsessed with the legends of Hermes, keeps a hidden laboratory on Mount Cyllene where the god was supposedly born, and believes that divining his nature will lay bare the roots of magic itself.

polydegmon.name: Polydegmon
polydegmon.summary: The best known of the Tribunal's 'Stygian' magi, who study binding magic, an art commonly thought suspect and perhaps Infernal because the Goetic Arts lead the field. He practises a non-Hermetic tradition of binding, unique in the Tribunal until he trains an apprentice. Chapter nine names him; the book gives no House or age (Tytalus, among the covenant's Tytalan theurgists, is assumed here).

anna_psellus.name: Anna Psellus
anna_psellus.summary:
Mother Anna, looking sixty-two, spiritual head of Koukoubiou, a small retreat of the kind Byzantine ladies found when they would rather not enter a great convent; she and her sister founded it straight after the sack of 1185 and laboured to rebuild the city and heal its wounds, the spiritual ones above all. Strong-willed and clear of purpose, having seen at first hand what sin and the Infernal do, she rules her nuns with an iron hand, thinks herself a soldier of the spirit, and has no patience with stupidity, cowardice or compromise.

When she must she can be civil, even play the meek servant, while skewering her betters with a dry wit inherited from her grandfather, a celebrated scholar and courtier. She serves the city and God only, and some say in that order.

theocharista_psellus.name: Theocharista Psellus
theocharista_psellus.summary: Anna's younger sister, looking sixty-three, who has always lived in her shadow: as kind and self-effacing as Anna is bold, but strong in her own quiet way. A brilliant scholar of Neo-Platonic philosophy with a deep grasp of theology, above all the Cappadocian Fathers on the Holy Trinity, she holds the covenant together with her patient, loving calm.

nereida.name: Nereida
nereida.summary: Nonna's twin, a Seirene, looking twenty-two. Her music works on courage, but a Restriction stops her ever using it on a man she is drawn to, a real trouble for one so romantic. She waits on the queen's household at court. She has kept a Longevity Ritual since just after her Gauntlet to keep her looks, a vanity the other magae think sinful.

nonna.name: Nonna
nonna.summary: Nereida's twin and her opposite in all but looks, which are nearly identical but for their apparent ages (Nonna looks her age), to much confusion at court. Men do not interest her at all. A close friend of Queen Margaret of Hungary, now living in Athens, she is fond of King Demetrios but would rather have seen Margaret rule. She has just come back from years at Empress Yolanda's court in Constantinople, and her drive to empower women and barely hidden scorn for men's failings may set her against her sister and the others; she would fight any man's admission to the covenant.

pythia.name: Pythia
pythia.summary:
The oracle of Delphi: a lone Criamon maga living in the Temple of Apollon, which is her laboratory, under the ancient oracle's ceremonial name. Each Pythia chooses her successor, often her filia, who takes the name after initiation into the oracle's Mysteries without telling anyone, so Pythia is treated as one enduring person. Magi consult her before founding a covenant, adopting a patron or a great Tribunal decision; she breathes the omphalos's vapours to prophesy and gathers Delphi's Intellego and Creo vis for the Tribunal after taking her own share. She sees supplicants only between spring and autumn.

The book gives no age; her present self is not described.
pythia.secrets: In the Absent Oracle a girl claiming to be her apprentice meets visitors with the news that Pythia is gone.

lucian_the_scholar.name: Lucian the Scholar
lucian_the_scholar.summary:
Aegaea's unchallenged leader and the last filius of its founder Orithyia, looking sixty-five: a famous scholar of Byzantine and ancient Greek letters who can recite dozens of long poems by heart and studies the power of story and rhetoric. He is believed to know several Mysteries, among them the Folk Mystery of Story Magic. White-haired and kindly of face, he wears loud dark blue robes embroidered with scenes of Greek and Byzantine legend. Unlike most of his covenant he travels widely and cares little for the sea.

He is an active politician with obscure, eccentric aims, liable to switch his support at once to any magus he sees acting heroically or in keeping with old stories and traditions, though Aegaea's name for treachery blunts his influence. He leads the Children of Olympos, who want the old Greek gods as the covenants' patrons, and coined the names of the three titan factions (the Seekers of the Fallen, the Legion of Atlas and Kampe's Lovers) in a mocking speech four Tribunals ago. He claims to have met the infant Zeus on Ida, and enjoyed young Proximios's acrobatics when the Redcap brought messages.

His Twilight Scars are hidden: some mental flaws, above all lapses in which he forgets who he is and claims to be someone else, usually a hero of Greek legend.
lucian_the_scholar.secrets: He devised two Mysteries, Elysian Ecstasy and Olympian Pact, through which a person is possessed by a Greek god, and he alone holds an Olympian Pact. His changeable politics are a plan: he has cast the Tribunal's magi and covenants in roles in a grand re-enactment of the myths and steers them toward their parts, hoping Faerie will one day replace the Magic auras of the covenants. He may be duped by pretenders, faerie or infernal, and Proximios hopes to slip an infernalist into his league so that it raises a False God.

leukothea.name: Leukothea
leukothea.summary: Charming and lovely, looking twenty-five and younger every year: born with the blood of the sea nereids, she has tail fins for feet and purple eyes, and her Twilight Scars are making her less human and more nereid. The latest has given her a crab's pincers at her temples, mostly hidden in her blue-green hair. Lucian hails this as a sign that she will become the faerie Amphitrite, Poseidon's bride, and urges her toward the Inner Mystery of Becoming; she is of two minds about it, but has begun wearing queenly white robes trimmed with gold. She often rides her dolphin familiar, Hippothoon, named for a mortal son of Poseidon.

delfini.name: Delfini
delfini.summary: A plain, earnest woman who looks forty-three, whose heartbeast, as her name says, is a dolphin: she joined Aegaea for the water, not for any love of Faerie. Friendly and curious, she likes to swim beside ships carrying Redcaps to trade gossip (sailors think a dolphin alongside lucky). Most magi like her for her open ways, but some think her a busybody and distrust her.
delfini.secrets: Proximios has marked her as one of the innocents the League of the Vigilant is to be steered into accusing of diabolism.

krum_the_swift.name: Krum the Swift
krum_the_swift.summary: A tall, athletic Bulgarian who looks forty, with a stallion heartbeast. As a young magus of Moero's Garden in Constantinople he loved racing in the Hippodrome. After the sack and that covenant's flight to Nicaea he met Lucian at the Tribunal of 1207, who filled his head with tales of Poseidon, maker of the horse and inventor of riding and racing, and Krum joined Aegaea on the spot, a sharp change of scene. He now means to grow his heartbeast into one of the golden-maned sea-horses that drew Poseidon's chariot.

memnos.name: Memnos
memnos.summary:
Founder of Favonius and designer of its wonderful ships, looking fifty-eight: a hale man, black-bearded and curly-haired, his skin browned by life on the shore and his body hugely muscled from heaving beams, a fine climber with sure balance. A lifelong lover of ships, he specialises in enchanting them and is famous as a builder of sea-going vessels, nearly always busy with a commission. He is best in Rego and in craft magic, which eases his labour; four forge-companions work with him, and his laboratory on Andros is richly specialised.

He belongs to the Mystic Fraternity of Samos (The Mysteries Revised Edition), or whatever cult teaches Hermetic Architecture in your saga.
memnos.secrets: An initiation gone wrong left him with a Death Prophecy, that he will die with the sky above and the sea below; so he has never sailed on any of his own ships.

verecunda.name: Verecunda
verecunda.summary: Memnos's filia and the covenant's real leader, looking thirty-eight: a lithe woman who dresses as a sailor, far handier than robes on deck, and holds the title of Gubernatrix, chief helmsman of the fleet, captain of the Philomela. Her enchanting is in ropes, knots, cords and twine, very useful aboard but no way to win steady customers for items. Her familiar is a monkey she found on one of the fleet's longer voyages, often seen keeping watch from the Philomela's rigging. She and Basil of Andros argue endlessly over profit against adventure.

aeliophanes.name: Aeliophanes
aeliophanes.summary:
Captain of the Tereus, where his sanctum is, though he spends most of his time in a one-man sailing boat he paid Memnos to build. A monster hunter who chases creatures for their vis: the Tribunal knows that if a covenant has a monster too much for it, Aeliophanes will kill it, if he can be found. He is after glory, not helping, yet he is likeable, and the grogs love his dash and his Gentle Gift.

He looks nineteen, a dark-haired young hero with a neat beard, and is Unaging. His talisman is his spear, enchanted to strike home despite the Might of his quarry. Peter Monocheiros owes him his life and is utterly loyal.

stouritus.name: Stouritus
stouritus.summary:
Primus of House Verditius, looking ninety-three, and a rare thing in his House: a humble man. Long expecting to be primus, he shunned most of the Inner Mysteries that feed pride and studied instead the House's history, members and rulings. To him Verditius is the one House to outlast time, since a magus dies but an enchanted item may last for ever. He has made Ingasia a model Verditius covenant.

He would like to forbid vendettas among its members but has no power to, so he leads by example and refuses what he sees as a violent, divisive custom of his House; Hydatius follows him. He has taken part in the Tribunal's government for some seventy years and is known as honest and fair. His long cause has been how many items a Verditius may sell to mundanes: the Order only demands intermediaries, and many Tribunals follow Rome's one a year, but he has raised Thebes's limit to five and persuaded it that Items of Quality are not enchanted items and do not count. He is determined that the Contest of 1234 will be held at Ingasia.

theorus_the_old.name: Theorus the Old
theorus_the_old.summary: The second eldest of Ingasia, after Stouritus, and its keeper of the Forge of Hephaistos at the foot of Mount Olympos (see Greece), a Verditius cult site with a Faerie aura of 4 and legendary items of the god's making, where he lives alone. The book says nothing more of him.

hydatius.name: Hydatius
hydatius.summary: A magus of Ingasia who follows Stouritus's example and will not join in vendettas. With Proximios of Alexandria he has just founded the League of the Vigilant to hunt out infernal corruption in the Order, he as its general and the Redcap as its purse and supplier. They want members from outside the Tribunal, fresh blood to root out the bad, mean to keep the others' names secret while they themselves seek help openly, and watch their fellows patiently for a slip. Their fine reputations make the league respectable, and its critics hold their tongues.
hydatius.secrets: Proximios, an infernalist, founded the league through him and talked him into leading it, meaning to turn it on innocents (Caterina, the young magi of Erebos, Delfini). He will urge Hydatius to send members after the suspects, and a demon in Hydatius's shape will order them to attack.

eudoxia.name: Eudoxia
eudoxia.summary: A maker of enchanted mosaics who looks forty-two, one of the Confraternity of Irene (see Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults). Spiteful and proud, she has lately been initiated into the Inner Mystery of automata, and works to unlock the secrets of two statues from the Hippodrome's rows that she has got hold of. (The book once spells her Euxodia.)

gemma.name: Gemma
gemma.summary:
Conjoined twins, joined at the spine so that they always face away from each other, who look thirty-five. Stouritus trained them, and they make most of Ingasia's enchanted items, forever at work. They long ago learned to live with their bodies: their laboratories are joined and mirror each other, forge for forge and bench for bench, so each can work her own enchantment at the same station as her sister. Each has her own vendator and team of forge-companions and runs her own Hermetic business. They take a season off only to study vis.

Her twin is Bobila.
gemma.secrets: Unknown to Stouritus, they sell more items than the law allows, and favour Nicaea, Venice's sworn enemy; they enrich the covenant slowly so as not to be noticed, and their long-term plans are unknown.

bobila.name: Bobila
bobila.summary:
Conjoined twins, joined at the spine so that they always face away from each other, who look thirty-five. Stouritus trained them, and they make most of Ingasia's enchanted items, forever at work. They long ago learned to live with their bodies: their laboratories are joined and mirror each other, forge for forge and bench for bench, so each can work her own enchantment at the same station as her sister. Each has her own vendator and team of forge-companions and runs her own Hermetic business. They take a season off only to study vis.

Her twin is Gemma. (The book also spells her Boblia.)
bobila.secrets: Unknown to Stouritus, they sell more items than the law allows, and favour Nicaea, Venice's sworn enemy; they enrich the covenant slowly so as not to be noticed, and their long-term plans are unknown.

maria_laskarina.name: Maria Laskarina
maria_laskarina.summary: The Tribunal's polemarch, elected in 1207 and again in 1214: a sturdy grey-haired woman who looks fifty-eight and dresses as an ancient Greek soldier. Filia of Laskaris, the founder, and named for him, she is a seasoned hoplite known for ruthless efficiency, a master of Rego and Terram whose trademark is a crushing hail of stones. Her familiar Hadrianus, a fierce wild goat of the island and sure-footed on its rocks, patrols it hard and butts any suspicious newcomer down the cliffs into the sea.

gerasimos_the_simple.name: Gerasimos the Simple
gerasimos_the_simple.summary: Drakos blood makes him huge, strong and brave, and he is held to be Varazes's own grandson, heir to his mythic strength, and to the drakoi's dreadful stupidity: hardly a grog on Polyaigos is duller, and he reduced his long-suffering master to tears. He has had to give up most book learning, and subtle Arts like Mentem and Vim are nearly beyond him, but the raw force of his simple earth and fire magic makes up for it. Honestly pious, like many of his House, he looks forty-four and has fought in more than one Wizard's March.

ioannes.name: Ioannes
ioannes.summary: A lanky, fair-haired eunuch in plain white robes, looking forty-one. Bought as a castrated slave, he was educated for the imperial court like many eunuchs until a Jerbiton maga of Moero's Garden found him; she wanted him for her apprentice, but a Bonisagus of Trianoma's line saw his fine mind and claimed him at Tribunal. He has served twice on the Council of Magistrates, a brilliant administrator there and at home, and in his second term was chosen archon, a rare honour for so young a magus.

caterina_da_vigonovo.name: Caterina da Vigonovo
caterina_da_vigonovo.summary:
A Venetian maga trained in the Roman Tribunal, newly come to Thebes, the reverse of many of her House, who have gone the other way; she looks her age. Her apparent ties to Venice, chief author of the crusade that took Constantinople, make the Theban Jerbiton deeply distrust her. Polyaigos has put her in charge of running and growing its mines and trade, for which she has a true Venetian gift.

Like many Jerbiton she long refused a Longevity Ritual, but failing vigour has made her accept she needs one; she hopes the Tribunal will sponsor it, and is working to build a good name and earn tokens. As a metoikos she can hold none until her citizenship is decreed.
caterina_da_vigonovo.secrets: She has met the Duke of Naxos in the guise of a rich noblewoman and is preparing a discreet arrangement with him. Proximios has marked her as an innocent for the League of the Vigilant to accuse of diabolism.

satabus.name: Satabus
satabus.summary: A young Verditius, trained at Ingasia, who has just moved to Polyaigos. The book gives no age or traits.
satabus.secrets: He was born Pietro, younger brother of Marco Sanudo, Duke of Naxos, and nephew of Doge Enrico Dandolo: a pleasant, clever, bookish boy with something deeply strange about him, who made his brother uneasy. Among his last acts Dandolo found him a place, which was apprenticeship at Ingasia. At Polyaigos he has learnt of Marco's rise; he keeps a warm love for his family but has not yet got in touch, while Marco often wonders what became of him and hopes for news.

zacharias.name: Zacharias
zacharias.summary: A magus of the Cult of Orpheus (Houses of Hermes: Societates) who keeps Orpheus's sacred grove of Orphykia on Lesbos alone, belonging to no covenant. The book gives no more.

marcus_tauros.name: Marcus Tauros
marcus_tauros.summary: A Criamon described in Magi of Hermes who seems to have had visions of a past life as a priest of Minoan Candia, and may be found at the ruins of Knossos digging in the catacombs for the lore of a magical bull cult of the Minoans.
marcus_tauros.secrets: He has not yet found the regio in which the labyrinth survives whole.

petros.name: Petros
petros.summary:
The leader of Michael's Tabula, a man of thirty-six in the body of a boy of eleven. His apprenticeship went wrong twice: his pater Michael botched his own Longevity Ritual, which took hold of the apprentice instead and stopped him growing; then Michael died defending the city just before Petros was to swear the Oath. Young and untried as he was, the covenant chose him as its leader out of respect for his pater.

He is a sad man caught in a child's body. His prayers to grow up go unanswered, and he carries the shame of the city's fall and of Thermakopolis's end. At his lowest he has thought of entering a monastery, but he stays to honour Michael's cause.

wilrich.name: Wilrich
wilrich.summary:
A Saxon from the Holy Roman Empire who looks forty-three, one of the handful of 'Frankish' magi in the Tribunal, and one who fits the type: big, burly, fair and bearded, rough in his manners, and speaking Greek with a heavy accent. Under the bluster lies deep faith.

He went on the Fourth Crusade as a knight in the following of the bishop of Halberstadt, having sworn, to quiet the Quaesitores, to use no magic while it lasted. Along the way he came to doubt the crusade's righteousness, and when the city fell he left the assault to defend the innocent and fight demons, ending up beside the dying magi of Thermakopolis and saving Petros. A formidable swordsman, he is the covenant's most martial magus and the keenest in its military plans. As a magus trained outside the Tribunal he is a metoikos.

links.note: Saved him in the fall of the city

artoud.name: Artoud
artoud.summary:
Brother Artoud, leader of Xylinites, looking about seventy-one. Most of his life passed in central Anatolia's hills, in the Levant Tribunal, in a Criamon Clutch destroyed in the wars between the Sultanate of Rum and the empire. He is fanatically loyal to his House and cares little for the wider Order, which he thinks run by ignorant, boorish Frankish barbarians. His Gift is blatant. As a magus trained outside the Tribunal he is a metoikos.

He has turned down Repose to stay and serve his House, and gives sporadic, half-hearted support to the League Against Idolatry.
artoud.secrets: His body is in better shape now than at twenty-one: he does not age, shrugs off injuries quickly and moves with more than human grace, the fruit of long mastery of the flesh on the Path of the Body (Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults). He hides it, passing off the pale scars on his tanned skin as the marks of mortification, feigning a stoop and a slight limp among mundanes, and moving as little as he can.

theoderet.name: Theoderet
theoderet.summary: A Criamon of the Clutch who looks forty-three, trained by Artoud. He is the orphanage's official castrator and, known for his medical skill, has often been called on to carry out blindings at the palace and across the city. With his deft Corpus magic and his mastery of Perdo Corpus he does it by magic, painlessly and safely, and he holds his work to be philosophically right: it serves Harmony where the likely alternative, execution or murder, would only add to Strife.

trasaricus.name: Trasaricus
trasaricus.summary: The only member of Xylinites born in the Tribunal, Artoud's apprentice and a nephew of the deposed emperor Alexios IV Angelos, who was killed in 1204. Gelded as a small child because he was politically dangerous, he hates the Doukas family without mercy. His imperial blood fascinates Artoud, who will not expel him, though he sees that the young man must soon be sent far from Constantinople before he brings disaster.

passara.name: Passara
passara.summary:
Passara filia Bacauda filius Aella, a maga of Verditius with the Gentle Gift and of no covenant, who keeps the automata of the Palace of Magnaura safe from time and wear as her lineage's founder Aella did. She lives in apartments in the palace that the emperor's autocrat gave her, and, proud of her lineage and its mysteries, will live nowhere else. The book gives no age.

Formosos of Guernicus believes she works for the Latin emperor and does more than tend the automata, and means to prove it.
passara.secrets: The book leaves whether she truly serves the emperor to the storyguide.

formosos.name: Formosos
formosos.summary: The grand-filius of Vaanes of Guernicus, who defended his wife Aella of Verditius against charges of being the emperor's court wizard. Formosos thinks Vaanes's part in that was criminal, and his pride will not let the matter rest: he is set on proving that Passara, Aella's heir in the Magnaura, is working for the Latin emperor and not merely keeping the automata, and will try to recruit player magi to look into her and her mundane dealings in secret. The book gives no age and names no covenant for him.

links.note: Means to prove she serves the emperor

leontius.name: Leontius
leontius.summary:
The logothete, the Tribunal's Chief Redcap since Petronas stepped down in 1207: a tall, thin, unGifted man with a receding hairline and a long grey moustache, who looks eighty-two. An old Supernatural Virtue gives him the full benefit of a Longevity Ritual as a magus would have it, but Warping has lately given him his first Major Flaw: to his shame, the Curse of Lycaon. He turns into a wolf not at the full moon but when he grows too anxious.

He regrets ever taking the post. For all his efforts, records have gone astray, lists have vanished, and the register of tokens and shards, the most important book of all, has been found wrong; he scraped past ostracism in 1214, knows the Tribunal is unhappy, and means to resign at the next meeting.

proximios.name: Proximios
proximios.summary:
An unGifted Redcap who looks forty-two: broad in the shoulder, handsome, his dark hair neatly combed. He is of the blood of Andreas, a mythic hero of Justinian's Persian Wars, a gymnast rather than a soldier, who beat two armoured Persian champions hand to hand; from him Proximios has astonishing gifts, near-legendary feats of tumbling among them. As a young messenger he dazzled the magi he carried letters to with his acrobatics, and Lucian of Aegaea loved the show.

He is known as a quick, capable politician, though he has never held office and has always been somebody's assistant; so deep in Tribunal business is he that for twenty years he has been let off ordinary Redcap duty and carries no messages. It was his idea, in 1186, to make the logothete's post permanent instead of seven years, for continuity and so no newcomer need learn the records afresh, and it pleased those who complain the Tribunal's officers change too often. Many Redcaps want him as the next logothete and will propose it in 1221; he neither seeks nor refuses it, and most think that is humility.

With Hydatius of Ingasia he founded the League of the Vigilant, paying for it and supplying its magic while Hydatius leads it. He backs Ziper's wish to take the craftsmen Nanno and Ampelius into Moero's Garden, pointing to how well his own House of unGifted folk serves the Order.
proximios.secrets:
Proximios is an infernalist, unknown to anyone: a master of the Unholy Method of Incantation and the Unholy Power of Diablerie, with a long list of demons' True Names. He uses summoned demons as spies and lures, and sets Tempters and Evil Spirits to drive his fellows to sin. He means to bring down the Order, starting in Thebes, and works slowly and covertly among magi who would spot anything blatant, seeking a weak link in every covenant; his post at Alexandria shows him the letters and missives passing through. Neither Method nor Power is on his generated sheet: the storyguide adds them.

He set up the League of the Vigilant to aim it, in time, at innocent magi who look like diabolists (Caterina da Vigonovo, young magi of Erebos, nosy Delfini of Aegaea), sending league members to look into them, never going himself, and then having a demon dressed as Hydatius order an attack. He would turn Aiakia, or more easily the hotter Tisiphon, against Gigas by blaming its Tremere for Constantinople's fall, and set Celaenea, who adores Hermes, against Lucian's Children of Olympos; other infernalists have told him an infernalist planted in that league could make it raise a False God in place of a faerie.

In 1220 these plans are only forming. He will take the logothete's post, seeming reluctant so the blame falls elsewhere when things unravel, and use the register of tokens and shards to reward those who cooperate. He has not yet recruited magi, but has his eye on a few who might be tempted. His plots always look like someone else's work; the book suggests him as a saga's chief enemy, his threat growing slowly over the years (see An Enemy Within).

links.note: Co-founder of the League of the Vigilant, which Hydatius leads
Backs Ziper's proposal to take Nanno and Ampelius into Moero's Garden
Delighted Lucian with acrobatics as a young messenger

catella.name: Catella
catella.summary:
The only Gifted member of Alexandria, who looks thirty-nine. She came straight from her Gauntlet, two years before Constantinople fell, while the covenant's name was still good, drawn by Alexander's artifacts; in some twenty years of study she has got little further with them.

Because of that interest she was made keeper of the artifacts and their loans, which both thrills and galls her: she loves having charge of them but hates that they are often out when she wants to study them. Alexandria has chosen to lend them freely, and she abides by it even when it upsets her own plans. She has no Mechanica yet, so cannot mend the glass submarine. She would also dearly like Hagia Sophia in Constantinople studied for insights from Heron's theories, and will fund any magus with a way to do it.

ionnia.name: Ionnia
ionnia.summary:
The founder: a tall maga with thin white hair and dull blue eyes, who looks ninety-one and wears rich robes, gold necklaces, jewelled rings and bracelets crusted with gems. Before Moero's Garden she won a great name in House Jerbiton by collecting every poem of Kassia, the ninth-century nun who is the empire's most famous woman poet. A master of Rego and Mentem, she summons and questions ghosts in her hunt for old poetry.

Longevity Rituals have never worked well for her, and she is very frail and near her end, which does not trouble her: though she grieves for the old site, she is content with idle pleasures, letters to her two living daughters and early evening company. She has served the Tribunal before but says she is too old for politics now; still, she means to go to Delos for the next meeting to offer vis to the covenant's patron. She soothes Hipparchus's ghost with evenings of star-gazing.

syagricus.name: Syagricus
syagricus.summary:
The oddest Jerbiton of the covenant in body and temper, who looks forty-three: a true hermaphrodite, medically proven, proud of it, who dresses to show both natures, with a full beard and a gown that shows off his bust. He calls his nature beautiful and will not hide it; his sodales accept it but wish he spoke of it less. He takes his Longevity Ritual gladly, a daily draught of herbs and powders at noon, and is hale.

He shares his sodales' love of art, manners and comfort, but cares more for winning back the covenant's lost art than for pleasure: he belongs to Valnastium's league of New Iconophiles and goes to Constantinople at least once a year to hunt for the missing pieces. He sides with Ionnia against the League of Constantine, and is the only one besides Ziper not appalled at taking in Nanno and Ampelius. His apprentice Pancratius is due his Gauntlet at the Tribunal of 1221 and will probably join; Trasaric and Helladius hope he will vote with them.

ziper.name: Ziper
ziper.summary:
The eldest of Moero's Garden, who joined only after it moved to Nicaea, a Tytalus with the Gentle Gift. Stooped, wrinkled and wholly bald, in white robes under a red toga, he looks sixty-five and venerable, but has the energy and sharpness of a young man.

He thinks the covenant too small to carry weight in the Tribunal and has proposed taking the craftsmen Nanno and Ampelius in as members of House Jerbiton: they are not magi, but can put minor enchantments in their work. Proximios of Alexandria backs him. Everyone else but Syagricus is appalled, less because the pair are unGifted than because they are craftsmen. The book once calls Ziper a maga but elsewhere 'he'; the pack follows the latter.

trasaric.name: Trasaric
trasaric.summary: One of the two youngest magi of Moero's Garden and of the League of Constantine, who holds that Constantinople fell because the covenant's magi idled instead of defending their homeland, and wants it to help the Nicene emperor take the city back. He hopes Pancratius, once Gauntleted, will tip the vote his way. The book gives only his name and this stand.

helladius.name: Helladius
helladius.summary: With Trasaric the youngest of Moero's Garden and a member of the League of Constantine: he too blames the city's fall on the covenant's idleness and wants to back the emperor of Nicaea against the Latins, and courts Pancratius's future vote. The book gives only his name and this stand.

kristophoros.name: Kristophoros
kristophoros.summary:
A Bonisagus preacher who holds the First Commandment above everything. To him the pagan survivals all through the Tribunal's customs are a creeping evil, and he means to scrub every trace of idolatry out of Hermetic practice in Thebes. Oddly he has no quarrel with the titans, who ask no worship, only with the faerie gods who hunger for it. The book names no covenant for him.

That makes him the rallying point of the Legion of Atlas, whose aims match his though their reasons do not; his eloquence has more than once saved magi who harmed faeries from conviction, so player magi may find him an ally at Tribunal, wanted or not.

evantia.name: Evantia
evantia.summary: Of Moero's Garden, and the most respected of the Seekers of the Fallen, who look for the titans' return and study Magic auras, regiones and the ways into the Magic Realm. The book gives her only that line and no House; she is entered as Jerbiton, since seven of her covenant's eight magi are.
